The Chinese government is determined to lead the transformation toward a world of AI-powered robots. Beijing has placed embodied AI among what it calls the “industries of the future,” alongside 6G and quantum technology, and named it a priority in the 15th Five-Year Plan—the country’s socioeconomic blueprint through 2030. Facing high youth unemployment, a property market still in crisis, sluggish domestic consumption, and an aging and shrinking population, Beijing sees embodied AI as a new growth engine that could offset these headwinds while also pushing technological frontiers.

Innovations aimed at addressing domestic challenges could quickly create a geoeconomic advantage. China already controls key chokepoints in the emerging supply chain for embodied AI. Chinese companies, for example, produce about 80 percent of the world’s LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) sensors—the technology that underpins three-dimensional mapping and autonomous navigation in self-driving vehicles, warehouse robots, and precision agricultural tools. If AI-powered robots become as foundational to the global economy as Beijing hopes, countries would be as dependent on Chinese robotics supply chains as they are today for critical minerals, which has given Beijing enormous leverage over the global economy.

The strategic benefits of AI-powered robots extend to the military. In February, the Chinese Institute of Command and Control, a state-connected national scientific society, assessed that embodied AI could enable networks of unmanned systems operating across air, land, sea, and space to share information, anticipate battlefield developments, and carry out precision strikes in real time. This could significantly enhance the ability of the People’s Liberation Army to coordinate joint operations across varied terrain, such as around the disputed islands and outcroppings in the South China Sea.

Most important, a growing number of prominent scientists in China have argued that embodied AI could offer a potentially neglected pathway to building artificial general intelligence. Zhang Bo, the founding dean of Tsinghua University’s Institute for Artificial Intelligence and a pioneering AI researcher, has written that intelligence relies not only on cognition but also on the ability to learn from and make decisions in the physical world. Embodied AI, he argues, can overcome the shortcomings of traditional AI and accelerate progress toward AGI. Zhou Bowen, the director and chief scientist at Shanghai AI Lab, one of the country’s leading AI research institutes, has similarly argued that AI models need robotics to understand the physical world. China’s unmatched manufacturing base can become a training ground for artificial intelligence as real-world data feed back into AI systems. Horus (/hɔːrəs/),[c] also known as Heru, Har, Her, or Hor (/hɔːr/)[d][6] in Ancient Egyptian, is one of the most significant ancient Egyptian deities. He is known as the Ancient Egyptian god of kingship, healing, protection, the sun, and the sky. He was worshipped from at least the late prehistoric Egypt until the Ptolemaic Kingdom and Roman Egypt. Different descriptions of Horus are recorded in history, and these are treated as distinct gods by Egyptologists.[7] These various forms may be different manifestations of the same multi-layered deity in which certain attributes or syncretic relationships are emphasized, not necessarily in opposition but complementary to one another, consistent with how the Ancient Egyptians viewed the multiple facets of reality.[8] He was most often depicted as a falcon, most likely a lanner falcon or peregrine falcon, or as a man with a falcon head.[9][10]

The earliest recorded form of Horus is the tutelary deity of Nekhen in Upper Egypt, who is the first known national god, specifically related to the ruling pharaoh who in time came to be regarded as a manifestation of Horus in life and Osiris in death.[7] The most commonly encountered family relationship describes Horus as the son of Isis and Osiris, and he plays a key role in the Osiris myth as Osiris's heir and the rival to Set, the murderer and brother of Osiris. In another tradition, Hathor is regarded as his mother and sometimes as his wife.[7]

The conquest of Egypt by Alexander the Great opened a new era for the cult. In trying to find a religious cult that would unite both Egyptian and Hellenic subjects, Ptolemy Soter crafted the Isis cult as it would be introduced into Greco-Roman society.

Osiris was renamed Serapis and identified with a variety of Egyptian and Hellenic gods (Osiris, Apis, Dionysus, Hades). He became a god of healing and the underworld.

Isis was identified with Hellenic deities such as Demeter or Aphrodite.

Greek iconography was introduced to the cult which made it visually appealing to the Hellenes. In those days when the provincial city-states of the Hellenic world fell to Alexander's universal empire, the traditional gods of the city-state no longer sufficed. Gods like Isis and Serapis were not connected with any specific town and were truly universal in scope.

More importantly, the exotic Egyptian mysticism could offer the Greeks of the Hellenistic age something their own gods could not: a way to cheat fate and death.

Isis and Osiris were honored by the Greeks and by Egyptian emigrants as a kind of holy trinity, but always it was Isis who was the dominant member of the trio.

Isis became the protector of family (especially women), the protector of newborns, the goddess of fertility and good fortune, and the goddess whose magic could cheat fate and death.

She was also thought to be a protector of sailors, and sailors sailing from the great port of Alexandria took her cult all over the Mediterranean.

Backed by the Ptolemaic regime, the new cult spread throughout the Hellenistic Kingdoms.

The Nile Flows into the Tiber
The Roman Senate was not amused with Ptolemy's attempt to craft a universal religion.

When the cult of Isis swept into Rome via Hellenistic sailors and Egyptian emigrants, it became extremely popular with women and the lower classes, including slaves.

Fearing a religious unification of the lower strata of Roman society, and fearing the loss of piety in the traditional Roman gods of the state, the Senate repeatedly placed restrictions on the new cult.

Private chapels dedicated to Isis were ordered destroyed. When a Roman Consul found that the demolition team assigned to him were all members or sympathizers of the cult and refused to destroy their chapel, he had to remove his toga of state and do the deed himself.

How Did Different Roman Emperors View the Cult of Isis?
Augustus found the cult "pornographic," though the cult was known to proscribe periods of sexual abstinence to its adherents.

The real reason for Augustus' wrath was that the cult was linked to Egypt and thus the power base of his rival, Mark Antony. Cleopatra had even gone so far to declare herself Isis reincarnated.

Nonetheless, Augustus' scorn did little to stem popular opinion. Officials and servants of the imperial household were members of the cult. It seems even his own infamous daughter was a member; whether her belief was genuine or merely another aspect of her defiance against her father cannot be determined.

Tiberius, upon hearing of a sexual scandal involving the cult, had the offenders crucified and images of Isis cast into the Tiber. But much like Christianity in ancient Rome, periodic and sporadic persecutions did nothing to stem the tide. What was death when one's deity promised salvation and resurrection?

As part of his undoing of the policies of Tiberius, Caligula legitimized the religion. Temples to Isis were permitted to be constructed. Aspects of the Isiac festivals became public and part of the civil calendar (though there were still mysteries celebrated in private).

It is also known that Caligula had an Egyptian chamberlain who exerted influence on the emperor and helped him progress in the mysteries of the goddess. Perhaps this even helped play a role in Caligula's infamous promotion of himself as an autocratic, Hellenistic-like ruler. Whatever the truth, Isis was now part of Roman paganism for good.

The emperor Vespasian became acquainted with the cult while serving in the Eastern legions, and seems to have adopted Isis and Serapis as his personal savior deities. Domitian owed his life to fleeing opponents in the garb of Isiac cultists, and continued the family's association with the cult.

Hadrian and Marcus Aurelius were friendly to the cult, but most likely not initiates. Commodus, on the other hand, shaved his head bald like the priests of Serapis. He used to beat those around him with a mask of Anubis, which was common in the processions of the cult.

Septimus Severus was fascinated with the cult, and his son Caracalla dedicated a giant temple to Serapis that rivaled the one built to Jupiter, Rome's original patron god. The meaning was clear - the gods of the East that had once been maligned by the ruling classes of the Republic were now on equal footing with the traditional gods of the State. Among the common people, they were more important.

Stoic and Neoplatonic intellectuals tried to reinterpret the cult in terms of their own highbrow philosophies, with the deities of the cult serving as metaphors for great cosmic principles. While this may have held some influence in the literate classes, its doubtful it had any impact on the vast majority of followers.

To the average person Isis was not a metaphor or concept; she was as real to her followers as the Virgin Mary, Mother of God, is to billions of Christians around the world today. More to the point, she performed much the same function.

The Un-Roman Roman Cult
The Cult of Isis was, thanks to Ptolemy, Hellenized to a degree that the Roman mind could understand it, and yet still foreign enough to be exotic and alien.

Unlike most religious structures in the Roman world, the Iseum did not open to the streets or the Forum where public spectators could view the proceedings inside. The Iseum was walled off from the surrounding world, suggesting a space of inner sanctity.

Even within its walls, there was a "sanctuary", much like modern monasteries, where only clergy and the initiated could enter. In there, rituals involving fire, water and incense were conducted in front of a sacred statuary of the deities concerned.

This secret religious life that was set apart from the community and the State is what helped arouse the suspicions of the conservatives back in the days of the Republic.

Not much is known about the details of the inner workings of the mysteries, as they were by definition secret. Prospective initiates were called to the goddess by dreams and visions. Intense preparations of purification and meditation (and abstinence) were followed by exotic rites designed to recreate the myth of Isis and the resurrection of Osiris.

By enduring these rituals, the adherent was reconciled to the magic of Isis and effectively granted a favorable afterlife. He or she was in a sense spiritually reborn, in a manner common to Greco-Oriental savior religions.

But there were more public festivals, too, that didn't require initiation.

The first was conducted on March 5th. In honor of Isis sailing the seas to find pieces of her lost husband, a colorful procession of costumed people, including especially sailors, marched to port and ritually blessed a boat.

The second festival was held October 28th to November 3rd. This was an ancient passion play. Again, costumed enactors took to the streets, this time to reenact the death and resurrection of Serapis. Roman conservatives complained the festival was too loud and too colorful.

People also had private shrines to Isis and Serapis in their homes.

The subject of the ethics of the cult is a complicated one. We know that Egyptian culture as a whole was free with sexuality compared to Roman culture. Isis was, in fact, rather popular with courtesans and other such professions, and there are speculations that Isiac cults may have promoted a kind of "positive sexuality" among a more conservative Roman population. Augustus and Tiberius took this as proof of a "pornographic" cult.

Yet the Isiac cult also demanded regular periods of sexual abstinence from its adherents for purposes of ritual purification, and even apparently courtesans readily submitted to these observances.

Curiously enough, the early Christians who were quick to complain about the degeneracy of pagan cults could not offer as much criticism about Isis as they could about some other cults in the Empire.

In Kabbalah, concentric circles known as iggulim represent the ten sefirot (divine emanations) as a nested, cosmic order radiating out from a central infinite point (Ein Sof). This circular model emphasizes universal harmony and unchanging cosmic structure, contrasting with the linear, anthropomorphic yosher (Tree of Life) model.
Core Concepts of Iggulim (Circles)
Structure: Ten concentric spheres or rings where the outermost layer represents the highest emanation (Keter, the Crown) and the innermost layer represents the lowest emanation (Malkhut, the Kingdom/Physical realm).
Cosmology: Reflects ancient and medieval views of heavenly spheres, symbolizing how divine light successively contracts and envelopes creation from the outside in.
Independence: Each circle functions with a degree of autonomous, sequential flow rather than the dynamic, interactive inter-weavings shown in the vertical pillar arrangements of the traditional Tree of Life.
The Two Complementary Models
Iggulim (Circles): Represents transcendent, uniform divine light and cosmic macrocosm without personal differentiation.
Yosher (The Straight Line/Tree): Represents immanent divine flow, active relational attributes, and the blueprint of human consciousness (Adam Kadmon).

An Asherah pole is a sacred tree or pole that stood near Canaanite religious locations to honor the goddess Asherah.[1] The relation of the literary references to an asherah and archaeological finds of Judaean pillar-figurines has engendered a literature of debate.[2]

The asherim (the Hebrew plural form) were also cult objects related to the worship of Asherah, the consort of either Ba'al or, as inscriptions from Kuntillet ‘Ajrud and Khirbet el-Qom attest, Yahweh,[3] and thus objects of contention among competing cults. Most English translations of the Hebrew Bible translate asherim (Biblical Hebrew: אֲשֵׁרִים, romanized: ăšērim or אֲשֵׁרוֹת ăšēroṯ) to "Asherah poles".[4]

References from the Hebrew Bible
Asherim are mentioned in the Hebrew Bible in the books of Exodus, Deuteronomy, Judges, the Books of Kings, the second Book of Chronicles, and the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Micah. The term often appears as merely אשרה, (Asherah) referred to as "groves" in the King James Version, which follows the Septuagint rendering Koine Greek: ἄλσος, romanized: álsos, pl. ἄλση alsē, and the Vulgate lucus,[5] and "poles" in the New Revised Standard Version; no word that may be translated as "poles" appears in the text.

The Jesuit Historical Institute, also known as IHSI (Latin: Institutum historicum Societatis Iesu), is an international group of Jesuit historians committed since the end of the 19th century to bring out scientifically critical editions of the foundational texts of the Society of Jesus (the MHSI), and to promote research on the history of the Jesuits. Originally based in Madrid, the institute is now quartered in Rome.[1]

History
In the 19th century, a group of Spanish Jesuits began the publication of letters of Saint Ignatius of Loyola. The century's atmosphere of religious controversies and polemical anti-clerical and anti-Jesuit pamphlets and diatribes required, for appropriate rejoinders, that access be given to the foundational documents of Jesuit life and history.[2] Historical science had also made great progress. New methods had been developed.

Encouraged by General Congregation XXIV (of 1892) the Superior General of the Jesuits Luis Martin established in 1893 a 'College of writers' in Madrid, with mission to establish critical editions of the foundational documents of the Society of Jesus, particularly those regarding the life and times of the founders, Saint Ignatius of Loyola and his first companions. The purpose was also to provide material for accurate regional and national histories of the Society to be prepared in various European countries. The historians entrusted with the task adopted the critical methods of contemporary historical research. In January 1894 the first volume of the Monumenta Historica Societatis Iesu came out of the press.

text:
A lot of sauce 
Question : What is Palantir
 Palantir Technologies Inc. is an American public software company that builds data integration and analytics platforms for government agencies, the military, and major corporations.
  Core Platforms
Palantir does not sell or broker personal data. Instead, it licenses software systems that help organizations combine, organize, and analyze their own complex datasets:
• Palantir Gotham: Used mainly by defense, intelligence, and law enforcement agencies to connect disparate data sources and track operations.
• Palantir Foundry: Used by commercial enterprises and non-profits to integrate data, run analytics, and manage business workflows.
• Palantir AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform): Connects large language models and generative AI systems directly to private enterprise and military networks.
• Palantir Apollo: Manages continuous software delivery and updates across diverse or remote hardware environments.
  Background and Origin
• Founded: 2003 by Peter Thiel, Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale, Alex Karp, and Nathan Gettings.
• Name Origin: Named after the mystical, all-seeing "palantíri" orbs from J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings.
• Headquarters: Miami, Florida (with major operations in Denver, Colorado and Silicon Valley).

Question : How does it align with Mark Walter
  Palantir aligns with Mark Walter—the billionaire financier, CEO of Guggenheim Partners, and owner of major sports franchises like the Los Angeles Dodgers—primarily through a high-profile joint venture targeting artificial intelligence in the financial services sector.
   The Enterprise AI Joint Venture
In March 2025, Palantir Technologies and Mark Walter's holding company, TWG Global, launched a dedicated joint venture to bring operational AI to banking, insurance, and asset management.
• The Strategy: The venture pairs Palantir’s technical AI capabilities—specifically Palantir Foundry and AIP—with the deep operational and industry knowledge of Walter's massive corporate portfolio.
• The Goal: Instead of forcing banks to buy separate, fragmented AI products from dozens of vendors, the venture offers an end-to-end framework to automate high-stakes workflows like credit underwriting, compliance (KYC/AML), and portfolio risk mitigation.
    The xAI Collaboration
The alignment deepened in May 2025 when Elon Musk's AI startup, xAI, officially partnered with the Palantir-TWG Global venture. This tripartite agreement integrated xAI's "Grok" large language models with Palantir’s core data governance software. The collaboration aims to deploy an "agentic workforce" of hundreds of thousands of digital AI agents directly into major financial institutions.
    Internal Proof of Concept
Before taking this offering public, Walter and Palantir CEO Alex Karp spent over a year embedding Palantir's AI infrastructure into Walter's own commercial companies (including major firms like Guggenheim Investments and Delaware Life) to prove its financial returns and scale capabilities.

Question : Why would Elon Musk make a deal with these snake oil salesmen
   Elon Musk’s decision to partner xAI with Palantir and TWG Global is driven by distribution, data infrastructure, and commercial necessity, rather than an endorsement of Palantir's public hype.
While critics and short-sellers have historically questioned Palantir’s proprietary software, the strategic mechanics behind why xAI entered this deal center on very specific business requirements:
    1. Breaking into Highly Regulated Industries
Large Language Models (LLMs) like xAI's Grok are useless to massive financial institutions if they cannot safely access sensitive, proprietary data.
• Banks cannot simply upload their private financial records or client data into a standard public cloud AI.
• Palantir’s Role: Palantir acts as the "middleware." It has spent over two decades building the strict data governance, compliance frameworks, and secure access permissions required by the U.S. military and intelligence agencies. By tying Grok to Palantir's backend, Musk gains a secure, pre-approved pipeline into Wall Street.
    2. Immediate Commercial Distribution
Building an AI model is entirely different from building an enterprise software sales force.
• To make a return on massive computing costs, xAI needs giant corporate clients that pay tens of millions of dollars annually.
• Mark Walter's Role: Through TWG Global and Guggenheim, Mark Walter controls or heavily influences massive segments of the banking, asset management, and insurance industries. This partnership gives xAI immediate, executive-level access to dozens of massive corporate portfolios that can deploy their systems in 90 days, bypassing years of standard enterprise sales cycles.
     3. Funding the "Compute" War
AI development is an incredibly expensive cash-burn game, requiring continuous capital to expand supercomputers.
• Instead of selling software on a per-employee "seat" license—which slow-moving corporations hate—this joint venture uses an outcome-based pricing model.
• This allows xAI to monetize its infrastructure directly through concrete operational efficiencies (like automated risk modeling or underwriting), bringing in rapid, high-margin revenue to help fund its broader infrastructure projects.
     4. Overlapping Ideologies
Beyond pure business, there is a distinct political and operational alignment. Palantir's co-founder Peter Thiel was a co-founder of PayPal alongside Musk, and Palantir's current executive leadership has been vocal supporters of Musk's efficiency and government tech initiatives. This shared Silicon Valley network makes a collaborative megadeal much easier to broker.

Question : So is Guggenheim the odd group out ? Just a vehicle to carry Xal in?
   Guggenheim and TWG Global are absolutely not the "odd group out" or a passive vehicle—in fact, they hold the keys to the entire operation.
If xAI is the "engine" and Palantir is the "transmission," Mark Walter’s ecosystem is the destination and the fuel. Within this partnership, Walter brings three massive operational assets that Musk and Palantir completely lack:
   1. The Ultimate Testing Ground (The Guinea Pig)
You cannot sell unproven financial AI to Wall Street; the regulatory risks are too high. Walter provides a massive, built-in laboratory. Through TWG Global, he controls or owns major stakes in Guggenheim Investments, Guggenheim Securities, Delaware Life, and Group 1001 Insurance. Palantir and xAI spent an entire year embedding their systems directly into Walter’s own companies first, proving the tech works and makes money before trying to sell it to external banks.
     2. C-Suite Sales Credibility
Elon Musk is a polarizing tech disruptor, and Palantir’s Alex Karp is an eccentric Silicon Valley philosopher. Neither has the traditional corporate trust required to walk into a legacy commercial bank and change how they handle risk or underwriting.
Mark Walter is a deeply entrenched, institutional titan. In this venture, TWG Global explicitly leads the executive-level implementation. Walter and his team act as the trusted advisors who sit down with other Fortune 500 CEOs to convince them to deploy these AI agents at the highest operational levels.
     3. Infinite Capital Networks
xAI needs billions of dollars to build supercomputers like its Colossus cluster. Walter is a master allocator of global capital. For instance, TWG Global acts as a bridge to massive pools of global money, including a multi-billion-dollar strategic partnership with Mubadala, Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund. Walter provides the financial plumbing to scale these projects globally.
        The Division of Labor
The deal operates as a mutually dependent tripod, not a vehicle for a single player:
• xAI (The Brain): Supplies the foundational frontier LLMs and raw reasoning computing power.
• Palantir (The Shield): Wraps that brain in absolute security, data compliance, and enterprise guardrails.
• Guggenheim/TWG (The Market): Deploys the tech into its own firms, brings the wall of corporate clients, and structurally finances the venture.

Question : What happens when TWG collapses due to Government investigation ?
   The premise of your question is highly relevant given that TWG Global is actively facing civil and criminal federal investigations by the DOJ and the SEC.
The probe centers on a whistleblower complaint alleging that Walter’s insurance companies (Delaware Life and Clear Spring Life) concealed risk by failing to disclose that over $20 billion in private credit loans were funneling back into other companies Walter controlled. While TWG Global maintains "there has been no fraud", the business is under immense strain—Walter has already unloaded his stake in the LA Lakers and Chelsea FC to shift capital, and regional banks are pausing distribution of TWG financial products.
If TWG Global were to completely collapse under the weight of this investigation, the ripple effects would reshape the xAI and Palantir partnership in very specific ways:
    1. The Tech Survives, but the "Guinea Pig" Dies
The core software agreement between Palantir and xAI would not disappear, but they would lose their immediate playground. The tri-party venture used Walter's massive corporate portfolio—like Guggenheim and Group 1001—to test Grok and Palantir Foundry internally. A collapse of TWG would tie those target companies up in bankruptcy courts, asset freezes, and regulatory receivership, effectively killing the enterprise "proof of concept" data loop.
     2. Palantir and xAI Absorb the Joint Venture
In the event of a TWG insolvency, the joint venture agreement likely contains standard "key man" or "bankruptcy default" clauses. Palantir Technologies and xAI would likely exercise clauses to buy out or seize TWG’s share of the technology venture. Because Palantir and xAI own the actual IP (the Grok model and the Foundry software), they would simply take full control of the financial AI platform and eliminate the middleman.
      3. Immediate Loss of C-Suite Distribution
The true damage to Musk and Palantir wouldn't be technological; it would be commercial. As established, Mark Walter was the trusted wall street operator who provided the executive-level relationships to sell this tech to other Fortune 500 banks. If Walter's empire goes down in a fraud or disclosure scandal, the joint venture becomes toxic by association. Legitimate banks would flee the partnership to avoid catching the attention of the SEC and DOJ.
       4. Direct Pivot to Defense and Sovereigns
If the commercial pipeline to Wall Street dries up due to a TWG collapse, Palantir and xAI would almost certainly pivot the joint venture's infrastructure entirely toward the public sector. Palantir already holds massive sway over Allied intelligence networks, and Elon Musk's xAI has massive computing power. They would re-tool the financial data models to focus on macroeconomic tracking, state-sponsored financial warfare, and sovereign wealth fund allocation (such as their existing connections to Abu Dhabi's Mubadala), bypassing traditional commercial banking entirely.
In short: TWG Global is the distribution vessel. If the vessel breaks, the cargo (Palantir’s security framework and xAI’s intelligence) will just be re-routed by Musk and Karp to a different port.

Question :If Xal is in there, wouldn't it be able to discover discrepancies ?
   Technically, yes, xAI’s Grok is capable of finding those discrepancies—but legally and operationally, it is strictly prohibited from doing so.
Independent testing has proven that Grok's recent models excel at accounting forensics. xAI even designed a custom version of Grok specifically for TWG Global that improved dense financial document extraction accuracy to 97.5%.
However, Grok will not uncover or expose the specific transactions under federal investigation due to three structural boundaries:
      1. Hardcoded Guardrails (The "Palantir Shield")
The joint venture relies on Palantir’s Governance Foundation. Palantir’s primary role in this partnership is to act as the security boundary. When an AI model is deployed inside a corporation, human administrators explicitly map out what data the AI can see, read, and manipulate. If TWG executives or general counsels do not explicitly feed the disputed related-party loan records into Grok's permission silo, the AI is completely blind to them.
       2. Disclosures vs. Sub-ledger Intent
The DOJ and SEC probe centers on a disclosure failure—specifically, whether Walter’s insurers properly informed regulators that $20 billion in private credit loans were being funneled back into other Walter-controlled entities.
• AI agents are highly effective at finding mechanical discrepancies (e.g., a mathematical error on a spreadsheet or a missing wire signature).
• They cannot naturally detect a strategic omission of legal ownership unless they are explicitly instructed to audit corporate org charts against thousands of private credit agreements.
     3. Conflict of Interest & Attorney Privilege
Corporate AI tools are deployed to optimize P&L and automate tasks like underwriting or KYC compliance. If a company detects an internal accounting anomaly via AI, that data is instantly routed to corporate attorneys under legal privilege—not broadcasted to the public or federal investigators. Furthermore, because TWG Global is the entity leading the executive implementation of this AI suite, their own data systems are under tight corporate lock and key.
In short, while Grok has the processing power to trace the money, it only looks where its handlers point it. It acts as an operational employee, not an independent, unprompted federal auditor.

Choosing the right AI model can save you hours of work.
Stop using one AI tool for everything. Different models are built for different tasks, and knowing which one to use can give you a serious productivity advantage. 🧵

ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Pi are useful for everyday questions, brainstorming, writing, and getting work done faster.

Building software, debugging code, or learning programming? ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot, and specialized coding models can help you move faster.
4. Creative Writing & Ideation
For content creation, storytelling, brainstorming, and developing fresh ideas, try ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Mistral.
5. Search, Research & Web Knowledge
Need to explore a topic or find information online? Perplexity, ChatGPT, and Grok can help you research and investigate ideas.
6. Long Documents & Data Analysis
When analyzing lengthy reports, summarizing documents, or working with large amounts of information, choose a model that supports your document size and analytical needs.
7. Multimodal Tasks
For working with images, audio, text, and other media, look for models with the specific multimodal capabilities your project requires.
8. Open-Source & Self-Hosted AI
Want more control over your AI setup? Explore DeepSeek, Mistral, and other open-weight models that may offer greater flexibility for local deployment.
9. Enterprise & Secure Workflows
For business use, prioritize access controls, privacy settings, compliance requirements, and the security features offered by the provider.
10. Education & Tutoring
Use ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, or Perplexity to understand difficult concepts, practice new skills, and build personalized learning plans.
Here's the real lesson:
The best AI model isn't necessarily the most popular or the most expensive one.
It's the one that solves your specific problem with the right balance of quality, speed, cost, and reliability.
Don't chase every new AI launch. Build a toolkit that works for you.

text:
Córdoba: A Centre of Learning in Andalucia
By Deborah Cater
November 14, 2024
In the heart of Andalucia, Córdoba is a captivating city celebrated not only for its architectural wonders but also as a historic epicentre of intellectual and cultural achievement.

A Golden Age of Learning
During the 10th and 11th centuries, Córdoba was one of the most sophisticated cities in the world. Under the rule of the Umayyad dynasty, it emerged as the most important intellectual hub in Europe. This period saw an unprecedented flourishing of knowledge as libraries and academies sprung up throughout the city. Scholars and students from the Islamic world, as well as Jewish and Christian intellectuals, gathered here to exchange ideas and foster learning, laying a foundation for the Renaissance that would later sweep across Europe.

The Great Library of Córdoba was reputed to hold hundreds of thousands of manuscripts, rivalling the collections of even the famed Library of Alexandria. Córdoba was a city of learning and enlightenment, a place where the flow of knowledge was cherished as deeply as the material wealth amassed by the caliphs.

Intellectual Exchange and Multiculturalism
Córdoba’s intellectual landscape was diverse, shaped by the convergence of different cultures and religious traditions. The city exemplified convivencia, a unique co-existence of Muslims, Christians, and Jews who shared not only a physical space but also a commitment to mutual respect and shared learning. This multicultural environment encouraged scholars from all backgrounds to interact and learn from one another, leading to groundbreaking advancements.

Jewish scholars such as Maimonides, one of the most influential Jewish philosophers of the Middle Ages, and Muslim scholars like Ibn Rushd (Averroes), an early proponent of Aristotelian philosophy, made invaluable contributions. Their works, often written in Arabic or Hebrew, would eventually be translated into Latin, bringing ancient and contemporary ideas into Europe.

Legacy of Scientific and Philosophical Innovation
Córdoba’s scientific and philosophical achievements were just as profound as its cultural impact. Fields like astronomy, mathematics, and medicine saw significant advancements due to the work of scholars such as Al-Zahrawi, whose surgical texts were used for centuries across Europe. Cordoban astronomers also made substantial strides, mapping constellations and refining mathematical tools, which would influence the field of navigation for generations.

The city was also a central node in the trade of ideas, where scientific and philosophical texts from ancient Greece, Persia, and India were translated into Arabic and then disseminated across the Mediterranean and beyond. This intellectual cross-pollination would later fuel European scholars’ curiosity, leading to an era of scientific inquiry and humanistic philosophy.

Córdoba’s Architectural Homage to Knowledge
Walking through Córdoba today, the physical spaces echo the city’s past as a centre of learning and enlightenment. The iconic Mezquita-Catedral, originally built as the Great Mosque of Córdoba, is testament to the architectural and intellectual prowess of its time. Its impressive arches, intricate carvings, and cavernous spaces were built to inspire awe and contemplation, a fitting homage to a society that valued learning and introspection.

The Judería, Córdoba’s historic Jewish quarter, remains a reminder of the intellectual contributions of the Jewish community, with narrow, winding streets that lead to the Synagogue of Córdoba, one of the few remaining in Spain. In these historic districts, visitors are invited to ponder the city’s legacy, sensing the echoes of ancient debates and groundbreaking ideas that shaped the course of European history.

Discover the Legacy of Córdoba’s Intellectual Golden Age
TOMA & COE offers unique insights into Córdoba’s historical richness, providing travellers with experiences that reveal the city’s pivotal role as a cradle of knowledge and culture. From guided tours of the Mezquita-Catedral to explorations of the Judería and beyond, TOMA & COE’s tours encourage guests to immerse themselves in the spirit of discovery that defined Córdoba’s Golden Age.

I spent some time looking into the FDE model for Palantir, OpenAI and Anthropic last week

When you dig into Palantir's Ontology/Foundry its obviously insanely complicated and hard to use and I've built agents for years. Thats why they sell you an FDE to come into your business, connect all of your data sources and systems, let you use any model and give you enterprise AI intelligence

It's AI hand holding and your friendly 60+ year old S&P 500 CEO wants their hand held into the AI realm

Palantir also launched a self serve AI FDE Chatbot style interface which is actually pretty easy to use just hard to find unless you search for it. 

I watched a lot of the demos (hertz, construction companies) and its clear businesses are unlocking a lot of value with Ontology. They just say the word ontology way too much it is annoying. 

Net, it feels like a CEO/company decides they want AI, they go to Palantir and they upgrade their business. They control their data and choose between models, which fits part of my Sovereign AI thesis, but their workflows and applications are built on Palantir so its very sticky for them. Your data, their platform kinda deal

Net, Palantir feels like an enterprise AI systems upgrade through connecting mass data and applications 

On the other hand, OpenAI/Anthropic are doing an emergent model

It’s emergent because employees can adopt the tools, build workflows and become the internal champions for company wide adoption. Getting the same company specific value from Palantir generally takes more upfront setup.

Instead, you have an AI champion or head of AI at a company and you give all your employees access to AI connected to their granola, and calendar and email and internal systems to boost their own individual productivity

Instead of upgrading all legacy systems with AI like Palantir, with OpenAI/Anthropic it feels more akin to giving each employee more reasoning and individual AI capabilities

For enterprise it feels like Palantir is upgrading Systems

For enterprise it feels like OpenAI/Anthropic are upgrading employees

I feel @NousResearch is also in a very strong position since theres millions of Hermes users and these folks act as as champions to upgrade their companies to Hermes enterprise AI. Hermes offers the self serve emergent model but you can expand it company wide with Hermes enterprise. 

Who wins on the Palantir vs OpenAI/Anthropic side? 

I think short term Palantir wins since they have an FDE army, enterprises want to cut AI costs and they want to upgrade their systems to use AI. Every board and shareholder will demand businesses do an AI upgrade cycle and CEOs want their hands held. I think enterprises want long term control and ownership of their AI stack. 

I will note note OpenAI/Anthropic already exclude business data from model training by default but this isn't broad ownership of your creations and there is platform lock in here. 

I feel enterprises owning their AI stack drives the creation of unique business outcomes and applications. Frontier for a business may be an open source model (or fine tuned version) + their data/memory/interactions/entire stack. @brian_armstrong demonstrated part of this today with Coinbase's fine tuned model release. 

Longer term it feels like OpenAI/Anthropic go overboard hiring FDEs (or acquiring all of the mini palantirs out there) and having the frontier model lead so net new technologies are created in a productive human + AI situation and OpenAI/Anthropic capture value as the infrastructure these creations depend on. 

I think OpenAI/Anthropic also eventually own a percentage of these new technologies and creations to rationalize the capex spend for these models and businesses are ok with it since its less upfront cost (but IP farming) and they share the equity upside. 

Net, I think Palantir is upgrading legacy systems with AI and OpenAI/Anthropic upgrading employees with AI

I really like PLTR thesis wise but I can't get comfortable with the valuation here since I can be right on the thesis and lose money if the (very high) multiple compresses. I'm interested in counterpoints here so DM or reply why I'm wrong here or your financial model

Anyway GN sleepy time tea is kicking in 🫖

Jumping on the new AI animation trend! 💅 

Created this in Seedance 2.5. The kitten knights are everything! 😻⚔️

 Dropping ALL exact prompts for FREE in the thread below. 👇

📌 PROMPT  (Animation prompt):

SCENE ARC: A mysterious royal command → a mixed kitten army intercepts a Coca-Cola truck → tiny soldiers overturn it → one bottle per wagon returns to the castle → the queen accepts the tribute.

SHOT STRUCTURE: Exactly 10 shots, 30 seconds, 16:9. Hard cuts at the specified times. Natural-speed action, precise physical camera movements and stable optics within each shot.

REFERENCES:
@Image1 — Queen: preserve her exact face, tall hourglass figure, hairstyle, complete lavender-and-burgundy costume, crown and jewelry.
@Image2 — Kittens: preserve the four designs, pink capes, silver armor and broad swords: pink bow, black bob, jeweled tiara, heart-painted helmet.
@Image3 — Truck and driver: preserve the complete vehicle and the seated man's appearance.
@Image4 — Wagon and bottle: preserve construction, solid wooden wheels, hinged T-handle, one 0.33-liter bottle and its four securing cables.
Use references for appearance; replace their grey backgrounds with the locations below.

GLOBAL STYLE NOTES:

• look:
Lavish late-1940s to early-1950s Hollywood Technicolor fantasy comedy, photographed as live action. Tangible embroidered costumes, weighted velvet, detailed fur, metal armor and wooden props.

Creamy ivory highlights, rose-peach skin, dusty lavender, blush pink, deep burgundy, rich cherry red, dark forest green and warm brown-plum shadows. Rich dye-like color separation, dense readable darks and softly compressed highlights. Clearly visible fine moving 35mm grain, restrained warm halation and vintage optical diffusion around bright edges. Eyes, fur, engraving and lettering stay readable.

Afternoon sunlight from the west models the exterior scenes. Cream stone provides reflected fill at the castle; tree-filtered sun creates distinct light patches on the mountain road. The throne room receives west-window sunlight and warm candlelight. Consistent vintage color timing throughout, natural shutter motion blur.

• locations:
BALCONY AND COURTYARD — A cream-limestone mountain castle above a forested valley. Carved arched doors, burgundy curtains, brass fittings, lavender mosaic borders, sculpted balustrades and feline heraldic reliefs. Copper planters overflow with pink roses; wisteria, ivy, embroidered pennants and scattered petals enrich the foreground.

Below: a cobbled court with arcaded galleries, a moss-edged fountain, carved columns, stone benches, iron lanterns, rose trellises and slate-roof towers. Mountains rise beyond the walls. Keep the central route to the gate clear.

MOUNTAIN FOREST ROAD — A winding ochre gravel road across a wooded mountainside. Tall pines and firs, exposed roots, mossy boulders, ferns, fallen branches and pink woodland flowers. Forested valleys and layered mountain ridges appear through gaps between trunks. Natural rock, earth and vegetation line the road; no fences, garden walls or orchard gates.

The interception happens at a broad bend: uphill rocky bank to the south, a wide fern-covered shoulder to the north before the valley drops away. The truck points west. Cameras stay south of the road; kittens push its south side, tipping it north onto this shoulder.

THRONE ROOM — Carved cream columns, ribbed vaults, floral tapestries, burgundy curtains with tassels, leaded windows, branching brass candleholders, porcelain flower vessels and an inlaid floor. A lavender-and-wine runner leads to a three-step dais and gilded burgundy throne beneath an embroidered canopy. Feline armrest carvings, a silver ewer, closed illuminated book and bowls of roses provide smaller details. A low embroidered footstool stands before the queen; bottle wagons occupy the side aisles.

• continuity:
Mix all four kitten types throughout every army view and procession, approximately equally represented. Vary their order within rows and across foreground, middle distance and background. Never group the army into separate accessory-based units. The four foreground leaders are one of each type.

Kittens stand approximately 35 cm tall; bottles remain ordinary 0.33-liter bottles, approximately 20 cm tall. During running, pushing and transport, swords are secured on their backs, leaving paws free.

The driver remains inside the cab throughout the truck sequence. The queen raises her sword only for the command, then immediately lowers it; at the throne it is sheathed.

• acting:
QUEEN — Treat the wish as royal business: locate the target, address the army, then later inspect the delivered bottle and acknowledge its bearer. Measured movement and engaged eyes.
KITTENS — Perform each duty with solemn concentration: watch the leader, contact points, path and load; the bearer waits for the queen's secure grip.
DRIVER — Brake, investigate the tiny obstruction through the window and brace at the wheel when the vehicle tilts. Remain seated.
Natural blinking and purposeful attention throughout.

• sound:
Period orchestral adventure score: strings, restrained brass and military snare, becoming ceremonial during the return. Duck music beneath dialogue. Distinct heels, cloth, armor, engine, gravel, suspension, impact and wooden-wheel sounds.

No synchronized meowing or feline chorus. Only one brief individual mew during the procession. The queen's written line is the only speech.

SEQUENCE LIST:

SHOT 1 — 0.0–4.0s — HOOK
• first_frame: Queen already stepping through the balcony doors, framed by burgundy curtains and foreground roses.
• camera: medium-full, slightly below chest height, 47° field of view. Physically dolly two meters backward and one meter sideways as she advances, creating clearly visible parallax between doorway, flowers and balustrade. Finish in a closer three-quarter view.
• action_visual: ONE CONTINUOUS UNCUT ACTION — 0–2s, she takes two purposeful steps, sword low in her right hand. 2–3.3s, she briefly raises it toward the distant road and delivers the command. 3.3–4s, she immediately lowers the sword completely beside her thigh. Her left hand rests on the railing; her cape settles behind her.
• acting: locate the distant target, then look down to address the soldiers.
• dialog: Queen, low clear voice, measured authority: “Bring it to me.”
• exit: sword fully lowered before the cut.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 2 — 4.0–6.0s — ARMY REVEAL
• camera: extreme wide over her shoulder, elevated rear three-quarter, 84° field of view; crane outward above the balustrade.
• action_visual: Reveal hundreds of pink-caped kitten knights filling the detailed courtyard. Bow, bob, tiara and heart-helmet designs are visibly intermingled throughout. The tiara leader gives a downward paw signal. Leading ranks turn toward the gate, followed by slightly staggered movement deeper in the crowd.
• acting: kittens follow the signal and locate their route.
• exit: the mixed army begins moving; fountain water, small footfalls and armor clicks.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 3 — 6.0–8.0s — TARGET REVEAL
• SHIFT: mountain forest road; dappled afternoon sun, engine rumble, gravel crunch and forest air.
• first_frame: Red truck rounds a wooded mountain bend, framed by rocks and tall trunks; forested ridges recede beyond it.
• camera: wide front-left three-quarter, low roadside height, 47° field of view; track alongside the truck.
• action_visual: Truck travels at approximately 15 km/h. Its Coca-Cola side lettering becomes readable. Suspension responds to shallow ruts; the reference driver steers from inside.
• acting: driver watches and follows the bend.
• reaction: the royal military objective is revealed as a delivery of cola.
• exit: truck approaches the wider interception bend.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 4 — 8.0–10.0s — INTERCEPTION
• camera: medium tracking view at kitten-eye height, side three-quarter, 84° field of view; travel alongside the charging leaders.
• action_visual: Small armored feet run between ferns, roots and mossy rocks. Pink capes trail behind. All four leader designs remain recognizable, with mixed ranks following. They emerge from the uphill forest onto the road; the truck begins braking in the background.
• acting: leaders judge the slowing vehicle and move toward its south-facing side.
• exit: kitten boots reach the gravel as the truck stops.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 5 — 10.0–13.0s — DRIVER REACTION
• camera: close-up through the open driver's window, eye level, side three-quarter, 29° field of view; short physical push-in.
• action_visual: Driver stays seated with both hands on the wheel. He leans toward the window to look down at the kittens, then checks the side mirror. Pink capes and silver helmets move below the window. The cab gives a slight lateral rock; he braces against the wheel. Door stays closed.
• acting: inspect the obstruction, then determine what is pushing the vehicle.
• exit: suspension creaks as he holds his position inside.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 6 — 13.0–17.0s — OVERTURN
• camera: wide rear three-quarter from the southeast, slightly elevated, 84° field of view. Brief lateral track establishes the pushing formation, then hold the full action clearly.
• action_visual: ONE CONTINUOUS UNCUT ACTION — mixed kitten rows plant paws against the low south-facing cargo sill; rear rows brace behind them. The tiara leader drops its paw. Everyone leans forward together.

The truck rocks, south-side wheels lift, and the chassis rotates around the north-side tires. It makes one quarter-turn away from the kittens and lands on its north side on the broad fern-covered shoulder. The driver stays braced inside the rotating cab.

Maintain visible paw contact during the push. The kittens step back once the truck passes its balance point. Ferns flatten, gravel scatters and low dust spreads from the landing.
• acting: pushers watch their contact points; the leader tracks the lifting wheels.
• reaction: tiny soldiers accomplish the enormous feat through collective fairy-tale strength.
• audio: suspension groan builds to one heavy metal-and-earth impact; music briefly drops around it.
• exit: truck rests on its side. Cut forward in time to the prepared delivery.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 7 — 17.0–21.0s — ONE BOTTLE PER WAGON
• first_frame: Bow kitten at foreground left walks toward screen-left, its wagon following at right. Paw grip, lifted handle, bottle and securing cables are visible together. Mixed kitten-and-wagon pairs recede behind.
• camera: medium-full profile at kitten-eye height, 47° field of view; track alongside at walking speed.
• action_visual: Each kitten walks upright ahead of its own wagon, back toward the bottle. Its right paw reaches slightly behind the right hip and grips the center of the T-handle. The hinged drawbar rises to the lowered paw, outside the legs; the left paw swings naturally. Cape and tail stay clear of the wheels.

Exactly one bottle stands in each wooden holder, secured by four taut cables from its neck collar to the wagon corners. Solid wooden wheels rotate against the uneven forest road. Carts respond to bumps while bottles remain secure. Alternate the four kitten designs throughout the line in varied order.
• acting: foreground kitten briefly checks its load, then returns attention to the path.
• audio: wheel rattle, tiny footsteps, cloth rustle and one soft individual mew from this kitten only.
• exit: procession follows the road toward the castle.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 8 — 21.0–23.0s — PROCESSION SCALE
• camera: extreme wide elevated rear three-quarter, 84° field of view; crane upward.
• action_visual: Reveal a long winding column of separate kitten-and-wagon pairs approaching the flower-covered castle gate. All four types remain mixed. Each wagon carries one bottle with visible space between carts. Foreground trees, embroidered pennants, carved towers and distant mountains create depth.
• acting: nearest pullers follow the curve through the gate.
• exit: leading carts enter; cut forward in time to the ceremony.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 9 — 23.0–27.5s — PRESENTATION
• SHIFT: furnished throne room, west-window sunlight and candlelit depth; soft hall reverberation.
• first_frame: Queen seated at frame-right; bow kitten on the low footstool before her knees at frame-left, holding one sealed bottle in both paws. Other three leaders wait below the dais. Mixed ranks and parked loaded wagons extend into the decorated hall.
• camera: medium two-shot, slightly below the queen's seated eye level, three-quarter 45°, 47° field of view; gentle dolly inward.
• action_visual: ONE CONTINUOUS UNCUT ACTION — kitten offers the bottle. Queen leans forward, grips it below the neck with her right hand and supports the base with her left. Kitten releases only after her grip is secure. She checks the label, looks back at the bearer and gives one slow approving nod.

The presented bottle's transport collar and cables were removed during the time ellipsis. Its empty wagon rests in the side aisle with released fittings; other bottles remain secured.
• acting: kitten waits for acknowledgment; queen directs approval toward its face.
• exit: nod completes and the kitten begins to bow.
HARD CUT.

SHOT 10 — 27.5–30.0s — ROYAL SALUTE
• camera: wide frontal view of the dais, slightly elevated, 84° field of view; slow dolly backward.
• action_visual: Bow kitten kneels on the footstool; the other three leaders kneel below. Mixed ranks follow with slight natural timing differences. Heads lower and one paw rests against each breastplate. The heart-painted helmet slips slightly forward during its wearer's bow.

Queen remains upright, holding the sealed bottle, with a faint closed-mouth smile. The widening composition reveals tapestries, candleholders, flowers, canopy, carved columns and rows of miniature bottle wagons.
• acting: kittens complete the salute; queen watches the leaders.
• exit: hold through 30 seconds as the orchestral cadence settles.

DIALOGUE CONSTRAINTS:
Only “Bring it to me.” spoken once in English. No extra dialogue, narration, subtitles or title cards. Preserve Coca-Cola lettering on the physical truck and bottles.

We have not seen anything comparable to the “AirLand Battle” doctrine or the “Deep Battle” theory — concepts that reshaped entire military systems.
The Ukraine war has offered a glimpse of the future of high-intensity land warfare.
Unmanned systems are not simply replacing soldiers.
They may redefine the rules of ground combat.
If the US Army had already completed this transformation, its options against opponents like Iran might look very different today.

The technique targets a fraction of soil phosphorus that is bound up in microbial DNA, a pool that conventional soil tests largely miss. Making that measurement cheaper and easier could give growers and researchers a clearer picture of how soil microbes help feed plants. The work points toward routine soil testing that accounts for biology, not just chemistry.

Italian rice farmer Alice Cerutti has restored roughly a third of her family's four-century-old rice fields in northwest Italy to natural marshland, Phys org reports. The farm, first carved out of marsh by monks 400 years ago, now runs as a biodiversity haven alongside its rice production. Cerutti's approach treats habitat restoration as a defense against heat stress rather than a retreat from farming. For rice growers facing hotter seasons, the case offers a working example of pairing cultivation with restored wetland.

Namibia - An Incredible Experience!

Namibia: Africa’s Masterpiece of Space, Silence, and Adventure

For travelers who believe they have already seen the world's great wonders, Namibia often becomes one of their most memorable destinations. For first-time visitors to Africa, it is equally captivating because it offers extraordinary landscapes, excellent tourism infrastructure, political stability, and some of the safest and easiest independent travel on the continent. Namibia combines dramatic scenery, abundant wildlife, rich cultural traditions, and genuine wilderness in a way few countries can match.

What makes Namibia truly special is that it feels vast, untouched, and deeply authentic. It is a country where you can watch the sunrise over some of the world's tallest sand dunes, encounter desert-adapted elephants in seemingly impossible environments, photograph lions drinking at a waterhole under the stars, and drive for hours without seeing another vehicle.

Why Namibia Stands Out

Many African destinations are defined primarily by wildlife. Namibia offers something different.

The country's greatest attraction may be its landscapes. Wildlife is important, but Namibia's deserts, coastlines, mountains, canyons, and open horizons often become the true stars of the journey. The country is home to the ancient Namib Desert, regarded as one of the oldest deserts on Earth, along with the Skeleton Coast, Etosha National Park, Damaraland, and the immense Fish River Canyon.

Unlike East Africa's lush savannahs or Central Africa's forests, Namibia's beauty is stark and minimalist. Travelers frequently describe it as one of the most photogenic countries on Earth.

Another distinguishing feature is the sense of freedom. Namibia is among Africa's premier self-drive destinations thanks to excellent roads, low population density, and well-developed tourism services.

Landscapes
The Namib Desert

The Namib stretches along much of the Atlantic coast and contains the spectacular red dunes of Sossusvlei and Deadvlei. Some dunes rise more than 1,000 feet (300 meters), glowing orange, red, and gold as the light changes throughout the day.

The contrast of giant dunes against bright white clay pans creates some of Africa's most iconic photographs.

Skeleton Coast

This remote coastline is famous for dense fog, shipwrecks, towering sand dunes, and an almost otherworldly atmosphere. The name comes from the many vessels that met their fate along this harsh Atlantic shore.

Damaraland

A region of volcanic mountains, dry river valleys, ancient rock art, and desert wildlife. It feels more like Arizona, Utah, and Africa combined into one extraordinary landscape.

Etosha National Park

Etosha centers around a vast salt pan visible from space and ranks among Africa's finest wildlife destinations. During the dry season, animals congregate around waterholes, creating remarkable viewing opportunities.

Fish River Canyon

Often considered the second-largest canyon in the world, it offers dramatic vistas and exceptional hiking opportunities.

Flora and Fauna

Because Namibia is predominantly arid, its plants and animals have evolved remarkable survival strategies.

Unique Flora
Welwitschia mirabilis, one of the world's strangest plants, can live well over 1,000 years.
Camelthorn trees create iconic desert silhouettes.
Quiver trees flourish in rocky desert regions.
Succulents and hardy desert grasses thrive in areas that receive very little rain.
Wildlife

Namibia hosts:

African elephants
Lions
Leopards
Cheetahs
Black and white rhinos
Giraffes
Zebras
Springbok
Oryx (gemsbok)
Hyenas
Meerkats
Hundreds of bird species

Perhaps most famously, Namibia has:

Desert-Adapted Elephants

These elephants roam seemingly barren desert valleys and have adapted their behavior to survive long periods without water.

Desert Lions

Found primarily in the northwest, these lions are among Africa's most fascinating predators.

Rhino Conservation Success

Namibia has become a global leader in community-based conservation, helping protect one of the world's largest free-ranging black rhinoceros populations.

The People and Culture

Although one of Africa's least densely populated countries, Namibia is culturally diverse.

Major groups include:

Ovambo
Herero
Himba
Damara
Nama
San (Bushmen)
The Himba

The Himba of northwestern Namibia are perhaps the country's most recognizable Indigenous people. Known for covering their skin with a mixture of butterfat and red ochre, they maintain traditions that have survived for centuries.

German Heritage

From 1884 to 1915 Namibia was part of German South West Africa. German influence remains visible in architecture, food, bakeries, breweries, and towns such as Swakopmund and Lüderitz.

Today Namibia blends African traditions with European influences in a uniquely welcoming and cosmopolitan manner.

Brief History
Indigenous peoples inhabited Namibia for thousands of years.
Germany colonized the region in 1884.
South Africa administered the territory following World War I.
Namibia achieved independence in 1990.

The nation is now considered one of Africa's most stable democracies and one of its conservation success stories.

Cuisine

Namibia's food reflects African, German, and South African influences.

Visitors can expect:

Game Meats
Oryx
Springbok
Kudu
Zebra

These are often served as steaks or grilled over open flames.

Braai

Southern Africa's famous barbecue tradition is a social institution.

German-Inspired Foods
Fresh breads
Pretzels
Sausages
Cakes and pastries
Excellent beer
Coastal Seafood

Walvis Bay and Swakopmund offer:

Fresh oysters
Lobster
Atlantic fish

The quality rivals some of the world's best seafood destinations.

Top 3 Must-See Experiences
1. Sunrise at Sossusvlei and Deadvlei

This is arguably one of Earth's great landscape experiences.

Climb one of the giant dunes before dawn and watch sunlight sweep across the desert. Then walk into Deadvlei, where 900-year-old dead acacia trees stand against white clay and red sand.

Why it is unforgettable: Many experienced travelers rank it among the greatest natural spectacles they have ever witnessed.

2. Safari in Etosha National Park

Etosha offers a style of safari unlike anywhere else.

The park's waterholes become gathering points for elephants, rhinos, lions, giraffes, zebras, and antelope. During the dry season, wildlife viewing can be phenomenal.

Must-do: Stay at a lodge with a floodlit waterhole to watch animals throughout the night.

3. Explore Damaraland and the Skeleton Coast

This region showcases Namibia at its wildest.

Expect:

Desert elephants
Ancient rock engravings
Dramatic mountains
Remote luxury lodges
Astonishing night skies

For many luxury travelers, this becomes the highlight of their entire African journey.

Best Time to Visit

Namibia is a year-round destination, but the dry season from May through October is generally considered the best period for most visitors. Wildlife viewing is particularly strong because animals gather around scarce water sources.

May to October

Best Overall

Comfortable temperatures
Excellent wildlife viewing
Clear skies
Great photography
July to October

Best Safari Season

Peak game viewing
Concentrated wildlife around waterholes
Cool mornings and evenings
November to April

Best for Landscapes and Photography

Greener scenery
Dramatic skies
Fewer tourists
Excellent birding
What Makes Namibia's Safaris Different?

Compared with Kenya or Tanzania:

Fewer Vehicles

Wildlife sightings are often shared with only a handful of other guests.

Greater Focus on Landscape

The scenery frequently rivals the wildlife as the main attraction.

Self-Drive Possibilities

Namibia is perhaps Africa's leading self-drive safari destination. Visitors can safely and comfortably explore many regions independently.

Desert Wildlife

Few safari destinations offer:

Desert elephants
Desert lions
Oryx against giant dunes
Wildlife surviving in extreme conditions
Luxury Wilderness

Many lodges are built in spectacular remote settings where guests may feel they have an entire valley to themselves.

Final Thoughts

Namibia is not merely another safari destination. It is one of the world's great adventure and luxury travel experiences, blending desert grandeur, extraordinary wildlife, fascinating cultures, excellent lodges, and a profound sense of space.

For first-time visitors to Africa, it offers accessibility, safety, and unforgettable scenery. For well-traveled explorers who thought they had seen it all, Namibia often delivers something rarer: surprise. The country's immense landscapes, dramatic light, and feeling of endless possibility create memories that differ from any other destination on the continent. Many experienced travelers leave believing that Namibia is not just one of Africa's greatest journeys, but one of the greatest journeys anywhere in the world.

text:
Córdoba: A Centre of Learning in Andalucia
By Deborah Cater
November 14, 2024
In the heart of Andalucia, Córdoba is a captivating city celebrated not only for its architectural wonders but also as a historic epicentre of intellectual and cultural achievement.

A Golden Age of Learning
During the 10th and 11th centuries, Córdoba was one of the most sophisticated cities in the world. Under the rule of the Umayyad dynasty, it emerged as the most important intellectual hub in Europe. This period saw an unprecedented flourishing of knowledge as libraries and academies sprung up throughout the city. Scholars and students from the Islamic world, as well as Jewish and Christian intellectuals, gathered here to exchange ideas and foster learning, laying a foundation for the Renaissance that would later sweep across Europe.

The Great Library of Córdoba was reputed to hold hundreds of thousands of manuscripts, rivalling the collections of even the famed Library of Alexandria. Córdoba was a city of learning and enlightenment, a place where the flow of knowledge was cherished as deeply as the material wealth amassed by the caliphs.

Intellectual Exchange and Multiculturalism
Córdoba’s intellectual landscape was diverse, shaped by the convergence of different cultures and religious traditions. The city exemplified convivencia, a unique co-existence of Muslims, Christians, and Jews who shared not only a physical space but also a commitment to mutual respect and shared learning. This multicultural environment encouraged scholars from all backgrounds to interact and learn from one another, leading to groundbreaking advancements.

Jewish scholars such as Maimonides, one of the most influential Jewish philosophers of the Middle Ages, and Muslim scholars like Ibn Rushd (Averroes), an early proponent of Aristotelian philosophy, made invaluable contributions. Their works, often written in Arabic or Hebrew, would eventually be translated into Latin, bringing ancient and contemporary ideas into Europe.

Legacy of Scientific and Philosophical Innovation
Córdoba’s scientific and philosophical achievements were just as profound as its cultural impact. Fields like astronomy, mathematics, and medicine saw significant advancements due to the work of scholars such as Al-Zahrawi, whose surgical texts were used for centuries across Europe. Cordoban astronomers also made substantial strides, mapping constellations and refining mathematical tools, which would influence the field of navigation for generations.

The city was also a central node in the trade of ideas, where scientific and philosophical texts from ancient Greece, Persia, and India were translated into Arabic and then disseminated across the Mediterranean and beyond. This intellectual cross-pollination would later fuel European scholars’ curiosity, leading to an era of scientific inquiry and humanistic philosophy.

Córdoba’s Architectural Homage to Knowledge
Walking through Córdoba today, the physical spaces echo the city’s past as a centre of learning and enlightenment. The iconic Mezquita-Catedral, originally built as the Great Mosque of Córdoba, is testament to the architectural and intellectual prowess of its time. Its impressive arches, intricate carvings, and cavernous spaces were built to inspire awe and contemplation, a fitting homage to a society that valued learning and introspection.

The Judería, Córdoba’s historic Jewish quarter, remains a reminder of the intellectual contributions of the Jewish community, with narrow, winding streets that lead to the Synagogue of Córdoba, one of the few remaining in Spain. In these historic districts, visitors are invited to ponder the city’s legacy, sensing the echoes of ancient debates and groundbreaking ideas that shaped the course of European history.

Discover the Legacy of Córdoba’s Intellectual Golden Age
TOMA & COE offers unique insights into Córdoba’s historical richness, providing travellers with experiences that reveal the city’s pivotal role as a cradle of knowledge and culture. From guided tours of the Mezquita-Catedral to explorations of the Judería and beyond, TOMA & COE’s tours encourage guests to immerse themselves in the spirit of discovery that defined Córdoba’s Golden Age.

text:
Surely you're kidding if you think the physical action determines whether something is worship. 😂

Abraham "bowed himself to the people of the land" in Genesis 23:7.

Jacob bowed to the ground seven times before Esau in Genesis 33:3.

Bathsheba bowed before King David in 1 Kings 1:16.

Were they worshipping human beings as gods?

Of course not.

Bowing can express worship, honor, respect, submission, or reverence depending upon the OBJECT and INTENTION of the act.

Same with asking favors.

Paul repeatedly asks other Christians to pray for him. Asking someone for something doesn't magically make that person God.

And Catholics aren't asking a STATUE for anything.

If I kneel at my bedside holding a photograph of my deceased father and say, "Dad, I miss you," I haven't suddenly developed the theological belief that Kodak manufactures deities. 😂

The image represents someone.

Catholics distinguish between the image, the saint represented by it, and God Himself.

And Scripture makes an even more devastating distinction for your argument:

God explicitly COMMANDS the making of sacred images.

Two golden cherubim on the Ark - Exodus 25:18-20.

The bronze serpent - Numbers 21:8-9.

Cherubim throughout Solomon's Temple - 1 Kings 6.

So the biblical prohibition obviously isn't:

"Never make a religious image."

It's:

"You shall not make an image and WORSHIP IT AS A GOD."

And Catholics agree completely.

We don't believe statues are gods.
We don't believe Mary is God.
We don't believe the saints are gods.
We don't offer them the worship due to God alone.

So showing me somebody kneeling in front of a statue doesn't establish idolatry any more than showing me Abraham bowing before the Hittites establishes that Abraham worshipped the Hittites.

You have to demonstrate that Catholics believe the statue or saint IS GOD or offer it the worship belonging to God alone.

That's the part your argument keeps skipping.

text:
Day 3 of Navratri: the bride who picked up 10 weapons 🔔

Day 1 gave you a foundation. Day 2 gave you discipline.

Day 3 asks the harder question: when the world tests you, will you stay calm or will you break?

Read this once. You will never confuse "peace" with "weakness" again. 👇

🔥 The story nobody tells you
➤ After years of tapasya, Parvati was finally to marry Lord Shiva
➤ On the wedding day, Shiva arrived as he truly is
➤ Ash on his body, snakes around his neck, ghosts and ganas dancing behind him
➤ Parvati's mother Mena saw the procession and fainted in fear
➤ Parvati did not panic. She did not run
➤ She took a fierce form with ten arms, riding a tiger, a half-moon bell on her forehead
➤ Calm and fearless, she stood before Shiva and asked him to take a gentle form
➤ Shiva agreed and appeared as a handsome prince. The wedding went ahead
➤ The lesson: she was soft enough to love, and strong enough to protect

🙏 How to recognise her
➤ "Chandra" = moon, "Ghanta" = bell
➤ A half-moon shaped like a bell rests on her forehead
➤ Rides a tiger - courage that is always ready
➤ Ten arms holding trishul, gada, sword, bow, arrow, kamandalu, lotus and more
➤ One hand in abhaya mudra - "do not fear"
➤ Golden glow, eyes calm, body ready for battle

🔔 The power of the bell
➤ The sound of her bell is said to scare away negative forces
➤ That is why every temple bell is rung before darshan
➤ One sound clears the noise in your head
➤ The deeper meaning: a strong voice stops trouble before it starts

🌱 Why she comes third
➤ She governs the Manipura chakra, the solar plexus
➤ Manipura = confidence, willpower, personal power
➤ She is linked to Shukra (Venus), the planet of grace and beauty
➤ Root on Day 1. Discipline on Day 2. Courage on Day 3
➤ Peace without strength is just helplessness. She is both

🪔 Puja vidhi: step by step
➤ Bathe early and wear clean red clothes
➤ Check the Akhand Jyot and water the jau
➤ Offer red flowers, kumkum, akshat and sandalwood
➤ Ring a bell during the puja - today it matters most
➤ Offer the bhog, then chant her mantra 108 times
➤ Close with aarti and pray for courage and peace in the home

❤️ Colour of the day: Red
➤ Courage, strength and passion

🥛 Bhog: milk, kheer or milk-based sweets
➤ Offered to remove pain and bring joy to the family
➤ Later, give the prasad to a needy person or a child

🌺 Flowers
➤ Red flowers, especially red lotus or hibiscus

📿 Mantra (108 times)
ॐ देवी चन्द्रघण्टायै नमः
Om Devi Chandraghantayai Namah

🕉️ Dhyan mantra
पिण्डजप्रवरारूढा चण्डकोपास्त्रकैर्युता।
प्रसादं तनुते मह्यं चन्द्रघण्टेति विश्रुता॥

🍎 If you are fasting
➤ Day 3 is when the body settles in. Keep going
➤ Yes: fruits, milk, sabudana, kuttu, singhara, makhana, sendha namak
➤ No: grains, onion, garlic, regular salt, alcohol, non-veg
➤ The real fast today: no fear, no panic, no reacting in anger

✨ What Day 3 is really asking you
➤ What are you avoiding because you are afraid?
➤ When life showed up looking scary, did you faint or did you stand?
➤ Be calm in the moon, fierce like the tiger
➤ You do not need to fight every battle. But you must be ready for one
➤ Ring your bell. Speak up. Protect what is yours

🗓️ Where we are
➤ Day 1 Shailputri ✅ → Day 2 Brahmacharini ✅ → Day 3 Chandraghanta 🔔 → Day 4 Kushmanda → Day 5 Skandamata → Day 6 Katyayani → Day 7 Kalaratri → Day 8 Mahagauri → Day 9 Siddhidatri

Type "Jai Mata Di" 🙏 if you are choosing courage over fear today.
Save this for your puja. Share it with the one person who is fighting a silent battle right now.

Shubh Navratri 🌺

**California Blood Banks Cash In on Midwest Demand for THC-Laced Plasma**

By Mary Jane High  
October 12, 2026  

SACRAMENTO — California blood banks have begun quietly exporting units of whole blood and plasma to several Midwestern states after buyers specifically requested inventory known to contain residual THC from the state’s heavy cannabis users.  

Industry sources confirm that facilities in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and the Inland Empire have shipped more than 4,200 units since August to hospitals and private clinics in Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, and Missouri. Purchasers have stated that they want the blood primarily for its measurable cannabinoid content rather than for ordinary transfusion needs.  

“We test every unit,” said a compliance officer at a major Southern California blood center who spoke on condition of anonymity. “When the THC numbers come back higher than average, we flag those bags. Midwest buyers started asking for the flagged ones by name. They call it ‘West Coast Reserve.’”  

Midwestern hospital administrators describe the product as a low-volume experimental therapy. One Nebraska clinic has used small aliquots of the plasma in patients who previously failed conventional pain protocols. A Kansas private practice has offered it to cash-paying clients seeking “a mild, medically supervised effect without smoking or edibles.” No state medical board has formally approved the practice.  

California regulators have not prohibited the sales. State law requires only that donors meet standard eligibility rules and that blood is screened for infectious disease. THC is not among the mandatory exclusion criteria. Blood banks report that roughly 38 percent of recent donations from urban coastal areas test positive for cannabinoids at levels detectable by standard immunoassay.  

A spokesperson for the American Association of Blood Banks said the organization is reviewing whether units with elevated THC should carry additional labeling. “We are still determining whether this is a clinical feature or a contaminant,” the spokesperson said.  

Midwest buyers have so far paid a premium of $180 to $240 per unit above the usual inter-state transfer rate. California centers say the extra revenue has offset rising collection costs. One facility has begun asking regular donors whether they used cannabis in the previous 48 hours and routing those units into a separate inventory stream labeled “High Desert Premium.”  

No adverse reactions linked to the THC content have been reported in the receiving states. Several Midwestern recipients have, however, requested second units within the same week.
