text:
WODEMAN
A Romaunce in Three Actes

THE JESTER III

In the following month, a new proposal was presented: the arch should be embellished with a frieze depicting the victories of Bològne under Herod's protectioun. The proposal had been submitted by a poet who had received a small appointment in the Hegemon's household and who had discovered that the fastest road to advauncement lay through the expressioun of ideas that Herod had already imagined but had not yet learned how to praise.

The frieze would show the Citie rysing from a cloud of disorder into the clear lyght of a new age. At the centre, Herod himself would stand robed in civic splendour, not as a sovereign but as a guardian of liberty, holding a sheathed swerd in one hond and a book of ordinaunces in the other.

The poet declared that the image would be understood throughout Christendom.

The treasurer asked whether Christendom myght be expected to contribute towards the expense.

The poet stared at him.

Herod did not laugh.

The frieze was commissiouned.

By the time the design had been approved, the cost of the arch had increased beyond the fyrst estimate, and the western quarter had been ordered to surrender another series of houses in order to widen the approach. Several of the families received compensatioun. Others did not. A guild lodged a complaint concernyng the removal of its meeting hall, which had stood upon the same site for a century and possessed rights recorded in several municipal charters.

Herod declared that no ancient privilege could be permitted to obstruct the advauncement of the Citie.

The guild was offered a smaller hall at a distaunce from the principal market, where the members could assemble without interfering with the processioun of commerce.

They accepted the offer.

They had little choice.

The new building lacked sufficient space for all the members, and the distaunce reduced attendaunce at meetings. Several craftsmen ceased paying their guild dues. The guild's charitable fund, from which widows and injured workers had received assistaunce, was diminished by the cost of moving its stores and repairing the new premises.

The office of the One Way recorded the dispute as resolved.

It was during this period of almost dailie improvement that Herod discovered a defect in his happinesse.

The Citie obeyed him. The merchaunts feared him. The magistrates deferred to him. The architects praised his visioun, the poets his grandeur, and the priests his gyfts. His wyfe possessed jewels, silks, gardyns, and attendants. His son was being instructed by scholars selected from among the finest men available, each of whom had been told that the future of the House Malvezzi depended upon the excellence of his pupil.

Yet Herod was bored.

It was not the boredom of a man who has exhausted himself through labour, nor the peaceful wearinesse of one who has fulfilled a long and difficult obligatioun. His was a more peculiar afflictioun: he had grown accustomed to the immediate gratificatioun of desyre, and thus every fulfilled desyre appeared to him less ynteresting than the one which remained beyond his reach.

When he had fyrste sought wealth, a purse of silver had been an occasioun for delyght. Now he could receive the accounts of a hundred thousand florins without experiencing anything beyond impatience at the clerk's slownesse.

When he had fyrst sought influence, a magistrate's favourable word had seemed a conquest. Now the entire council awaited his approval, and their deference had become as ordinary as the lyght of day.

When he had fyrst desyred Desiderata, her attentioun had been precious preciselie because it was not his to command. Now she lived within his household, and every gyft he laid before her seemed to him an affront to his generosité if she failed to respond with gratitude.

Even the One Way, which had so recentlie seized his imaginatioun, had begun to reveal the intolerable weaknesse of all earthlie undertakings: the stones would require years to be laid, the galleries would remain incomplete for months, the statues would need to be carved, and the finished work would thereafter stand in its full perfectioun for the sole purpose of becoming familiar.

Herod could not endure the prospect that the world myght become ordinary again.

He needed a new thing to admire, a new thing to possess, a new event which would compel the attendaunce of his courtiers and give him the agreeable sensatioun that the world had not yet finished arranging itself around him.

This need was not unknown to the sages of olde, who had observed that a man may become more miserable through the satisfactioun of his appetites than through their denial. But Herod had little acquaintaunce with the sages, except when their sayings myght be adapted to decorate an argument he had already decided to win.

He therefore sought entertainment.

Musicians were summoned from neighbouring cities. Jugglers, acrobats, tumblers, dauncers, singers, and men who trained animals to perform small wonders were received into the palays. A companie of players staged a drama concernyng the fall of a tyrant, whose name was altered at Herod's request so that no spectator myght foolishlie connect the villain's behaviour with any living person of consequence. Another companie performed a comedy in which a jealous husband was deceived by his servaunts, and the audience laughed at the husband's stupidité until Herod observed that the man's fortunes were rather too similar to those of a certain magistrate whose favour he required.

The play was thereafter revised.

The magistrate attended the next performaunce and laughed more loudlie than anyone else.

Herod was still bored.

He attended a hunting party, where the hounds pursued a stag through a wodeland whose bounds had recentlie been extended by the acquisitioun of several properties from families unable to meet their debts. He held a banquet for foreign merchaunts and listened to the recitatioun of a new poem composed in his honour. He ordered a great fountain for the palays gardyn, the water of which should rise in the shape of a crown before falling into a marble basin.

The fountain pleaused him for three days.

Then the central jet failed.

The engineers explained that a defect in the supplie pipe had reduced the pressure of the water. Herod asked why such a defect had not been discovered before the fountain was constructed.

The engineers answered that the pipe had been examined, but the fault had arisen under the increased pressure of continuous use.

Herod demaunded to know whether the water itself was disobedient.

No one knew how to answer.

The pipe was repaired, the jet restored, and a new ornament placed at the summit of the fountain. Herod approved it and went elsewhere.

The following week, he ordered the gardyn enlarged.

Thus did his imaginatioun proceed from one dissatisfactioun to another, laying fresh demaunds upon the world whenever the present arrangement began to grow familiar.

It was not enough that he should be wealthy. Others must know it.

It was not enough that he should rule. Others must be reminded of it.

It was not enough that the Citie should be beautiful. Its beauty must be attributable to him.

And it was not enough that he should be entertained. The very nature of entertainment must be transformed into another proof of his authorité.

The court had learned to respond to these demaunds with the practised enthusiasm of servaunts who understood that their employment depended upon the successful management of their master's temper. They proposed entertainments, praised his ideas, anticipated his wyshes, and took care to ensure that no inconvenience should remain visible long enough to interrupt the appearaunce of his satisfactioun.

Yet there persisted a certain emptinesse at the centre of the palays.

The courtiers could praise him, but praise had become predictable.

The musicians could delyght him, but delyght was too brief.

The architects could show him new designs, but every design began to resemble the last.

Herod wanted something which would not merelie obey him.

He wanted something which could resist him, so that he myght enjoy the pleausure of overcoming resistaunce without suffering the danger of being denied.

And, as it happened, such a thing was soon brought to his door.

The man who came to be known throughout the palays as the Jester had been born beneath a less favourable star than the Hegemon, though he had discovered that stars, like other authorities, may be persuaded to look away.

His proper name was Violanté, and his surname, if ever he possessed one by lawful transmissioun, had long since been lost beneath the accumulated titles bestowed upon him by those whom he had offended. Some called him Grillo, on account of his shrill and incessaunt voice; some called him Cagnaccio, because he followed whatever household promessed a full table; some called him the Little Abbot, because of the peculiar delyght he took in burlesquing the habits of clerics. He had served in taverns, wandered with players, slept in stables, been expelled from more than one market town, and acquired the art of making himself useful to men who desyred an object of amusement but had no wysh to be held responsible for the consequences of providing one.

He was not beautiful.

His head was large in proportioun to his body, his cheeks heavy, his nose thick and red, and his mouth so accustomed to a grin that his expressioun appeared to be one of permanent invitatioun. He had a small, dryk beard which he neglected to comb, a pair of livelie eyes whose chief virtue was their readinesse to seek out whatever myght be stolen, and a bellie which testified to the efficacy of any household that had tolerated him for more than a week.

His clothing was a collectioun of motley patches, sewn in the manner of a man who considered neatnesse an unnecessary labour. He wore bells upon his cap, though several were cracked, and a pair of soft shoes which enabled him to move about a hall without attracting the attentioun his voice would inevitablie demaund a moment later.

His gyfts were not extraordinary.

He could mimic the speech of a pompous magistrate, though his imitatioun consisted principallie of pursing his lips and making a noise in the back of his throat. He could tumble upon a rush-covered floor, provided he had consumed no more wyne than was good for him. He knew a modest number of songs, most of them bawdy, and possessed a greater number of jokes, a large proportioun of which relied upon the propositioun that women were greedy, husbands were fools, priests were hypocrites, and anyone who possessed a better garment than Violanté ought to be made to surrender it.

He had never troubled himself to consider whether these opiniouns myght be improved by reflectioun.

He had discovered, rather, that reflectioun was a poore substitute for supper.

Yet he had one talent of considerable practical value: he understood that the riche frequentlie desyre to hear what they already believe, provided it is expressed in a manner that allows them to imagine themselves unusuallie daring for agreeing with it.

Before Herod's court, Violanté would call a fat merchaunt a walking hog, a thin courtier a dried stick, a solemn clerk a bag of wind, and an aged lord a relic whose preservatioun had become more expensive than its use. Such insults, directed at people whom Herod had already judged beneath contempt, brought him applause. When he had exhausted the harmless targets, he moved towards the more dangereux ones, testing each joke with the care of a man dipping a toe into a river.

If the audience laughed, he proceeded.

If the audience did not laugh, he declared the joke too subtle for ordinary minds.

If the person insulted protested, Violanté fell upon his knees and begged forgivenesse with such exaggerated misery that the entire companie laughed at the protester for having taken offence.

He did not know the meanyng of liberty, but he knew its smell.

Liberty smelled of a table from which one myght eat without paying, a chamber in which a man myght sleep without permissioun, and a woman whom he myght pursue without fear that a husband, father, brother, or magistrate would make the pursuit costlie.

When he had found such a place, he treated the discovery as an act of supreme intelligence.

He had been married once, if his own account were to be believed, though he had described the marriage in such contradictory terms that no one could determine whether it had been lawful, theatrical, or merelie a prolonged arrangement for the provisioun of food. He spoke of his wyfe when he wyshed to make a jest concernyng the miseries of matrimony, and denied ever having possessed one when a woman asked whether he had any domestic obligatiouns.

The stories he told of his adventures were numerous and mutuallie incompatible. In one, he had escaped a jealous husband by hiding beneath a table. In another, he had persuaded the husband to forgive him by revealing that his wyfe had been unfaithful with a man of greater wealth. In a third, he had been chased from a town by a processioun of women bearing sticks, all of whom, he claimed, had been overcome by a violént attachment to his person.

It is possible that some of these incidents occurred.

It is more certain that Violanté took pleausance in the telling of them.

He did not consider himself wicked. Wickednesse was a word employed by men who wyshed to deny others the pleausures they had secured for themselves. Violanté's own conscience, when consulted, retourned a brief account of his needs: food, drynk, sleep, and the companie of women. Everything else was a matter of circumstaunce.

He would take a purse if he could reach it.

He would lie if the truth threatened to inconvenience him.

He would flatter a man whose favour he desyred and mock him the moment the favour had been secured.

And if a servaunt was punished for an offence Violanté had committed, he would shrug, explain that the servaunt ought to have been more careful, and ask whether any supper remained.

He was not a monster of exceptiounal design. There were men throughout Bològne who behaved in much the same fashioun, except that they lacked bells upon their caps and were required to conceal their appetites beneath the forms of respectable conduct.

What distinguished Violanté was not the depth of his depravité, but the remarkable extent to which he was willing to exhibit it.

He came to the Malvezzi palays through the recommendatioun of a minor officer who had witnesseed him at a private feast. The officer, a man much given to the appearaunce of knowing amusing people, declared that Violanté possessed a rare and inexhaustible gyft for keeping a companie in good humour. He could imitate a bishop, mock a merchaunt, insult a soldier, and make even the most solemn gathering descend into laughter.

Herod asked whether he could mock a great lord without fear.

The officer assured him that Violanté could mock anyone.

"Anyone?" Herod repeated.

"Anyone, my lord."

"Even a hegemon?"

The officer, who had not expected the questioun to be quite so literal, hesitated for the briefest moment.

"Especiallie a hegemon, my lord."

Herod smiled.

"Bring him."

Violanté arrived at court wearing a motley coat of green, yellow, and faded crimson. His cap was so heavilie adorned with bells that each movement produced a discordant little musique, and he had tied a woden spoon to his belt, for reasons which he explained at considerable length to the guards before they permitted him to pass.

He was conducted into the great hall, where Herod sat beneath the painted heavens. Around the Hegemon were gathered the familiar faces of his administratioun: magistrates, captaines, wealthy merchaunts, architects, poets, clerks, priests, and those more ambiguous persons whose occupatioun consisted in being present wherever power was exercised.

Violanté entered with a stumble.

He recovered himself, made a circle about the hall as though searching for something he had misplaced, and at length approached the dais.

He bowed so low that the bells of his cap struck the floor.

"Rise," said Herod.

Violanté rose onlie halfway.

"My lord, I fear I cannot."

"Why not?"

"I have heard that Your Magnificence commands all things in this Citie to rise in your presence. I thought to make myself an example of obedience, and so have remained upon my knees lest I rise higher than I ought."

A few of the courtiers smiled.

Herod looked at him.

"And who told you that I commanded all things to rise?"

"The steward, my lord."

"Which steward?"

"Whichever one is nearest the kitchenne, for he is the fellow most likelie to know what rises and what does not."

The courtiers laughed.

Herod leaned forward.

"You have a ready tongue."

"It is the onlie part of me that has never been refused supper."

The laughter grew louder.

Herod considered the man. He had seen better tumblers, more accomplished musicians, and fools whose jokes possessed greater ingenuité. Yet Violanté had already performed a serwyse which the others could not: he had made the court laugh without requiring Herod himself to supplie the occasioun.

It was a small distinctioun.

Herod felt it to be a revelatioun.

"Tell me," he said, "what think you of my court?"

Violanté tourned and examined the assembled companie.

He looked at the richlie dressed merchaunts, the solemn magistrates, the young lords whose hair had been arranged by servaunts, the clerks with their papers, the captaines with their polished arms, and the poets whose expressiouns suggested that the world had been constructed primarilie for the purpose of supplieing material for their next verses.

At length he nodded.

"My lord, it is a most excellent court."

"Why so?"

"Because every man here has brought something which he wyshes to conceal, and every man has dressed himself so hondsomelie that no one may be blamed for looking elsewhere."

The hall broke into laughter.

A magistrate coughed.

A merchaunt stared at his cup.

One of the poets, who had spent the mornyng composing a verse in which the Hegemon was likened to a spotless mirror, appeared suddenlie to have discovered an urgent ynterest in the floor.

Herod laughed.

Not his publick laugh, the measured and agreeable sound with which he acknowledged the clevernesse of others, but a fuller laugh that rose from his chest and continued long enough to surprise him.

He struck the arm of his chair.

"Again!"

Violanté, who possessed an excellent instinct for the appetite of his audience, began at once to imitate the manner in which a magistrate examined a petitioun, the pomp with which a merchaunt declared himself ruined, the solemn gait of a priest retournyng from a feast, and the peculiar grimace adopted by a courtier who wyshed to demonstrate that he had understood a joke before anyone else.

Each imitatioun was coarse, exaggerated, and imperfect. Violanté knew little of the inner nature of the men he mocked, and what he did know he had learned through observatioun of their clothing, their gestures, and their appetites. Yet the imperfectiouns made the performaunce more pleausing, for the court was not assembled to hear a profound examinatioun of human follie. It desyred merelie to be assured that the follie of others was greater than its own.

When Violanté had finished, Herod summoned him nearer.

"What shall I give you?"

Violanté looked about the hall, then towards the tables beyond.

"My lord, I had hoped for a little supper."

"You shall have supper."

"And a bed?"

"You shall have a bed."

"And a cup of wyne?"

"You shall have wyne."

Violanté folded his honds.

"My lord, I begin to perceive why they have made you Hegemon."

The court laughed once more.

Herod ordered that Violanté should be lodged in the palays, provided with a proper allowaunce, and maintained as a permanent member of his household. A tailor was to make him garments worthy of his statioun. A servaunt was to attend him. He was to be permitted access to the great hall whenever the Hegemon desyred amusement, and he should answer to no officer save Herod himself.

These provisiouns were delivered in the hearing of the assembled companie.

Every person present understood that a new privilege had been created.

No one understood quite how far it would extend.

Violanté understood onlie that he had secured a bed, supper, wyne, and a place near the source of his future comforts. He bowed with renewed energy, nearlie struck himself in the face with his own cap, and declared that he would serve Herod until death, or until the kitchenne ceased to provide the sort of meat he considered necessary for a man of his calling.

Herod laughed again.

The jester had been appointed.

It was soon discovered that Violanté considered the limits of his office to be much broader than those which Herod had actuallie prescribed.

On the fyrst evenyng following his appointment, he ate with such determinatioun that the servaunts were obliged to bring a second dish. On the next, he entered the wyne cellar without permissioun and emerged bearing a bottle which had been reserved for a visiting bishop. When the cellarer remonstrated with him, Violanté explained that he was engaged in an act of religious preparatioun, for no man should be expected to entertain a bishop without fyrste acquiring some knowledge of the sacred substaunce over which the bishop presided.

The cellarer informed him that the wyne was not intended for immediate consumptioun.

"Then it is a wyne of unusual patience," Violanté replied. "I shall endeavour not to offend it by keeping it waiting."

He drank the bottle.

The cellarer complained to the household steward, who complained to the chamberlain, who finallie approached Herod with a request that the jester be instructed concernyng the proper use of the cellars.

Herod asked whether the wyne had been wasted.

The chamberlain replied that it had been consumed.

"Then it was not wasted."

The chamberlain attempted to explain that certain bottles were intended for particular occasiouns, and that the order of the cellar had been established according to the needs of the household.

Herod waved his hond.

"Do we employ a fool, or a second cellarer? Let him drynk what he pleauses, provided he entertains us."

The chamberlain withdrew.

Violanté learned of the complaint and thereafter made a habit of entering the cellar whenever he was bored.

He took the same view of the kitchennes, the wardrobes, the private gardyns, and the servaunts' quarters. He appropriated food that had been set aside for others, borrowed garments without asking, and wandered into chambers where his presence had not been invited. He was reprimanded by servaunts who possessed little authorité and ignored by those who possessed too much to be troubled.

At fyrste his conduct produced a successioun of minor inconveniences. A page was blamed for the disappearaunce of a silver cup. A kitchenne boy received a beating because the jester had stolen a dish intended for an importaunt guest. A maid was dismissed after a length of embroidered cloth, which Violanté had taken to wrap around his shoulders, was discovered missing from the wardrobe.

When it was learned that Violanté had been responsible, Herod laughed at the absurdité of the incidents and ordered that the servaunts be compensated for their trouble.

The maid did not receive her place again.

The kitchenne boy was obliged to retourn to his village.

The page remained in serwyse, but was thereafter watched as though he had developed a particular talent for theft.

Violanté, meanwhile, acquired another garment and a new story concernyng the wickednesse of servaunts.

He also acquired a reputatioun among the women of the household.

Some avoided him. Others, who had been required to attend him by the duties of their office, endured his coarse remarks with the expressioun of those who know that a refusal may prove more costlie than sylence. He addressed maidens as though they were characters in a tavern song, commented upon their bodies, demaunded kysses in exchaunge for scraps of food, and boasted loudlie of the women he claimed to have enjoyed before entering the Hegemon's serwyse.

The boasts varied according to the audience.

Before men, he represented himself as irresistible.

Before women, he represented himself as a victim of irresistible affectioun.

Before his employers, he declared that the troubles of the household arose because certain women had become enamoured of him and sought his attentioun at inconvenient times.

His conduct was not always received with amusement. A young serving woman whom he cornered beside a stair struck him across the mouth with a woden tray. Violanté retreated, clutching his cheek, and announced to everyone who would listen that he had been assaulted by a woman of violént passiouns.

text:
Hello, I am Palestinian. 
And since honesty is rare in my politics, let me admit a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised the war would "throw the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and it was called the Nakba. Not because I was not offered a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. The Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they kept me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and cages for me. They used me as propaganda, not as a human being.

1967. After another war I lost, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three no's. Fifty years later, I am still without a state. It turns out rejection does not pay the rent.

Oslo, the 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions of dollars in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an Intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I got a chance to turn Gaza into the Singapore of the Mediterranean. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions of dollars in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I have not had elections for almost 20 years. Hamas kills opponents in Gaza. Fatah jails them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they are too busy fighting over power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on television who teach children to hate Jews. I praise the "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I replace hope with holy war.

The Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They marginalize me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next to Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a technological superpower, farms in the desert, cities from dust. Without oil, without endless wealth, only with courage. I could have learned, copied, cooperated. Instead, I chose jealousy and anger.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of presenting respect, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I presented only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to Jews. And then I wonder why Israelis do not trust me, why they are angry, disappointed, and convinced that I do not want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I praise death more than life? Israel's fault. Responsibility is not my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own decisions, and my own refusal to abandon hatred.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit.

text:
A. Your Personality

Although Elon Musk possesses vast wealth and controls major corporations, I view him as someone who seeks to act for the benefit of all humanity—driven by motives that go beyond mere financial gain.

However, I must clearly express my opposition to the idea of ​​building rockets for a mass exodus from Earth—essentially constructing a modern-day Noah's Ark.

I believe that the original teachings of Christianity, Islam, and Judaism were never intended to instill fear regarding the apocalypse or the finitude of time; rather, they offered a path for people to live better lives and, ultimately, find happiness. I feel that these teachings have been distorted, reinterpreted, and misused.

Given this, I would propose that we abandon the concepts of apocalyptic doom and the fear associated with limited time.

Regarding the concept of limited time: while current science—including medical technology—cannot grant us infinite life, and we will all inevitably die, the evidence of our lives and the legacy of history are passed on to future generations.
In that sense, I do not view death as an absolute end.
Furthermore, certain religions—such as Tibetan Buddhism—teach the concept of reincarnation, suggesting that we are reborn as humans or other living beings until we complete a specific mission or task.
While the span of a single lifetime may indeed be quite limited, perhaps we should view our existence not as something that ends, but as part of a cycle—considering it in terms of the soul's journey rather than a final conclusion.

text:
My Lions Party platform for the 2026 US Midterms, which overshadows both established parties and unites a convincing majority of the American population, can overcome deep ideological divides and focus on pragmatic, popular solutions to the most pressing everyday problems.

https://t.co/hRv4sutf8A

According to current polls and sociological data, my Lions Party "Super-Platform" would need to include the following core points:

1. Economy: Strengthening the Middle Class & Purchasing Power
Economic concerns are almost always the most important voting criterion for US citizens.
• Radical reduction in the cost of living: Capping the prices of essential medicines (such as insulin) and eliminating hidden fees ("junk fees") across all economic sectors.
• Tax relief for workers, closing loopholes: Lowering income tax for the lower and middle-income brackets, funded by a strict minimum tax on billionaires and large corporations (a point supported by both left-wing and populist right-wing voters).
• "Made in America" infrastructure: Massive investments in roads, bridges, the power grid, and modern technologies, coupled with the requirement to use American materials and labor.

2. Healthcare: Affordability Without System Overhaul
Americans do not want a purely state-run system like in Europe, but they hate the current bureaucratic and expensive system.
• Transparent pricing & negotiation rights: Requiring hospitals and laboratories to disclose all prices upfront. At the same time, granting full rights to the federal Medicare program to negotiate the prices of all drugs directly with the pharmaceutical industry.
• Protection against medical debt: Prohibiting medical debt from negatively impacting citizens' credit scores.

3. Security & Migration: Pragmatic Border Protection
An extremely polarizing issue where a large majority of Americans are actually looking for a middle ground.
• Strict border security with humane efficiency: A massive increase in border patrol agents and modern scanning systems at crossings, combined with a tripling of immigration judges to legally conclude asylum proceedings within days rather than years.
• Combating the fentanyl crisis: Classifying the smuggling of synthetic opioids as a national security threat with draconian penalties for cartels, paired with nationwide addiction treatment options at home.

4. Government Reform: Fighting Corruption ("Drain the Swamp")
Frustration with the political class in Washington is the greatest bipartisan unifying factor.
• Banning stock trading for members of Congress: Representatives and Senators would no longer be allowed to buy or sell individual stocks during their term in office to stop insider trading.
• Term limits: Introducing maximum terms for members of Congress (e.g., a maximum of 12 years in the House of Representatives or Senate) to prevent "career politicians."
• Restricting lobby money: Banning donations from so-called Super PACs and foreign interest groups.

5. Society & Family: Everyday Support
Instead of culture war issues (culture wars surrounding gender or religion), this platform focuses on the family budget.
• Affordable childcare: Introducing a permanent, generous child allowance in the form of tax credits (Child Tax Credit) and federal subsidies for daycare centers.
• Protecting online privacy: A strict national data privacy law that specifically protects children and teenagers from the algorithms of major tech corporations.

Why this Lions Party platform would beat both existing parties
The Lions Party platform breaks with the traditional political geography of the US: It takes the economic and anti-corruption components of the populists (from both the left and the right) and combines them with the conservatives' demand for stability, law, and order, as well as the progressives' social protection measures. Because it deliberately excludes toxic culture war issues (such as abortion or gun laws) or leaves them to local states, it offers no ideological targets and focuses purely on the economic and structural benefit for the "average" American.

Boldly Honest Successful and always Direct!

text:
Tuesday morning headlines from #Azerbaijn, 13 October

● Authorities in Baku are actively monitoring compliance with school uniform rules for pupils and clothing requirements for teachers in state schools, including the requirement that they be secular. Female pupils and teachers wearing religious headscarves are being asked to remove them or face suspension from classes. Protests in support of classmates and colleagues have been held outside many schools. The Interior Ministry said 37 people had been arrested. More details and several videos here https://t.co/sYdtv2apRB

● The Media and Broadcasting Council urged citizens not to fall for information manipulation surrounding uniform dress rules in schools, saying that “certain groups are trying to politicise the issue and give it a religious character”. According to the Council, similar posts and comments are being deliberately circulated on social media, suggesting a coordinated campaign allegedly directed from abroad. The Council said the aim was to create the artificial impression of widespread public discontent and heighten social tensions.

● A delegation led by Czech Transport Minister Ivan Bednárik has arrived in Azerbaijan.

● Czech company Škoda Group plans to establish a joint venture in Baku to manufacture and service transport vehicles for markets in the Caucasus and Central Asia. Škoda Group deputy chairman Tomáš Ignačák announced the plan during an expanded meeting in Baku between Bednárik, representatives of Azerbaijan’s AZCON Transport and Communications Holding, and the country’s railway industry executives.

● Azerbaijan plans to expand railway cooperation with the Czech Republic, including the supply of engineering equipment, introduction of innovative technologies and infrastructure modernisation, AZCON executive director Shahin Babayev said. He stressed that Azerbaijan is investing heavily in railways, ports and logistics to strengthen its role in the North–South and East–West corridors and become a regional logistics hub.

● Czech direct investment in Azerbaijan reached $74 million between 1995 and the end of the first half of 2026, with around $70 million going to the non-oil and gas sector, a business forum in Baku was told. Azerbaijan’s investment in the Czech Republic over the same period totalled around $70 million. Thirty-four Czech companies operate in Azerbaijan, while transit freight between the two countries rose by 47% in 2025.

● President Ilham Aliyev held an expanded meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, who is visiting Azerbaijan. Aliyev expressed confidence that the visit would be highly productive and continue efforts to develop active bilateral cooperation. Aliyev was invited to visit Cambodia.

● An Azerbaijan–Cambodia business forum was held in Baku, focusing on potential joint investment in renewable energy, agricultural processing, logistics and digital services. Oknha Sok Piseth, president of the Federation of Employers and Business Associations of Cambodia, said Cambodia could export rice, cashews, mangoes and other agricultural products through Azerbaijan to markets in the South Caucasus and Central Asia. He also highlighted prospects for transport and logistics cooperation, with Cambodia potentially helping connect ASEAN countries — the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, which has 11 members — with the Caspian region.

● Cambodia is ready to offer Azerbaijani investors tax incentives for up to 12 years, allow full foreign ownership of businesses and guarantee the free repatriation of capital, Prime Minister Hun Manet said at the business forum. He cited the country’s young, skilled workforce, strategic location, access to regional markets and development of renewable energy among its advantages.

● Azerbaijan could learn from Cambodia’s experience in processing raw cotton into finished products, Economy Minister Mikayil Jabbarov said at the business forum. He said the countries could also develop logistics routes and cooperation in artificial intelligence, digital technologies, data centres and paperless trade. Jabbarov said Cambodia could provide Azerbaijani companies with access to Southeast Asian markets and urged businesses and logistics operators to explore opportunities for cooperation.

● Azerbaijan is preparing an agreement with Cambodia on the mutual protection and promotion of investment, Jabbarov said. The two countries have already signed an agreement on avoiding double taxation. He identified mining, green energy and investment projects in Azerbaijan’s industrial parks as potential areas for cooperation.

● Cambodia has called on Azerbaijan to open a full diplomatic mission in Phnom Penh.

● A delegation led by Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni arrived in Azerbaijan to discuss expanding cooperation in emergency management. Momeni met President Ilham Aliyev, with both sides stressing the importance of high-level cooperation, including in security and public order.

● Momeni and Azerbaijan’s Emergency Situations Minister Kamaladdin Heydarov discussed information-sharing and coordination in responding to emergencies. The Iranian interior minister thanked Azerbaijan for providing humanitarian assistance during major emergencies.

● The president of Laos has arrived in Azerbaijan for an official visit.

● Azerbaijan has approved an agreement with Slovakia on the exchange and mutual protection of classified information.

● French company Vallourec, which specialises in high-quality seamless pipes, is joining the development of the Absheron gas field in the Caspian Sea off Azerbaijan. The company will supply more than 16,000 tonnes of seamless pipes, with around 159 km of anti-corrosion-coated line pipe also planned.

● Italy will be the main partner country at BakuBuild 2026, which opens in Baku tomorrow, 14 October, and will present a national pavilion featuring 24 companies. They will showcase construction and engineering solutions, innovative materials, energy-efficient technologies and products for sustainable urban infrastructure. The participation is organised by the Italian Trade Agency in cooperation with industry federations, with the stated aim of expanding trade and industrial cooperation with Azerbaijan.

● Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi will make his first official visit to Azerbaijan in seven years. On 15 October, he will attend the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit as a special representative of the Chinese president. Talks with Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov are also planned.

● A ceremony was held in Baku to launch the joint Azerbaijan–United Arab Emirates tactical flying exercises “Falcon Meet 2026”. Military aviation and air defence units are taking part.

● Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said peace between Azerbaijan and Armenia had been established to some extent both de facto and de jure, although a peace treaty had not yet been signed. He said the two countries’ leaders had already initialled a peace agreement. Pashinyan also recalled the joint declaration on peace adopted in Washington on 8 August 2025 and said that in 2024 Baku and Yerevan had signed their first legally binding bilateral document on state border delimitation, which was subsequently ratified by both countries.

● Brenda Shaffer, an energy and foreign policy expert and Atlantic Council fellow, has outlined five lessons the world can learn from the rapid progress towards resolving the Armenian-Azerbaijani conflict:

1. Military action can shape diplomatic outcomes.

Elon Musk is once again at the center of major political, technological and business debates, with developments spanning Washington, artificial intelligence, electric vehicles, space technology and international telecommunications. His expanding influence highlights how one entrepreneur’s decisions can affect industries and public discussions across the world.

💰 A MASSIVE ROLE IN AMERICAN POLITICS

Recent reports published on October 12 indicate that Musk has contributed more than $276 million to Republican-aligned political groups since July, bringing his reported spending during the election cycle to approximately $366 million. His financial support includes organizations seeking to influence the 2026 US midterm elections, making him one of the most prominent billionaire donors in American politics. Republicans see major financial backing as an advantage in competitive congressional races, while critics warn that enormous political contributions can give wealthy individuals disproportionate influence over public policy. The ultimate impact will depend on voter turnout, campaign performance and the results of the November elections.

🤖 xAI AND GROK IN THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RACE

Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI, continues to compete in a rapidly developing market dominated by powerful technology companies. Its Grok platform is part of a broader strategy connecting AI development with the social media network X and Musk's wider technology businesses. The challenge is to deliver increasingly capable models while managing computing costs, competition, product reliability and public concerns about AI safety. The company's future success will depend on whether it can turn its technological ambitions into sustainable commercial growth.

🚀 SPACEX AND STARLINK PUSH TOWARD GLOBAL CONNECTIVITY

SpaceX is pursuing opportunities beyond rocket launches, with Starlink seeking to expand satellite internet access into additional markets. India remains a particularly important opportunity because of its enormous population and competitive telecommunications industry. However, regulatory approvals, security requirements, infrastructure and affordability remain essential hurdles. If Starlink can establish a commercially viable presence, satellite connectivity could offer another option for customers in remote communities and areas underserved by conventional broadband.

🇮🇳 STARLINK'S COMPETITION WITH INDIA'S TELECOM GIANTS

Musk's ambitions in India have also drawn attention to competition with established telecommunications businesses, including Reliance Industries. Differences over satellite spectrum policy and market access have made the issue commercially and politically significant. Starlink must demonstrate that its service can compete on price, reliability and coverage while complying with Indian regulations. Any suggestion that approval or a final market agreement has already been secured should be treated cautiously until confirmed by official announcements.

🦾 TESLA OPTIMUS: THE CHALLENGE OF BUILDING USEFUL HUMANOID ROBOTS

Tesla's Optimus programme represents another major element of Musk's long-term vision. Developing a robot that can reliably handle everyday objects requires far more than impressive demonstrations. Precise hand movements, tactile sensing, balance, safe operation and dependable software remain substantial engineering challenges. Musk has highlighted the difficulty of replicating the dexterity of the human hand, particularly when performing delicate tasks. If Tesla eventually delivers reliable robots at commercially competitive prices, the technology could have applications in factories and other workplaces. For now, practical performance and large-scale production remain crucial tests.

Paul Staniland’s piece is fair and candid. I agree with much of it.

India has long enjoyed bipartisan backing in Washington. That backing rested largely on a shared assessment of India’s strategic value. When that assessment changes, yesterday’s consensus offers little protection.

The Senate’s 86–11 vote on August 7, 2026, for Russia sanctions that could hit India makes this clear. Democrat Richard Blumenthal later explicitly told India to buy its oil elsewhere. Pressure on India has support across party lines. Democrats can criticise Trump’s treatment of India and still accept damage to the relationship when confronting Russia takes priority.

Blaming Trump alone, or the Republicans, misses this broader shift. The same political forces that helped build the partnership are willing to sacrifice its interests for other goals. A Democratic administration might treat India more respectfully without restoring its previous priority. India has little electoral weight to make that choice costly.

text:
No, James Dolan did not choose Amar'e Stoudemire over LeBron James. In fact, it was completely the other way around: the Knicks aggressively pursued LeBron James as their top choice, but James rejected New York after a presentation that insiders widely described as a disaster. 

How the 2010 Decisions Played Out
•LeBron Was the Primary Target: The Knicks spent two full years intentionally clearing salary-cap space specifically to sign LeBron James in the summer of 2010. He was always Plan A. 
•The "Disastrous" Pitch Meeting: Rumors and reports from NBA insiders, including Bill Simmons, revealed that the Knicks' initial free-agency meeting with LeBron went incredibly poorly. Owner James Dolan reportedly lacked a prepared basketball presentation and instead focused on non-basketball pitches and even famously handing out copies of his blues band's CD to those in the room. James refused to grant the Knicks a second meeting after that. 
•The Stoudemire Insurance Plan: On Sunday, July 4, 2010, word leaked that LeBron James was delaying his decision. Fearing they would be left completely empty-handed, Dolan and team president Donnie Walsh pivoted on July 5 to offer Stoudemire a 5-year, $99.7 million max contract.
•Not an Impediment: Before committing to Stoudemire, Knicks management explicitly verified that his contract would still leave them enough cap space to sign LeBron if he chose New York. Stoudemire even openly recruited LeBron to join him. 
Ultimately, Stoudemire was the "consolation prize" after LeBron spurned New York to join the Miami Heat. Years later, former player Charles Oakley even noted that LeBron privately cited Dolan's management style and behavior as the core reason he would never play for the Knicks.

text:
No Flock Cameras on the Atchafalaya Basin Bridge: Separating Fact from Speculation in the Christin “Chrissy” Munn-Holliday Case

Missing Lost And Trafficked 
Lured Lost And Unsolved 

Lafayette, La.-Amid the ongoing investigation into the September 30, 2026, disappearance of 22-year-old Christin “Chrissy” Munn-Holliday from Katy, Texas, social media and public discussion have circulated claims about the presence—or absence—of Flock Safety automated license plate reader (ALPR) cameras on Louisiana’s Atchafalaya Basin Bridge.

 Her gray late-model BMW was found empty after a hit-and-run crash on I-10 eastbound near milepost 128 in Iberville Parish, close to the Whiskey Bay exit.

 Authorities say preliminary evidence indicates she left the scene on foot; her family disputes this account, notes the difficulty of going unnoticed on the roughly 18-mile elevated span, and has pointed to traffic camera footage of her driving at high speed, raising the possibility she was being pursued.

The Misinformation
Claims have suggested that Flock cameras (or similar ALPRs capable of capturing plates, vehicle details, and timestamps) were already active on the bridge and should have recorded her vehicle, the other car involved, or her movements after the crash. 

Comments in  online discussion have asked variations of “Where’s your Flock cameras when you need them?” Some appear to conflate Flock-style ALPRs with the separate, canceled plan for automated speed-enforcement cameras.

 In reality, no Flock Safety cameras (or any photo-enforcement speed cameras) were installed on the bridge itself.

 Flock systems, which use AI to log plates, make, model, color, and other features and share data with law enforcement for investigations (typically retaining data for about 30 days), are deployed in many Louisiana communities, but mapping and official records do not place them on the Atchafalaya Basin Bridge corridor.

This gap fuels speculation, especially given the family’s emphasis on reviewing available surveillance and the remote nature of the elevated roadway through swamp terrain.

Cameras Actually Active Near the Bridge
What exists near the crash site is more limited and different in purpose:

DOTD traffic monitoring camera Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development (DOTD) and 511LA networks provide live views at approaches including Henderson, Whiskey Bay, and Butte La Rose. These help monitor fog, congestion, and incidents for the public and responders. 

Family accounts have referenced traffic camera video of Munn-Holliday’s driving. They are not continuous ALPR systems designed to log every plate or vehicle for later investigative search.

Your speed” radar feedback signs**: Installed as part of safety upgrades (completed around July 2024). These display a driver’s speed in real time and may flash a slowdown warning. They collect aggregate speed data to help target enforcement but do not photograph plates, issue tickets, or function as surveillance cameras.

Local law enforcement ALPR capability Iberville Parish Sheriff’s Office has used automated license plate readers since at least 2017—initially mobile units on patrol vehicles and plans for fixed cameras focused on uninsured motorists, hot sheets (stolen vehicles, Amber alerts), and investigations. St. Martin Parish and nearby areas (Lafayette, East Baton Rouge) have broader ALPR/Flock deployments. 

These are generally at pinch points, high-traffic roads, or community locations rather than continuous coverage of the full bridge span. DeFlock and similar volunteer maps document dozens of ALPR cameras in the broader parishes but none specifically documented as Flock units fixed on the bridge itself.

Standard highway signage for the safety corridor remains, and Louisiana State Police and local agencies continue traditional enforcement. The early-morning timing of the crash (around 1 a.m.) and the bridge’s narrow shoulders further limit incidental capture by any existing systems.

The Failed 2024 Effort to Install Cameras
In 2022, Act 426 (championed under then-Senate President Page Cortez) designated the Atchafalaya Basin Bridge a Highway Safety Corridor due to high crash rates (averaging more than one every two days in prior years, with multiple fatalities). 

It authorized a three-phase approach: additional signage (phase 1), “your speed” feedback devices (phase 2), and automated camera safety devices for speed enforcement with doubled fines (phase 3). Revenues were to support camera operations, with the remainder going to Iberville and St. Martin parishes. DOTD began preparatory work, including signage and the feedback signs.

In 2024, Sen. Blake Miguez (R-New Iberia), joined by others, introduced SB 379 to repeal the camera mandate and the doubled-fine provisions. The bill passed the Senate 38-0 and the House 92-0. Supporters, including the Iberville and St. Martin parish sheriffs, argued that human officers provide better real-time enforcement, can address issues like unsafe vehicles or trafficking during stops, and keep fine revenue in local criminal justice systems rather than private camera contractors. Gov. Jeff Landry signed it; the law took effect August 1, 2024. The speed-enforcement cameras were never installed. Phase 2 feedback signs and related signage stayed in place, and the speed limit was set at 60 mph for all vehicles (with trucks still restricted to the right lane).

This legislative reversal is the factual basis for the absence of automated enforcement cameras on the bridge. It was never a Flock ALPR project; it was a DOTD-managed speed-camera program aimed at crash reduction.

The distinction matters for the Munn-Holliday investigation: available traffic cameras and any nearby ALPR data (mobile or fixed in the parishes) can still be relevant and have been referenced by family members, but there is no dense Flock grid on the bridge itself that would automatically log every vehicle and passenger-side details at the crash location.

 Authorities have described the case as active and ongoing, with coordination between Louisiana State Police (crash) and Harris County Sheriff’s Office (missing person), plus volunteer search support from groups like the United Cajun Navy. A $20,000 reward has been offered for information leading to her safe return.

Public speculation is understandable given the circumstances and the bridge’s isolation, but accurate information about what technology is (and is not) present helps focus attention on the evidence that does exist and the questions still unanswered.

text:
Tax dollars reach media companies through several distinct channels—some direct, some indirect. Commercial networks like ABC and Fox primarily benefit from paid advertising and production incentives, while public media has historically received more structured appropriations.

Government advertising purchases (largest commercial channel)
The federal government is one of the country’s biggest advertisers, spending roughly $1–1.3 billion per year across all media. Much of this goes to commercial television, cable, digital platforms, and print for military recruitment, public-health campaigns, disaster messaging, and other communications. 
•  Networks and stations (including ABC, Fox, CBS, NBC, CNN, and others) are paid market rates for the airtime, just as they are paid by any other advertiser.
•  High-profile recent examples include Department of Homeland Security / Customs and Border Protection ads placed on Fox, ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN, and other outlets. These have drawn scrutiny when the content is promotional or political, but the mechanism is still a commercial ad buy funded by appropriated dollars. 
State and local governments also buy advertising and place legal notices in newspapers.
3. Film and television production tax incentives
Dozens of states offer transferable or refundable tax credits (often 20–40% of qualified spending) to attract film and TV production. California’s program is now funded at about $750 million annually; New York, Georgia, and others run large programs as well. 
•  Major studios (Disney/ABC-related entities, Warner Bros., Paramount, etc.) regularly receive tens or hundreds of millions in credits for series and films. Credits can offset state taxes or be sold to other taxpayers.
•  Federal proposals for a national 20–30% production tax credit have been introduced; past rules (such as Section 181) allowed accelerated deductions for production costs. Advertising costs themselves have long been fully deductible, which some economists treat as a large tax expenditure that benefits media outlets.

Spectrum access and other regulatory benefits
Commercial broadcasters receive free (or very low-cost) licenses to use public electromagnetic spectrum. In exchange they accept public-interest obligations (local news, emergency alerts, children’s programming rules, etc.). Critics call the free spectrum an indirect subsidy; defenders note the public-interest quid pro quo and the fact that spectrum is allocated rather than sold at full auction value for broadcast use.
Retransmission consent rules also allow stations to negotiate fees from cable and satellite providers. Those fees ultimately come from subscribers, not directly from taxes, but the regulatory framework shapes the revenue.

 Their main taxpayer-linked revenue comes from selling airtime to government advertisers and from production incentives that reduce the cost of making content.

When these old college friends (who never dated) unexpectedly reunite on the way to the enchanted world of Gambler’s Folly, sparks fly and a full-blown romance blooms. Will they seize this second chance at a happily-ever-after, or will doubts and fears snatch it away? On Gambler’s Folly, every love story is a gamble—and Fate always deals the final hand. A slow-burn friends-to-lovers tale full of heart, sensuality, and the series’ signature fantasy charm.

text:
🚨BREAKING: $20 BILLION AI data center in North Carolina is facing a massive backlash, and it raises a question that EVERY American community should be asking.
How much are we willing to sacrifice to build the future of artificial intelligence?
Across the country, massive technology companies are racing to construct AI data centers.
We’re talking about facilities filled with thousands of powerful computers operating around the clock.
And while these projects can bring billions of dollars in investment, construction jobs, and additional tax revenue, there’s another side to the story that doesn’t get nearly enough attention.
ELECTRICITY.
WATER.
LAND.
INFRASTRUCTURE.
And the people who actually LIVE in these communities.
Because AI data centers aren’t your typical office buildings.
They can require enormous amounts of electricity to operate and significant cooling resources to keep equipment from overheating.
Depending on the facility and its cooling technology, water consumption can also become a major concern.
And here’s where things get interesting.
Imagine living in a quiet community for 20 years.
You bought your home.
Raised your children.
Paid your property taxes.
Then one day, you find out that a multibillion-dollar technology project could be built near your neighborhood.
Suddenly, residents are asking questions.
Will our electricity bills increase?
Where is all that power coming from?
How much water will this facility consume?
Will the project create permanent local jobs, or mostly temporary construction work?
And who benefits financially from the tax incentives being offered?
Those are LEGITIMATE questions.
Because when a company announces a $20 billion investment, politicians often celebrate the dollar amount before explaining what the community might be giving up in return.
And I’m not against artificial intelligence.
AI could revolutionize medicine, education, scientific research, and countless industries.
But technological progress shouldn’t mean local residents lose their voice in decisions that affect their neighborhoods.
If companies want communities to welcome these enormous projects, they should be willing to demonstrate that the benefits outweigh the costs.
That means transparent environmental reviews, responsible water usage, infrastructure planning, and clear commitments to local communities.
Because the people living next to these facilities shouldn’t be the last ones to find out what’s happening.
The bigger question is whether America can lead the AI revolution WITHOUT forcing ordinary communities to absorb costs they never agreed to.
And that’s a conversation worth having before billions of dollars are spent.
So I’m curious.
Would you SUPPORT a $20 BILLION AI data center being built near your neighborhood if it created jobs and economic growth, or would you OPPOSE it because of the potential impact on electricity, water, and your community?

A Super-Platform to Unite the American Majority

Our nation is trapped in deep ideological divides, orchestrated by an obsolete political establishment. The Lions Party platform shatters the traditional political geography of the United States. We bridge the gap by combining the economic security and anti-corruption focus of populists with the stability, law, and order of conservatives, and the essential social protections of progressives.
By deliberately leaving toxic, polarizing culture-war issues to the individual states, we offer zero ideological targets. Instead, we focus entirely on pragmatic, high-impact, and popular solutions for the economic and structural benefit of the average American.

1. Economy: Strengthening the Middle Class & Purchasing Power

Economic concerns are the ultimate priority for American citizens. We will directly restore the purchasing power of hard-working families.
• Radical Reduction in the Cost of Living: We will cap the skyrocketing prices of essential life-saving medicines (such as insulin) and eliminate hidden, predatory fees ("junk fees") across all corporate and financial sectors.
• Tax Relief for Workers, Closing Corporate Loopholes: We will drastically lower income taxes for the lower and middle-income brackets. This relief will be fully funded by a strict, non-negotiable minimum tax on billionaires and multinational corporations—a move backed by an overwhelming majority of both left-wing and populist right-wing voters.
• "Made in America" Infrastructure: We will launch massive, targeted investments into our roads, bridges, power grids, and modern technologies. This expansion will be strictly coupled with the legal requirement to utilize American materials and American labor.

2. Healthcare: Affordability Without System Overhaul

Americans fiercely reject a purely state-run, bureaucratic health system like those in Europe, but they despise the current, opaque, and hyper-expensive model.
• Transparent Pricing & Direct Negotiation Rights: We will legally mandate all hospitals, clinics, and medical laboratories to disclose clear, upfront prices before any treatment. Simultaneously, we will grant full, unrestricted rights to the federal Medicare program to negotiate drug prices directly with the pharmaceutical industry.
• Protection Against Medical Debt: We will pass federal legislation prohibiting any medical debt from negatively impacting a citizen’s credit score (Credit Score), ensuring a health crisis does not lead to financial ruin.

3. Security & Migration: Pragmatic Border Protection

Border security is a heavily polarized topic where the vast majority of Americans are actually looking for a common-sense, effective middle ground.
• Strict Border Security with Humane Efficiency: We will deploy a massive increase in border patrol agents and equip crossings with state-of-the-art technological scanning systems. To eliminate the multi-year backlogs, we will triple the number of federal immigration judges to legally and safely resolve asylum proceedings within days rather than years.
• Combating the Fentanyl Crisis: We will legally classify the smuggling of synthetic opioids as a paramount national security threat. This allows the full utilization of federal law enforcement to enact draconian penalties against foreign drug cartels, paired with the rapid expansion of nationwide, accessible addiction treatment options at home.

4. Government Reform: Fighting Corruption ("Drain the Swamp")

The deep-seated frustration with the career political class in Washington, D.C. is the single greatest bipartisan unifying factor in modern America.
• Banning Stock Trading for Members of Congress: To permanently eliminate insider trading, Representatives and Senators will be legally prohibited from buying or selling individual stocks during their entire tenure in office.
• Congressional Term Limits: We will introduce a constitutional amendment establishing maximum terms for members of Congress (e.g., a maximum cumulative total of 12 years in the House of Representatives or the Senate) to put an end to self-serving "career politicians."
• Restricting Lobby Money: We will ban all political donations from corporate Super PACs and completely outlaw any financial influence originating from foreign interest groups.

5. Society & Family: Everyday Support

Instead of engaging in divisive, media-driven culture wars surrounding gender or religion, this platform focuses heavily on protecting the family budget and our children.
• Affordable Childcare: We will introduce a permanent, robust child allowance through expanded Child Tax Credits and direct federal subsidies for local daycare centers to ease the burden on working parents.
• Protecting Online Privacy: We will enact a strict, comprehensive national data privacy law designed to actively shield children and teenagers from the predatory, addictive algorithms of major big-tech corporations.

6. Infrastructure & Mobility: The $2,000 Private AI-Car & Ownership Freedom

The Silicon Valley elite and mega-corporations are attempting to force Americans into a permanent subscription model, aiming to replace private vehicle ownership with corporate-controlled robotaxi fleets. We reject this assault on personal independence.
• Defending the "Hunter-Gatherer" DNA: The human desire for self-reliance, freedom, and private property is hardcoded into our nature. A vehicle remains a private asset. The Lions Party will legally protect your right to own your vehicle.
• The Upgrade & Molecular Recycling Principle: By leveraging full AI-driven automation, highly sophisticated, safety-compliant private vehicles will be manufactured at an unprecedented consumer price point between $2,000 and $3,000.
• Ending the Trash Crisis: Used vehicles will no longer pile up in landfills. Utilizing advanced, automated recycling systems, old models will be fully disassembled into their molecular components within minutes and fed right back into the production cycle—guaranteeing affordable, state-of-the-art mobility for everyone.

7. Economy & Labor: The AI Transformation Tax for American Workers

As advanced AI systems and robotics rapidly eliminate human labor costs in manufacturing, corporate profit margins will skyrocket while 20% to 25% of the traditional workforce faces immediate operational disruption. We will not allow Big Tech to bankrupt the American middle class.
• The AI Special Levy: We will implement an automated AI Transformation Tax levied exclusively on corporate hyper-profits generated through autonomous robotic labor.
• Securing the American Worker: 100% of these revenues will be legally firewalled to protect the financial existence of displaced workers and fund immediate, large-scale, high-tech retraining programs. This is not welfare—it is a mandatory dividend paid by automation to the citizens who built this nation.

8. Education: The STEM & AI Tools Revolution

The current public school system of rote memorization is completely obsolete in an era where generative AI can instantly recall facts and solve standard formulas. We must fundamentally overhaul education to ensure American children lead the global future.
• Scrapping the Obsolete Curriculum: We will eliminate outdated testing models and replace them with a radical, future-proof curriculum starting from the very first grade.
• Next-Gen Leadership Skills: American students will be trained in critical hard sciences and strategic thinking. The new curriculum will focus heavily on quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, system design, materials science, and the elite mastery of AI command tools.

9. Fiscal Responsibility: Private Capital to Eradicate National Debt

Washington’s toxic obsession with funding the future through endless money printing and a skyrocketing national deficit is actively destroying the value of the US dollar. The Lions Party will fundamentally shift the financial burden of innovation.
• Zero Taxpayer Risk: Major breakthroughs in AI, robotics, and next-generation energy systems will be fueled exclusively by unlocking massive pipelines of private venture capital and private equity. We shift the financial risk entirely away from the state and onto private investors.
• The Path to Debt-Free Freedom: By leveraging private money as the ultimate catalyst for exponential economic growth, the United States will generate unprecedented, innovation-driven revenues. Our definitive target is to aggressively pay down the national deficit, ensuring a debt-free future for the next generation without raising a single cent in taxes for everyday working families.

10. Bureaucracy: Radical "Regulatory Sandboxes" for Tech Pioneers

American genius is being choked to death by unelected bureaucrats, slow permitting processes, and endless red tape in Washington. We will unleash the full power of American engineering by restoring absolute operational freedom.
• Establishing Innovation Freedom Zones: We will mandate the creation of regional "Regulatory Sandboxes" across the nation. Within these designated geographic zones, all bureaucratic hurdles, regulatory gridlocks, and restrictive rules for experimental testing in robotics, AI, and alternative energy will be completely suspended.
• Unleashing the Pioneers: If you want to build the future, the government will get out of your way. We will transform America into the ultimate global safe haven for hyper-growth and technological supremacy.

text:
It is good to be skeptical.

Here is something to check out:
https://t.co/vHz94cIhpG

You can examine the figures and do your own calculation if you like. The US import of Capital Goods, which is generally equipment used to produce products, is the highest it has been since the 1930s. Grok there says "the highest it has access to in those records".  I have looked deeper into it, we hit those numbers last in the 1930s.

Very very very high numbers.

At the same time, our present tax policy permits 100% tax deduction for capital goods spending. If you build a 20 billion dollar factory, then you can deduct 20 billion dollars from your revenue deferred over several years. Which basically means you can build factories in the US for free. Zero cost. Free factory. As you'd have to pay that 20 billion or whatever in income taxes otherwise from your other operations. There's no reason not to build and to build as lavishly as possible. A major corporation of whatever size would be encouraged to build something simply for the tax break.

Then we have the tariffs that locks off some markets worse than others but encourages US production where ever possible. Companies that have committed to US production have in compensation been offered tax exemption for the tariffs. Allowing them to continue existing supply chains if they are actively shifting production to the US.

Then we have an embarrassing amount of technology we haven't applied because the cheap imports made the risk and capital expense uneconomical before. The cheap labor and dumping from china was retarding US technological application. Not technological development... simply the application of it. That context removed, there is a lot of deferred new tech that hasn't been applied that will now all be applied at once.

There is the AI race. Which I'm sure everyone is bored to tears hearing anything more about but it does have multiplicative consequences.

And then we have secured the resources we need domestically or from safe trade partners. There are going to be some gun duels out there over some of it. I expect we're going to have to do something in the Congo at some point. It must be done. The estimate is five years for total network independence. We simply have to nurse the existing supply chains along for five years and then we'll be able to switch off them.

Then we have our trade partners that we hope to have profitable mutual trade amongst. They will get access to US capital markets, US technology, US consumer markets, and the resource networks that are being established. It is our hope this will be enough of an inducement for trade partners to see this arrangement as mutual and attractive.

All of this done at once. That is basically the "grand plan".

What do you think? So far, it is looking good and everything is looking easier than we feared it would be. We're feeling good about it. Many years of work left ahead. But the great fear would be a lack of traction. To grip our feet into the earth and slip falling into the mud to no purpose. That was the first great fear. We got traction and have taken off.

Now we have momentum. It will take something big to stop it now. We just have to keep moving and we'll be okay.

📅 WHAT I'M WATCHING TODAY — OCTOBER 13
A busy Tuesday for macro and earnings, with four major U.S. banks reporting alongside UnitedHealth, Johnson & Johnson and Domino's Pizza.
German inflation, U.S. housing data, the IMF's global outlook and OPEC's oil report are also in focus.
The question: Can companies continue delivering strong earnings while inflation and borrowing costs remain elevated?
🇺🇸 U.S. MACRO — ET
🔹 6:00 AM — NFIB Small Business Optimism
🔹 8:15 AM — ADP Weekly Employment Change
🔹 10:00 AM — Existing Home Sales
🔹 11:30 AM — 3-Month + 6-Month Treasury Bill Auctions
🔹 1:00 PM — Fed Barkin Speech
🔹 2:00 PM — Monthly Budget Statement
🔹 4:00 PM — Fed Collins Speech
KEY EXPECTATIONS
▪ Existing Home Sales: 3.96M expected vs 3.98M previously
▪ Small Business Optimism: 98 expected vs 98.7 previously
I'll be watching whether elevated borrowing costs continue to weigh on housing activity, business confidence and investment.
🇩🇪 GERMANY — 7:00 AM BST
September Final Inflation:
🔹 Headline CPI: 3.3% YoY expected vs 2.9% previously
🔹 Monthly CPI: +0.6% expected vs +0.2% previously
🔹 Harmonised CPI: 3.3% YoY expected vs 2.9% previously
An acceleration would complicate the ECB's policy outlook, particularly with economic growth already under pressure.
🇯🇵 JAPAN — RELEASED
🔹 Producer Prices YoY: +6.8% vs +7.6% expected
🔹 Producer Prices MoM: −0.3% vs +0.5% expected
🔹 Bank Lending YoY: +5.3% vs +5.5% expected
Softer producer inflation offers some relief on input costs, although currency weakness and energy prices remain important risks.
🇬🇧 UK — BST
🔹 BRC Retail Sales Monitor: +1.0% YoY vs +0.7% expected, previously +0.5%
🔹 4:00 AM — BoE Greene Speech
🔹 10:00 AM — UK Treasury Gilt Tender
🔹 5:00 PM — BoE Dhingra Speech
Retail sales beat expectations, but stronger nominal spending doesn't necessarily mean stronger volumes.
🌍 GLOBAL EVENTS
IMF — WORLD ECONOMIC OUTLOOK
Focus: Global growth, inflation forecasts, government debt and investment.
OPEC — MONTHLY OIL MARKET REPORT
Focus: Oil demand, production and supply expectations.
With energy prices elevated, both reports matter for inflation expectations and the wider economic outlook.
📊 EARNINGS — BEFORE THE BELL
🏦 U.S. BANKS
🔹 JPMorgan $JPM — Net interest income, trading, investment banking and credit quality.
🔹 Citigroup $C — Institutional banking, restructuring and profitability.
🔹 Wells Fargo $WFC — Lending, deposits, funding costs and credit losses.
🔹 Goldman Sachs $GS — M&A, trading and capital-market activity.
What matters: Are higher yields supporting profitability, or are rising funding costs and weaker loan demand becoming more significant?
I'll be watching management guidance and credit quality as closely as headline earnings.
🏥 HEALTHCARE
🔹 UnitedHealth $UNH — Medical costs, Medicare Advantage, Optum, margins and guidance.
🔹 Johnson & Johnson $JNJ — Innovative Medicine, MedTech growth and profitability.
$UNH is one of my main focuses today.
I want to see whether medical cost pressures are stabilising and whether management can demonstrate progress on margin recovery.
🍕 CONSUMER
🔹 Domino's Pizza $DPZ — Same-store sales, order volumes, pricing, international growth and margins.
A useful test of consumer spending: Are households maintaining demand or becoming more selective?
MY THREE MAIN FOCUSES TODAY
🏦 $JPM $GS $C $WFC — Credit quality, funding costs and investment banking activity.
🏥 $UNH — Medical cost trends, margins and signs of profitability recovery.
📊 Inflation, oil and yields — Whether elevated borrowing costs continue putting pressure on corporate investment and equity valuations.
MY TAKEAWAY
What makes today interesting is the combination of bank earnings and economic data.
The banks should tell us more about lending, funding costs and corporate activity.
Healthcare and consumer earnings offer another perspective on profitability and household demand.
That matters for the AI infrastructure trade too.
Companies are committing enormous amounts of capital to data centres, compute and power.
But strong demand alone doesn't guarantee attractive returns, particularly when financing costs remain elevated.
Macro tells us where financial conditions are heading. Earnings tell us how companies are performing within those conditions.
That's the combination I'm watching today.
Which earnings report are you watching most closely — $JPM, $UNH, $GS or another name?

WhatsApp may be one of the most under-monetised assets in big tech.

The product already has billions of users, but the opportunity isn’t simply charging consumers to send messages.

Businesses want to communicate with customers where those customers already spend their time.

Order confirmations. Delivery updates. Authentication. Offers. Customer support. Sales conversations.

WhatsApp lets them do that without asking the customer to download another app or constantly check email.

Meta charges businesses for this communication, and paid messaging has already passed a ~$2B annual revenue run-rate.

My 2030 base case is roughly $8B.

🏷️ Maruti Suzuki has mastered the art of expanding its portfolio, offering multiple models across price points and body styles to keep customers within its ecosystem. 

🏷️ But replicating this strategy is easier said than done. 

🏷️ Managing product positioning, avoiding internal cannibalisation and building volumes for every model is a challenge few OEMs have mastered.
