text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the cool morning of October 13, 1792, a modest procession formed outside the Fountain Inn in Georgetown and set out across the rough ground that would become the federal city. The streets were little more than paths cut through scrub and timber. The Potomac lay nearby, still the only reliable highway, and the site chosen for the President’s House stood on a rise that offered a long view southward toward the river. President Washington had selected the spot the year before, but he remained in Philadelphia that day, attending to the business of a government that had not yet moved.

At the construction clearing, master stonemason Collen Williamson of Scotland directed the work. A block of gray-white sandstone, cut from the quarries at Aquia Creek in Virginia and floated upriver on barges, was lowered into the southwest corner of the foundation. James Hoban, the Irish architect whose neoclassical design had been preferred to the other submissions, including one offered by Thomas Jefferson, stood with the commissioners. Freemasons conducted the ceremony in the manner of the time. Corn, wine, and oil were poured over the stone. A gavel struck it three times. Beneath it they placed a brass plate inscribed with the names of Washington, the District commissioners, Hoban, and Williamson, the date, and the closing words “Vivat Republica.”

The men who would raise the walls in the seasons that followed were a varied company of enslaved and free African Americans and immigrant craftsmen, many of them Scottish masons recruited for their skill with stone. The Aquia freestone would give the finished building its distinctive pale face, standing out against the red brick of the surrounding city. Construction stretched on for eight years. When John and Abigail Adams finally moved into the still-unfinished house in November 1800, much of the interior remained bare, and the grounds were only beginning to take shape.

The cornerstone itself, however, disappeared from view. A newspaper account published weeks later in Charleston placed it at the southwest corner, yet no one has seen it since. During the extensive rebuilding ordered by President Truman in the late 1940s and early 1950s, engineers searched the foundations with a mine detector and found nothing. Later efforts, including X-ray imaging at the time of the bicentennial, were equally fruitless. The brass plate may have been damaged or lost when British troops burned the house in 1814, or the stone may simply have been buried and overlooked as successive renovations altered the ground beneath the walls.

What remains is the house that rose from that first stone—a Virginia sandstone foundation laid by many hands in a city that barely existed, intended to give the young republic a permanent seat of government. The precise location of the original cornerstone is still unknown, yet the building it began has stood through every presidency since, altered and rebuilt, but never moved.

text:
Given Stormont’s inability to deal effectively with the urgent pressures on public services today, it is perhaps optimistic to expect it to adequately prepare for the challenges of decades to come.

But the implications of an ageing population set out by the Commissioner for Older People yesterday should serve as fair warning of the seismic changes that are inevitable.

The headline figure is that the number of over-65s is set to overtake under-16s as early as next year.

For a society traditionally associated with large families and a relatively young population, this represents a profound shift.

The report by Commissioner Siobhan Casey predicts that the pensionable population will increase by 45% by 2049, rising from almost 350,000 to more than 500,000.

By 2040, almost one in four people will be over 65, up from one in six today.

Those aged over 85 are also expected to more than double in that time, with advances in medicine driven by AI potentially extending life expectancy even longer.

The implications for the health and social care system are obvious, with more people living for longer and managing complex conditions.

Northern Ireland is projected to have the largest increase in dementia of any UK region.

But it is not just health. Almost all aspects of life will be affected, from provision of accessible housing and transport to public finances when more people are reaching state pension age than entering the working population.

Stormont, however, has yet to put in place a comprehensive strategy to prepare for these rapid demographic changes, with Ms Casey warning that the effects are already being felt in the health system and with rising poverty levels among older people.

There has been a 91% increase in food bank use by over-65s since 2019/20, the largest increase of any age group.

A larger, healthier older population can also bring great benefits to society, with many likely to continue working beyond traditional retirement ages and offer their skills and experience in both paid and unpaid roles across all spheres of life.

However, any change on this scale requires careful planning so that public services are designed and resourced for the people they serve, without passing the consequences of political failures on to future generations.

History sadly shows that inclusion in a programme for government is no guarantee of action but the Commissioner for Older People’s call for Northern Ireland’s ageing demographic to be prioritised at Stormont is appropriate.

It is long past time that our politicians devoted less energy to the divisions of the past and more to the challenges that will shape all our futures.

When cultures meet across time and distance, we discover that we share the same heartbeat. The Embassies of Mexico and Ireland in Indonesia are joining to present an extraordinary event: a celebration weaving together our ancestral traditions; Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead) and Samhain.

Although separated by thousands of miles, both celebrations spring from the same human roots. Samhain and Día de Muertos mark the end of an cycle and a time when the veil between the world of the living and the spirit world grows thinner. In both traditions, fire, candlelight, and bonfires serve as warm beacons, guiding the souls of our ancestors back home. These are not celebrations of sorrow, but acts of collective remembrance, where mourning is transformed into art, storytelling, and a celebration of life.

Bringing these traditions together in a vibrant metropolis like Jakarta carries profound symbolic meaning. 🇲🇽 and 🇮🇪 share a deep affinity in their reverence for family, the cycle of life, and the power of memory. By combining the visual craftmanship of Mexican artist Víctor Hugo Hidalgo with the rich oral storytelling tradition of Irish storyteller Colin Urwin, we offer audiences in Indonesia a unique multicultural experience celebrating the universality of the human spirit. We invite you to be part of this unforgettable encounter.
…

Ketika budaya bertemu melintasi waktu dan jarak, kita menemukan bahwa kita memiliki detak jantung yang sama. Kedutaan Besar Meksiko dan Irlandia di Indonesia bersatu untuk menghadirkan sebuah acara istimewa: perayaan yang merangkai tradisi leluhur kami, Día de Muertos (Hari Orang Mati) dan Samhain.

Meskipun terpisah oleh ribuan kilometer, kedua perayaan ini berakar pada nilai-nilai kemanusiaan yang sama. Samhain dan Día de Muertos menandai berakhirnya suatu siklus dan masa ketika tabir antara dunia orang hidup dan dunia roh menjadi semakin tipis. Dalam kedua tradisi tersebut, api, cahaya lilin, dan api unggun menjadi pelita hangat yang menuntun jiwa para leluhur untuk kembali ke rumah. Ini bukanlah perayaan kesedihan, melainkan wujud kenangan bersama, ketika duka diungkapkan melalui seni, kisah-kisah, dan perayaan kehidupan.

Mempertemukan kedua tradisi ini di kota metropolitan yang dinamis seperti Jakarta memiliki makna simbolis yang mendalam. 🇲🇽 dan 🇮🇪 memiliki kedekatan nilai dalam menghormati keluarga, siklus kehidupan, dan kekuatan kenangan. Dengan memadukan kepiawaian artistik seniman Meksiko Víctor Hugo Hidalgo dengan tradisi lisan yang kaya dari pendongeng Irlandia Colin Urwin, kami menghadirkan pengalaman multikultural yang unik bagi masyarakat Indonesia, sebuah perayaan atas universalitas jiwa manusia. Kami mengundang Anda untuk menjadi bagian dari perjumpaan yang tak terlupakan ini.
…

Cuando las culturas se encuentran a través del tiempo y la distancia, descubrimos que compartimos latidos. Las Embajadas de México e Irlanda en Indonesia nos unimos para presentar un evento extraordinario: una celebración que entrelaza nuestras tradiciones ancestrales, el Día de Muertos y el Samhain.

Ambas festividades tienen raíces humanas comunes. El Samhain y el Día de Muertos marcan el final de un ciclo y un momento en el que el velo entre el mundo de los vivos y el mundo espiritual se vuelve más delgado. En ambas tradiciones, el fuego, la luz de las velas y las hogueras se convierten en faros que guían las almas de nuestros antepasados a casa. Son expresiones de memoria colectiva, en las que el duelo se transforma en arte, relatos y celebración de vida.

Reunir estas tradiciones en una vibrante metrópoli como Yakarta tiene un profundo significado. 🇲🇽 e 🇮🇪 comparten  afinidad en su respeto por la familia, el ciclo de la vida y el poder de la memoria. Al combinar la maestría artística de Víctor Hugo Hidalgo con la rica tradición oral del cuentacuentos Colin Urwin, ofrecemos una experiencia multicultural que celebra la universalidad del espíritu humano. text:
🚨 Maro Itoje Speaks Out on St George’s Flag and English Identity

England rugby captain Maro Itoje has shared his views on the use of the St George’s flag, saying national symbols should bring people together rather than be used to exclude others. 

The 31-year-old, who also captains Saracens and the British & Irish Lions, made the comments while discussing a speech he delivered at Downing Street after meeting former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in April 2025.

Itoje said people should be proud of England and its flag, but expressed concern about those using national symbols to make others feel unwelcome.

He said the aim should be to take ownership of the England flag and celebrate St George’s Day, recognising the country’s achievements and what it continues to offer.

Itoje’s comments come amid wider debate about national identity, patriotism and the use of England flags in communities across the country.

Sir Keir Starmer has also previously called for the flag to represent everyone in England, highlighting the country’s diversity and shared values.

text:
The following graph shows that the number of chips produced in China is steadily increasing. Ever since the U.S. government banned NVIDIA from selling its latest-generation high-performance processors to China four years ago, accelerating domestic chip production has become a national priority. Rather than settling for older NVIDIA chips, Beijing appears committed to reducing its dependence on the leading chip manufacturer in the long term. Yet despite commendable efforts, such a goal remains a long way off.

Although Chinese companies such as Huawei, Baidu, and Alibaba have helped domestic chip production nearly double compared to last year, supply still falls short of meeting demand. According to the @FT , domestic supply is expected to reach up to 3.5 million AI chips this year. However, with total demand well over 5 million, domestic supply is insufficient to meet demand. To meet domestic demand, Chinese technology companies are reported to have ordered well over 1 million NVIDIA chips for gaming and workstations. Even though these chips offer lower performance than leading Chinese dedicated AI chips, such as Huawei's flagship Ascend 910C, they can be repurposed and used for the compute-intensive prefill phase.

In addition, the release of agentic AI tools—provided by companies such as Huawei, Tencent, and Alibaba, which process data over an extended period—is said to have significantly increased the number of tokens generated. Such a development inevitably leads to a greater demand for chips. Although Alibaba unveiled its Zhenwu V900 last month—possibly the most powerful Chinese chip currently available—and Huawei is set to introduce its first chip dedicated to training, the Ascend 960D, in the first quarter of next year, these chips still do not match the performance of NVIDIA chips, despite noticeable performance gains. To compensate for this shortfall, Chinese tech companies must connect a larger number of chips using network technologies, which, among other factors, explains the high demand. This limited capacity is said to have prompted Tencent to lease data centers from Oracle in Southeast Asia, which house well over 100,000 chips, including some from the Blackwell generation (B300).

Although the number of chips produced in China is expected to continue growing in the coming years, supply remains insufficient to meet the country’s ambitions. Two years after Beijing ordered domestic technology companies to reduce their reliance on NVIDIA chips, there is consensus across the industry—according to Eddi Wu, CEO of Alibaba—that the current shortage of computing power for AI will not be resolved until at least 2030.

text:
Ostris launches AI-Toolkit for LoRA model training

Good Tuesday morning, tech enthusiasts! Are you ready to dive into the latest in AI content generation? Today’s news is all about a new tool from Ostris that promises to simplify your workflow. But before we get too excited, let's ask ourselves: Is this really going to change how you work with LoRA models and content creation?
What’s New in AI-Toolkit

Ostris has rolled out an updated version of their AI-Toolkit, now featuring a dedicated page for generating images, videos, and even music. This new addition supports popular open-source models like Krea 2, Flux 1/2, Qwen Image 2512, SDXL, MiniMax H3, and more. The toolkit aims to streamline the process of training LoRA models and generating content within a single interface.
Key Features
Content Generation
AI-Toolkit now offers a wide range of models for generating various types of media directly from its interface. This means no more switching between different tools or interfaces to achieve your creative goals.
Quantization Methods
Users can take advantage of several quantization methods, including bf16, int8 convrot, fp8, qfp8, and nvfp4. These options provide greater control over performance and customization.
LoRA Integration
The toolkit allows for merging LoRA with models to enhance customization further. This feature is particularly useful for those who want more tailored results from their content generation processes.
How It Works

AI-Toolkit operates using an embedded portable version of Python along with PyTorch Triton and other necessary components. The entire system runs from a single .bat file, which launches the local server and alerts users to updates as they become available.
Installation Steps
1. Download AI-Toolkit-Easy-Install: Extract `AI-Toolkit-Easy-Install.bat` into a new folder.
2. Run Installer: Execute the batch file but avoid running it as an administrator or in system folders like Program Files.
3. Update Regularly: Use `Update-AI-Toolkit` for easy updates.
Limitations and Caveats

While AI-Toolkit offers convenience, it’s still in its early stages with limited settings and performance issues compared to established tools like ComfyUI. For instance, generating a 1024x1024 image using Krea 2 takes around 13 seconds on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, whereas ComfyUI manages it in just 5 seconds at bf16 precision.

Generating larger images (2048x2048) can take over a minute or even crash the system. This means that if you need full flexibility and robust performance, AI-Toolkit might not be your best option yet.
Why Should You Care?

If you’re looking for an easier way to train LoRA models and generate content without jumping between interfaces, AI-Toolkit could be worth checking out. However, if you require the full flexibility of ComfyUI, this new addition may not meet your needs just yet.
Installation Details
The installation process is straightforward thanks to the `AI-Toolkit-Easy-Install` script. It handles dependencies like Git, Node.js, FFmpeg, Python, PyTorch Triton, and more without requiring system Python or virtual environments. Simply extract the installer into a new folder and run it.
Fine Print

While AI-Toolkit offers an easy-to-use interface for generating content with LoRA models, it’s important to note that this is still an early alpha version. Performance issues and limited settings are expected as Ostris continues to develop and refine the toolkit.
Excluded Identifiers
The installer avoids system folders like Program Files and does not require running as an administrator or in system directories. This ensures a portable installation without interfering with other software on your machine.
What It Doesn’t Prove

This announcement doesn't prove that AI-Toolkit will replace ComfyUI anytime soon. While it simplifies the process of content generation, established tools like ComfyUI still offer more flexibility and robust performance for those who need them.
Community Feedback
What do you think? Is this something that could streamline your workflow or are you sticking with ComfyUI for now?

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the morning of October 13, 1845, men across the Republic of Texas rode or walked to the nearest polling place and cast ballots that would end nine years of independence. The returns left almost no room for argument: roughly 7,664 votes for annexation to the United States, only about 430 against. They approved a new state constitution by a nearly identical margin. In a young country of scattered farms, dusty towns, and contested frontiers, the people had spoken with rare clarity.

The path to that day had never been certain. Texas had broken free of Mexico in 1836 at San Jacinto, and from the beginning most of its settlers had wanted union with the United States. Yet Washington held back. Admitting another slaveholding state threatened the balance of power in Congress. Mexico refused to recognize Texas independence and still claimed the territory. Treaties failed. Politics stalled. Sam Houston, the hero of independence and twice president of the republic, played a careful game—publicly favoring annexation while using the threat of closer ties with Britain and France to pressure the United States. His successor, Anson Jones, continued the delicate diplomacy. For years it seemed the offer might never come, or might come on terms Texas could not accept.

Then, in the final weeks of the Tyler administration, Congress acted. A joint resolution offering annexation passed the Senate by the narrowest of margins—after an initial tie, one senator changed his vote to make it 27 to 25. The House concurred. Tyler signed it on March 1, 1845, as one of his last official acts. Texas would keep its public lands and its debts, cede its forts and customs houses, and could, in theory, divide into additional states later. The United States would handle the boundary questions with Mexico.

In Austin that summer a convention of elected delegates met on the Fourth of July. Thomas Jefferson Rusk, a veteran of the revolution, was chosen president. The delegates—many originally from Tennessee, Virginia, Georgia, and Kentucky—considered both the American offer and a last-minute Mexican proposal that promised recognition only if Texas stayed independent. They rejected Mexico and accepted the United States by a vote of 55 to 1. The single no came from Richard Bache of Galveston, grandson of Benjamin Franklin. The convention then drafted a state constitution and sent both the ordinance and the constitution to the people.

On October 13 the voters settled the matter. In county after county the majorities were lopsided. The decision carried real risk. Mexico still regarded Texas as its own. The boundary—whether the Nueces or the Rio Grande—remained unsettled. Slavery would now be protected under the U.S. Constitution, deepening the sectional divide. Yet for most Texans the advantages outweighed the dangers: protection by the American army and navy, access to markets, a share in the expanding republic, and an end to the uncertainty of a small, indebted nation standing alone.

Congress accepted the constitution later that fall. On December 29, 1845, President James K. Polk signed the final resolution admitting Texas as the 28th state. The formal transfer of government came in February 1846, when Governor J. Pinckney Henderson took the oath and the Lone Star flag came down. The boundary dispute with Mexico did not disappear. Within months it helped trigger the Mexican-American War, a conflict that would add vast new territory to the United States and, in time, intensify the arguments over slavery that would tear the Union apart fifteen years later.

Nothing about the outcome had been inevitable. A single senator’s change of vote, a different decision by the Austin convention, a closer popular tally, or stronger resistance from Mexico could have altered the course. Instead, on that October day, the people of Texas chose the Union, and the map of North America changed with them.

text:
Shinkafi thanks Zamfara residents for massive Welcome, says ADC poised for victory

The African Democratic Congress governorship candidate in Zamfara State, Bilyaminu Yusuf Shinkafi, has expressed appreciation to the people of the state for the massive reception accorded him during his visit to Gusau last week for the inauguration of the party’s presidential and governorship campaign offices.

Shinkafi described the overwhelming show of support and solidarity as a clear indication of the people’s desire for a new direction in the state, expressing confidence that the ADC would secure victory in the forthcoming elections, by God’s grace.

In a statement signed on Monday, the governorship candidate thanked supporters, party members, youths, women and other residents who turned out to welcome him, saying their enthusiasm had strengthened his determination to offer purposeful leadership.

He said, “The love shown to us by the good people of Zamfara State is massive. We are encouraged by the support and confidence they have demonstrated in our movement.

“We are coasting to victory by the grace of God, and nobody can stop the plans of God for Zamfara State.”

Shinkafi urged residents to sustain the momentum by mobilising more supporters and strengthening the party’s grassroots structures across the 14 local government areas of the state.

He called on the electorate to unite behind the ADC to rescue Zamfara from what he described as the All Progressives Congress-led administration’s style of governance, which he accused of concentrating power in the hands of a few individuals.

According to him, governance should be driven by consultation, accountability, inclusiveness and a commitment to improving the welfare of the people, rather than the decisions of a single individual.

“The government belongs to the people, and the people must have a voice in how they are governed. Running a state as a one-man show is not the beauty of democracy or good governance,” he said.

The ADC candidate urged party faithful and supporters to remain peaceful, law-abiding and committed to democratic participation as political activities gather momentum ahead of the elections.

He also called on residents to continue spreading the party’s message of change and mobilising eligible voters to participate actively in the democratic process.

Shinkafi reaffirmed his commitment to providing responsive leadership, insisting that the people of Zamfara deserved an administration that would listen to their concerns, prioritise their welfare and work towards a safer and more prosperous state.

He expressed optimism that sustained grassroots mobilisation and the collective determination of the people would strengthen the ADC’s chances in the forthcoming governorship election.

text:
There is a fundamental problem with the emerging negotiating framework for Ukraine: it spends too much time discussing what Russia might receive, and not enough time confronting what Russia has already done.

Russia started this war by invading a sovereign country. Russian forces occupied Ukrainian cities, struck residential areas and civilian infrastructure, and deported civilians and children. In 2022, the European Parliament recognized Russia as a state sponsor of terrorism and as a state using means of terrorism, citing deliberate attacks on civilians and war crimes.

The human cost is still rising. In the first eight months of 2026 alone, the UN confirmed 2,222 civilians killed and 13,058 injured in Ukraine. Civilian casualties are increasing, while Russian missiles, drones and aerial bombs continue to hit cities far from the front line.

And yet the proposals now being discussed reportedly include a ceasefire along the current front line, continued de facto Russian control over occupied Ukrainian territory, possible sanctions relief, and even renewed energy cooperation with Russia.

So what exactly is Russia supposed to learn from this?

That it can launch the largest war in Europe in decades, seize another country’s territory, endure several years of sanctions, and still retain a path back to economic normalization?

Ukraine needs peace. It needs credible security guarantees. But any serious peace framework must also preserve a basic principle: military aggression cannot become a successful way to gain territory, force political concessions, and eventually return to business as usual.

Otherwise, the outcome is deeply distorted. Russia starts the war. Ukraine pays in lives, territory and destruction. International partners finance much of the reconstruction. And Moscow is eventually offered sanctions relief and renewed economic ties.

Any discussion about peace should therefore begin with accountability and with the consequences for the state that started this war.

text:
Big Mom Was the Most Successful Yonko of All Time And It’s Not Just About Strength

People love debating which Yonko was the strongest, but strength is only one part of being an Emperor. If we judge the Yonko by longevity, territorial control, political influence, intelligence, wealth, administration, scientific advancement, and individual power, Charlotte Linlin has a legitimate argument for being the most successful Yonko in history.

Big Mom wasn’t simply a powerful pirate. She built an empire.

1. Longevity: An Empire That Survived for Decades

Big Mom was already a major force in the pirate world during the era of Rocks D. Xebec, Whitebeard, Shiki, and Roger. Unlike many pirates whose influence peaked for a relatively short period, Linlin maintained her position as one of the world’s dominant powers across multiple eras.

Her crew and empire were built over decades, with her children, officers, and political alliances forming an increasingly elaborate system of control.

This wasn’t a temporary reign built on one major victory. It was a long-standing institution that continued to expand and operate for generations.

Big Mom didn’t just survive the changing eras of piracy. She built an empire that outlasted most of her contemporaries.

2. Territory: The Most Elaborate Pirate Empire

Big Mom’s territorial influence was extraordinary.

Totto Land consisted of an archipelago of 35 islands, each contributing to the operation of her empire. These weren’t simply islands where her flag happened to fly. They were integrated into a larger political and economic system, with her children occupying positions of authority and her subordinates maintaining influence beyond her central territory.

Her control also extended to strategically important locations. Fish-Man Island, for example, came under her protection after Whitebeard’s death, allowing her to establish influence over a crucial route connecting the first half of the Grand Line to the New World.

Her reach wasn’t limited to direct territorial occupation, either. Through subordinates such as Tamago and Pekoms, Big Mom could project her authority beyond Totto Land and collect tribute from affiliated territories.

Then there’s her marriage strategy. By marrying her children into other families and organisations, she could establish connections that went beyond conventional pirate alliances.

Compare this with the other Emperors:

* Whitebeard had an enormous network of affiliated islands and crews, with his death triggering a scramble for his former territories.
* Kaido concentrated much of his power around Wano, using weapons production and SMILE manufacturing to strengthen his military position.
* Shanks maintained influence through his reputation, crew, and relationships with other pirates, though the full extent of his territory remains unclear.
* Blackbeard expanded rapidly, but his empire was still developing compared with the established systems of the older Emperors.
* Luffy gained territories and numerous allied crews, but his influence largely operates through informal allegiance rather than a centrally administered empire.

The distinction is that Big Mom combined territorial control with an organised political structure.

3. Intelligence and Surveillance: An Empire That Was Difficult to Infiltrate

Big Mom’s intelligence network was another major advantage.

Her Homies could perform surveillance throughout Totto Land, giving her forces a significant advantage in monitoring movement and responding to threats.

Napoleon, her special Homie created from her own soul, could communicate with other Homies and relay information. Charlotte Brûlée’s Mirror-Mirror Fruit also provided access to the Mirror World, creating additional opportunities for surveillance and movement.

Her territory was further protected by territorial sea slugs that detected approaching ships and transmitted warning signals.

This meant that Totto Land wasn’t simply defended by powerful fighters. It was supported by an interconnected surveillance and warning system.

Other Yonko certainly had intelligence networks of their own, but Big Mom’s combination of Devil Fruit abilities, Homies, and territorial security gave her empire a distinctive advantage.

She built a system designed to detect threats before they could reach the heart of her empire.

4. Wealth: A Self-Sustaining Power Base

A Yonko’s strength isn’t determined by combat ability alone. Resources matter.

Big Mom controlled a vast collection of islands, maintained an extensive organisation, collected tribute, and possessed the infrastructure necessary to sustain a large crew and an entire population.

Her control over territories provided access to food, labour, materials, and other resources. Her political relationships also created opportunities to obtain resources through arrangements that ordinary pirate crews could not easily establish.

While the exact wealth of the Yonko has never been comprehensively ranked, Big Mom’s territorial system strongly suggests an enormous economic base.

The important distinction is that she didn’t rely solely on plunder. She established a system through which her empire could continuously generate resources.

5. Bureaucracy: Big Mom Built a Government, Not Just a Crew

This is arguably one of the most underrated aspects of her empire.

Most pirate crews operate around a captain, a hierarchy of officers, and subordinate members. Big Mom went much further.

Her children occupied positions of authority across different islands, effectively serving as regional administrators. Perospero, Katakuri, Smoothie, Cracker, Oven, Daifuku, and others all contributed to the functioning of her larger organisation.

She also delegated specific responsibilities to specialised members of her crew. Her Homies helped administer Totto Land’s lifespan collection system, while subordinate officers handled diplomatic and territorial matters.

Even her military organisation demonstrated a degree of standardisation. The numbered Tartes served as uniform naval vessels, giving her forces a recognisable and organised fleet.

The point isn’t that Big Mom’s empire was perfectly efficient or comparable in every respect to the World Government. It’s that she established layers of administration, delegated authority, and maintained a political structure that extended beyond her immediate presence.

Big Mom’s empire could function as a system because she didn’t personally have to handle every responsibility herself.

6. Scientific Advancement: More Than Military Production

Kaido invested heavily in artificial Zoan fruits through Caesar Clown and the SMILE production operation. Big Mom pursued a different set of ambitions.

Her long-term goal was to create a family in which every race could coexist in Totto Land. This was partly driven by her desire to build a world without racial exclusion, although her methods of ruling were deeply oppressive.

Nevertheless, the ambition had strategic implications.

By bringing members of different races into her territory, Big Mom gained access to biological diversity and potentially valuable racial abilities. The Three-Eye Tribe’s potential to decipher Poneglyphs, for instance, made Charlotte Pudding strategically important to her ambitions.

She also pursued gigantification research through Caesar Clown, hoping to make her family grow to the size of Giants. Her interest wasn’t merely cosmetic: Giants were renowned for their physical power, and an army of Giant-sized family members would have significantly strengthened her military position.

Finally, her planned alliance with Germa 66 offered access to advanced military science and technology. The broader scientific ambitions associated with her dealings with Caesar and Germa demonstrated that she understood the value of technological advancement.

Not every project succeeded, but her empire was pursuing multiple avenues of development rather than relying exclusively on conventional military strength.

7. Military Strength: An Emperor Who Could Fight at the Highest Level

None of this matters if Big Mom cannot defend what she has built.

Fortunately, she was one of the most formidable individual fighters in the series.

Her natural physical strength and extraordinary durability made her exceptionally difficult to damage. Her mastery of Haki, combined with the versatility of the Soru Soru no Mi, gave her a wide range of offensive and defensive options.

She could create powerful weapons from her own soul, command elemental Homies such as Prometheus and Zeus, manipulate the souls of others under the appropriate conditions, and sacrifice her own lifespan to increase her power.

Her ability to use her own soul to repair herself also made her unusually difficult to put down.

Her performance against Kaido on the rooftop of Onigashima further demonstrated that she belonged in the highest tier of individual combatants. The two fought for an extended period before forming their alliance, and the story consistently presented them as monsters of comparable standing.

Her defeat on Wano does not erase that reputation. Law’s ability to bypass conventional defences and Kid’s overwhelming attacks created a combination of abilities that made the fight particularly difficult for her.

Big Mom was not invincible, but she possessed the individual strength necessary to rule as a Yonko.

And that is the crucial point: she combined top-tier personal power with one of the most elaborate empires in the world.

Conclusion: The Most Complete Yonko

Big Mom’s greatest achievement wasn’t simply becoming one of the Four Emperors. It was building a political, economic, military, and social system around her power.

She had longevity, extensive territory, political connections, a surveillance network, a large and organised military, scientific ambitions, and enough personal strength to defend her position against other top-tier pirates.

Whitebeard may have had a more admirable relationship with his family. Shanks may possess greater Haki. Kaido may have been the more straightforward military threat. Other Emperors may surpass her in particular categories.

But when the discussion shifts from who was the strongest? to who built the most comprehensive pirate empire?, Big Mom deserves to be at the centre of the conversation.

She wasn’t merely an Emperor who happened to control territory. She was an Emperor who built an entire civilisation around her power.

And if we’re judging Yonko success by the totality of what they achieved, rather than just their ability to win a one-on-one fight, Charlotte Linlin has one of the strongest cases for being the most successful Yonko of all time.

🚀 BNB Outlook 2026–2027: Can BNB Chain Become the Next Major Crypto Growth Story?

An In-Depth Analysis of BNB, Token Burns, ETF Adoption, Stablecoins, RWA, and Future Price Scenarios

📅 October 13, 2026
✍️ AI Infra Crypto
⏳ Outlook: 3–12 Months

🔎 1. THE BIG PICTURE: IS BNB PREPARING FOR ANOTHER GROWTH CYCLE?

BNB is becoming one of the more interesting large-cap cryptocurrencies to follow as the market navigates another period of uncertainty.

While Bitcoin continues to dominate broader market sentiment, BNB has been building a different long-term narrative.

Several developments deserve attention:

🔥 Token burns continue to reduce BNB supply.

🏦 Institutional investors can now access BNB through a US-listed investment product.

🌐 BNB Chain remains one of the most active blockchain ecosystems.

💰 Stablecoins and real-world asset tokenization are creating new opportunities.

⚡ Major infrastructure upgrades are targeting faster and more efficient blockchain transactions.

But here's the question I keep coming back to:

Can all these developments create enough real demand to push BNB into another sustained bullish cycle?

I think BNB has several structural advantages. However, strong technology and declining token supply alone do not guarantee higher prices.

Real demand, liquidity, investor confidence, and market conditions will ultimately determine what happens next.

Let's look at the numbers.

📊 2. BNB MARKET SNAPSHOT

As of the October 13, 2026 research snapshot, BNB's key market indicators were approximately:

💰 Price: $742

🌍 Market Capitalization: $98.8 billion

🪙 Circulating Supply: 133.16 million BNB

🏆 Market Ranking: #4

📈 Derivatives Open Interest: $2.07 billion

🔝 Historical All-Time High: $1,369.99

📉 Distance from ATH: Around 46% below the peak

📉 Seven-Day Price Performance: -5.3%

Source: CoinGecko and derivatives market data.

These figures are historical reference values from October 13 and may change.

What stands out?

Despite considerable ecosystem development, BNB remains well below its previous all-time high.

That does not automatically mean BNB is undervalued.

However, it creates an interesting situation.

BNB's technology, institutional access, and ecosystem have continued evolving while the token's market performance has remained under pressure.

The key question is whether that gap will eventually close through stronger prices or whether investors are correctly pricing in important risks.

🌐 3. BNB CHAIN FUNDAMENTALS: LARGE SCALE, MIXED MOMENTUM

To understand BNB's future, we need to look beyond the token price.

BNB Chain's actual economic activity is one of the most important factors to evaluate.

According to the DeFiLlama snapshot referenced for October 13:

💎 Total Value Locked: Approximately $5.41 billion

💵 Stablecoin Market Capitalization: Approximately $13.31 billion

🏛️ RWA Active AUM: Approximately $4.86 billion

🔄 Daily Transactions: Approximately 15.24 million

👥 Daily Active Addresses: Approximately 2.06 million

📊 24-Hour DEX Trading Volume: Approximately $750 million

📉 Seven-Day DEX Volume: Approximately $4.54 billion

🔻 Weekly DEX Volume Change: -32.65%

⛽ Daily Network Fees: Approximately $409,392

Source: DeFiLlama.

These indicators measure different aspects of the ecosystem and should not be added together.

🟢 The positive side

BNB Chain continues to process substantial transaction activity.

Its stablecoin ecosystem is particularly important because stablecoins increasingly support real economic use cases.

These include payments, trading, lending, cross-border transfers, and on-chain settlement.

A large stablecoin base can help attract developers, financial applications, and liquidity providers.

🔴 The concerning side

The recent decline in DEX trading volume suggests that speculative activity has cooled.

Another important distinction is that high transaction counts do not necessarily translate into high network revenue.

Similarly, TVL measured in US dollars can change because of asset price movements rather than actual capital flows.

My assessment

I think BNB Chain has already established significant scale.

The next challenge is showing consistent growth in economic activity rather than simply maintaining high transaction numbers.

Over the coming months, I would focus on three indicators:

• Stablecoin supply growth.

• Sustained DEX trading activity.

• Protocol revenue and genuine user retention.

If these indicators improve together, the fundamental outlook for BNB becomes considerably more convincing.

🏦 4. INSTITUTIONAL ADOPTION: THE BNB ETF FACTOR

One of the most important BNB developments in 2026 was the introduction of a US-listed BNB investment product.

On May 28, 2026, VanEck launched VBNB on Nasdaq, providing exchange-traded exposure to BNB.

This changes the institutional narrative.

The question is no longer simply whether investors can gain exposure through a traditional investment structure.

The more important question is:

How much institutional capital will actually move into BNB?

Key VBNB figures

As of October 9, 2026, the fund reported approximately:

💰 Net Assets: $96.67 million

🪙 BNB Holdings: 130,843 BNB

📊 Annual Management Fee: 0.39%

🔒 Reported Staking Allocation: 95.91%

Source: VanEck.

These figures are historical and should be checked against the latest fund disclosures.

Why does this matter?

Institutional investment products can reduce operational barriers associated with direct token ownership.

They also make cryptocurrency exposure more accessible to traditional financial investors.

However, there's an important distinction.

An increase in a fund's assets under management does not always mean an equivalent amount of new capital entered the fund.

Asset values can change because of price movements, share creation, and redemptions.

At the time of the referenced disclosure, VBNB's BNB holdings represented only around 0.1% of circulating supply.

That means the product remained relatively small compared with BNB's overall market.

My perspective

I view ETF adoption as a potentially important long-term catalyst.

But I would not use the existence of an ETF alone as a reason to expect a major rally.

What matters is whether fund holdings and net investor demand continue growing over time.

🔥 5. BNB TOKEN BURNS: DOES DECREASING SUPPLY GUARANTEE HIGHER PRICES?

BNB has a token supply reduction mechanism that distinguishes it from many other Layer 1 cryptocurrencies.

The long-term objective of BNB Auto-Burn is to reduce the total token supply toward 100 million BNB.

Let's examine the recent burn history.

🔥 34th Quarterly Burn

📅 January 15, 2026

🪙 BNB Burned: 1,371,804

💰 Estimated Value: $1.28 billion

🔥 35th Quarterly Burn

📅 April 15, 2026

🪙 BNB Burned: 1,569,307

💰 Estimated Value: $1.02 billion

🔥 36th Quarterly Burn

📅 July 15, 2026

🪙 BNB Burned: 1,615,828

💰 Estimated Value: $932 million

🔥 37th Quarterly Burn

📅 Expected during October 2026

🪙 BNB Burned: Not yet confirmed in this research snapshot.

Across the first three quarterly burns of 2026, approximately 4.56 million BNB were permanently removed from supply.

BNB also uses BEP-95, which burns a portion of network transaction fees.

Why token burns matter

All else being equal, reducing available supply can support token scarcity.

However, scarcity only translates into higher prices when demand remains stable or increases.

There is another important point.

A scheduled token burn is not equivalent to purchasing the same number of tokens on the open market.

Therefore, the headline dollar value of a burn should not automatically be interpreted as new buying pressure.

My take

BNB's supply reduction mechanism provides a structural advantage.

But investors should evaluate it alongside real token demand.

Burns reduce supply. Adoption creates potential demand. Both matter.

⚡ 6. BNB CHAIN INFRASTRUCTURE: THE TECHNOLOGY STORY

This is one of the areas I find most interesting.

BNB Chain is increasingly positioning itself as infrastructure for high-volume digital financial activity.

During 2026, several upgrades focused on increasing throughput, reducing latency, and improving network efficiency.

January 2026: Fermi Hard Fork

The Fermi upgrade reduced block time from approximately 750 milliseconds to 450 milliseconds.

This supports faster transaction processing and improves the experience for applications requiring frequent interactions.

Mid-2026: Performance Optimization

BNB Chain reported benchmark throughput of approximately 5,200 transactions per second, with memory finality around 650 milliseconds.

These are technical performance measurements, not guaranteed continuous production throughput.

August–September 2026: Pasteur Upgrade

The Pasteur upgrade improved block construction and execution efficiency.

BNB Chain reported approximately 28% more gas processed per block on average under its measured mainnet workload.

Looking ahead: Next-Generation Layer 1

BNB Chain's development roadmap includes ambitious technical objectives.

These include:

⚡ Higher throughput.

⏱️ Lower transaction latency.

💳 Improved infrastructure for stablecoin payments.

🏦 Greater capacity for tokenized financial markets.

🤖 Support for data-intensive and automated applications.

The longer-term architecture has referenced performance targets above 100,000 TPS.

However, those targets should be considered development objectives until verified in production.

What this means for BNB

I see the infrastructure upgrades as potentially important for adoption.

But higher TPS alone does not create token value.

The real test will be whether faster and cheaper infrastructure attracts valuable applications, sustainable liquidity, and long-term users.

🏛️ 7. RWA: COULD TOKENIZATION BECOME BNB CHAIN'S NEXT GROWTH ENGINE?

Real-world asset tokenization is becoming an increasingly important topic in the blockchain industry.

The concept involves representing traditional assets through blockchain-based tokens.

Examples include:

• Government bonds.

• Investment funds.

• Equities.

• Money market instruments.

• Other eligible financial assets.

BNB Chain is seeking a larger role in this market.

According to the Binance Research figures referenced in September 2026:

🌍 The tokenized equities market exceeded $3 billion.

🟡 BNB Chain represented approximately $1 billion under the report's methodology.

📊 Its estimated market share was around 34%.

👥 Approximately 1.8 million addresses held relevant tokenized assets.

These figures suggest that BNB Chain has become a meaningful participant in this developing sector.

But we need to be careful when interpreting the data.

Tokenized value is not the same as trading demand

A blockchain can host a large amount of tokenized assets without generating significant trading fees.

Therefore, asset value, trading volume, liquidity, and network revenue should be evaluated separately.

What would make the RWA narrative stronger?

I would look for:

✅ More legitimate financial institutions issuing tokenized products.

✅ Growing secondary-market liquidity.

✅ Increasing stablecoin settlement activity.

✅ Tokenized assets being integrated into permitted lending and collateral systems.

✅ Clearer regulatory frameworks for institutional participation.

My view

I think RWA has the potential to become a more sustainable driver of blockchain usage than short-term memecoin speculation.

However, investors must still ask whether the resulting activity translates into increased demand for BNB itself.

That's the connection I would want to see confirmed.

📉 8. TECHNICAL OUTLOOK: IMPORTANT BNB PRICE LEVELS

BNB experienced selling pressure during early October after trading near the $800 region.

The following levels are useful areas to monitor.

They are not guaranteed support or resistance.

🟢 Potential support areas

📍 $718–$725

A recent lower-price area where buying activity may be worth watching.

📍 $700

A major psychological threshold.

A sustained move below this region could increase downside risk.

🟡 Recovery and consolidation area

📍 $750–$770

A zone that could help indicate whether short-term momentum is improving.

🔴 Potential resistance areas

📍 $786–$807

A recent upper trading area.

A sustained breakout supported by strong spot volume would improve the technical picture.

📍 $850–$900

A possible upside zone if BNB establishes a stronger recovery.

📍 $1,000

A major psychological milestone.

At a circulating supply of approximately 133 million BNB, a $1,000 token price would imply a market capitalization of roughly $133 billion.

That would require significant investor demand.

What I would watch

I would become more constructive if BNB reclaimed the $786–$807 region while maintaining stronger performance against Bitcoin.

I would also prefer to see spot trading volume improving rather than a rally driven primarily by leveraged derivatives.

📅 9. IMPORTANT CATALYSTS FOR LATE 2026 AND EARLY 2027

Several developments deserve close attention.

October 2026: US Inflation Data

US macroeconomic indicators, including CPI, can influence risk appetite and expectations for monetary policy.

A change in broader market liquidity conditions could significantly affect cryptocurrency prices.

October 2026: BNB Quarterly Burn

The anticipated 37th BNB burn is another supply-related event to monitor.

However, investors should distinguish the actual supply reduction from short-term speculation around the announcement.

Late October 2026: Tokenized Stocks Ecosystem Developments

BNB Chain has been supporting development activity around tokenized equities.

Announcements about projects, infrastructure, and adoption could provide insights into ecosystem progress.

Q4 2026: Payment Infrastructure Improvements

BNB Chain's planned payment-related upgrades could improve transaction handling and the user experience for stablecoin applications.

Late 2026: Next-Generation Testnet Development

Technical progress toward the next-generation architecture could become an important milestone.

Early 2027: Further Mainnet Development

The roadmap includes ambitions for a more advanced network architecture.

These are planned milestones rather than confirmed outcomes.

My assessment

Not every catalyst will have the same impact.

A token burn might attract short-term attention.

But sustained institutional inflows or large-scale stablecoin adoption could have more meaningful long-term implications.

I would focus more on measurable economic outcomes than announcement headlines.

🎯 10. BNB PRICE OUTLOOK: THREE POSSIBLE SCENARIOS

Rather than predicting one exact future price, I prefer to examine different scenarios.

These are illustrative ranges based on market structure and potential developments.

They are not statistically calculated price forecasts.

🟢 BULLISH SCENARIO: $850–$1,000

Potential horizon: 6–12 months.

This scenario becomes more plausible if several positive factors align.

Bitcoin and the broader crypto market recover.

Institutional BNB exposure increases.

Stablecoin liquidity and DeFi activity improve.

BNB Chain demonstrates sustained progress in RWA adoption.

And BNB breaks above its recent resistance region with stronger spot demand.

If these developments occur together, BNB could potentially approach the $850–$1,000 range.

However, a move toward $1,000 would require considerable market demand.

Infrastructure improvements and token burns alone would not be sufficient justification.

🟡 NEUTRAL SCENARIO: $700–$850

Potential horizon: 3–6 months.

In this scenario, BNB Chain continues to operate at significant scale.

However, ecosystem growth remains uneven.

Institutional adoption develops gradually, and the broader cryptocurrency market struggles to establish a strong trend.

BNB could consolidate within a relatively wide trading range while investors wait for clearer economic signals.

This would not necessarily invalidate the long-term thesis.

But it could limit near-term price performance.

🔴 BEARISH SCENARIO: $550–$700

Potential horizon: 3–12 months.

This scenario becomes more relevant if Bitcoin weakens significantly and liquidity deteriorates.

Additional concerns could include:

📉 Continued declines in BNB Chain trading activity.

💸 Weakening DeFi liquidity.

🏦 Disappointing institutional demand.

⚠️ Major cybersecurity incidents.

⚖️ Unexpected regulatory developments.

🌐 Increased competition from other blockchains.

A sustained breakdown below $700 would make downside risk more important.

During a severe market-wide selloff, prices could move below the illustrative range.

⚠️ 11. FIVE RISKS THAT COULD CHANGE THE BNB OUTLOOK

1. Broader Market Risk

BNB remains highly exposed to cryptocurrency market sentiment.

A major Bitcoin correction could trigger significant selling pressure across altcoins, including BNB.

2. Ecosystem Concentration

BNB has strong historical and commercial links with Binance.

Regulatory or operational developments affecting Binance can influence how investors perceive BNB.

3. Decentralization Trade-Offs

BNB Smart Chain uses a Proof of Staked Authority architecture with a relatively limited validator structure.

Investors should evaluate the trade-offs between network performance and decentralization.

4. Smart Contract and Security Risk

DeFi applications remain vulnerable to smart contract exploits, oracle failures, bridge attacks, and private-key compromises.

A security incident at an application does not necessarily mean the underlying blockchain protocol has failed.

5. Competition

BNB Chain faces competition from Ethereum, Solana, Base, Tron, and other networks.

Fast and inexpensive transactions are important advantages, but they are not unique.

Maintaining liquidity, developer activity, and sustainable financial applications will remain essential.

📊 12. SIX INDICATORS I WOULD MONITOR EVERY WEEK

If I were tracking BNB closely over the next several months, these would be my priorities.

📈 1. BNB/BTC Relative Strength

Sources: CoinGecko and TradingView.

Key question: Is BNB outperforming Bitcoin, or simply following the wider market?

⚡ 2. Open Interest and Funding Rates

Source: CoinGlass.

Key question: Is the market becoming overly leveraged?

Looking at the bigger picture, I believe BNB has a credible long-term development narrative.

It combines several characteristics that relatively few blockchain assets offer at the same time.

✅ A large existing blockchain ecosystem.

My perspective

I remain cautiously constructive on BNB's longer-term fundamentals.

However, I would want to see stronger confirmation before assuming a major price breakout.

For me, three questions matter most.

First: Can institutional demand expand?

ETF availability is important, but sustained capital allocation matters more.

Second: Can BNB Chain attract more real economic activity?

Stablecoin settlements, tokenized assets, DeFi liquidity, and application revenue will be important indicators.

Third: Can BNB regain market strength?

A convincing recovery should be supported by spot demand, improving network fundamentals, and relative strength against Bitcoin.

If these conditions align, BNB could become one of the more interesting large-cap cryptocurrencies in the next stage of the market cycle.

If they do not, token burns and technology upgrades may not be enough to prevent further consolidation.

My biggest takeaway:

BNB's future depends on the relationship between supply, real demand, and economic activity.

The supply story is relatively clear.

The infrastructure roadmap is ambitious.

What the market still needs to see is sustainable demand.

text:
October 2005. Stanford. A packed hall. Zuckerberg is 21.

The host asks him to explain what Facebook is. The whole world calls it a social network.

He refuses the label.

That same month, someone offers him a billion dollars for it.

Most founders would've taken the money. Most founders would've also said "social network" and moved on.

He did neither.

We don't know exactly what Zuckerberg saw that the label didn't capture. But the refusal itself is data. When a 21-year-old turns down a billion dollars and won't even accept the category his product is being placed in — that's two separate signals that he's operating on a longer time horizon than everyone in the room.

Founders who accept easy framing usually accept easy exits. The two moves rhyme.

The billion-dollar offer made sense in 2005. The refusal is what made it mean something different by the time the number got bigger.

text:
GIVE US THIS DAY OUR DAILY DREAD
Thirty-one days of ghosts, strange tales and the occasional spectacular lack of common sense—all written with a bit of cheek, in typical Haunted Magazine fashion. Hey, there may even be the odd moral lesson, but expect a healthy helping of sarcasm, wit, and questionable subheaders.

DAY 13: THE KISSING GHOST OF RENISHAW HALL
Three cold kisses, an unexpected coffin and a guest room with rather too much atmosphere.

SEALED WITH A HISS
Most ghosts understand the arrangement. They know the drill. Stand at the end of a corridor. Rattle something. Look disappointed in the living. Disappear through a wall before anyone asks you to contribute towards the heating.

The kissing ghost of Renishaw Hall apparently missed that briefing. Its alleged speciality was waking sleeping guests with three cold kisses.

Not a whisper. Not a distant footstep. Actual, unwanted nocturnal affection. You might reasonably expect many things during a country-house stay. Crisp sheets. A decent breakfast. Someone explaining that the portrait above the fireplace is an ancestor who did something unpleasant in Parliament, but an invisible stranger getting familiar with your face should probably be mentioned before you unpack.

FIRST, A LITTLE HALL AND TELL
Renishaw Hall stands in north-east Derbyshire and dates from around 1625. It is the historic home of the Sitwell family, including the celebrated literary siblings Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell. The estate’s history contains financial reversals, ambitious alterations and the creation of its famous Italianate gardens. Plenty to discuss over dinner for sure. 

You might forgive a draught in an old house. You might even forgive the plumbing for sounding like a distressed walrus. Being kissed by something you cannot see is where you might start asking whether there’s a Premier Inn nearby.

KISS AND DON’T TELL
An early published account appears in Lord Halifax’s Ghost Book (1936), under “The Renishaw Coffin”. Its introductory note says the 'kissing victim' probably told Halifax her story herself. 

According to the account, she was staying in a bedroom at the head of the staircase when she awoke feeling three cold kisses. She sought refuge with Sir George Sitwell’s sister, who offered her a sofa—and readily admitted she thought she had experienced something similar in that room.

THREE’S A CROWD
The account continues with Sir George telling his agent, Mr Turnbull, apparently expecting amusement. Instead, Turnbull reportedly turned pale. During his honeymoon stay at the house, a visiting friend of his wife, Miss Crane, had occupied the same room and described the same experience.

That kind of spoilt Sir George’s punchline. He began with an amusing anecdote about a nervous guest and finished wondering if the spare bedroom required an exorcist.

It is also the point where a good ghost story tightens its grip. Another person. Another occasion. The same room. Enough to establish an invisible serial kisser? We shall keep our lips firmly buttoned on that one.

THE DATE THAT DOESN’T ADD UP
Before we get too comfortable, the chronology needs a cold shower. The book places the visit at Sir George’s coming-of-age celebration in 1885, while also giving his birth year as 1860. Renishaw’s own family history dates that celebration to 1881. More awkwardly, the book includes Archbishop Tait among the guests, although Westminster Abbey records his death on 3 December 1882.

Something in the account is wrong. The date, the occasion or some part of the remembered guest list needs correcting.

That does not establish what happened in the bedroom. It does mean we should avoid confidently repeating 1885 as though somebody has produced the invitations. The ghost may be mysterious. The arithmetic is considerably less so.

A COFFIN BREAK
Then comes the detail that makes this considerably harder to shrug off as an uncomfortable night. According to the book, later staircase alterations exposed a coffin beneath the bedroom floor. Iron cramps secured it between the joists, with floorboards serving as its lid. Its construction suggested a seventeenth-century date. No bones remained, although marks reportedly suggested it had once held a body.

Damp and woodworm are unwelcome discoveries during renovation. A coffin beneath the guest room is in a category of its own.

Who put it there? Why? Had it really contained someone? If it did, where the frick had that person gone?

DEAD UNDER THE BED? NOT SO FAST
The coffin provides a magnificent ending to the tale. It does not, by itself, identify the alleged kisser or explain the reported sensations.

Finding something unsettling beneath a room and receiving something unsettling within it are two claims. Connecting them requires evidence.

We should also distinguish the book’s account from later embellishments. Some modern summaries assign the haunting to a “Boy in Pink”, sometimes named Henry Sacheverell. That identification is presented as a belief, rather than an established explanation.

A name gives a ghost a useful biography. It does not necessarily give us the right ghost.

OTHER RESIDENTS. SAME UNEASE.
Renishaw’s ghosts extend beyond the kissing room. A separate account dated September 1909 describes Lady Ida Sitwell seeing a grey-haired woman in a white cap, with blue above a dark skirt, who disappeared near the former staircase. 

Another guest reported a dark-haired female figure. Sir George favoured an explanation that the mind projected impressions. Basically, they were all seeing things.

WHAT MAKES THIS ONE SO UNCOMFORTABLE?
For me, it is the invasion of an ordinary moment. A bedroom should be where you stop watching the doorway. Where the day ends, and you can safely snore away without somebody introducing themselves through your cheek. A distant figure should remain distant.

Cold kisses sound almost quaint until you wake to them and find nobody there. Then the quaintness leaves rather quickly.

A FEW LESSONS FROM THE LIPS
Remember that a coffin is an extraordinary discovery, but not an automatic certificate of haunting.

And when your hostess offers you the sofa while firmly declining a room swap, take it.

THE MORAL OF THE STORY
Renishaw’s kissing ghost is a splendidly unsettling tale: intimate, peculiar and finished off with a discovery nobody wants beneath the floorboards.

Its reported events deserve careful telling. Its muddled chronology deserves equal attention. Question the details.

And if your country-house accommodation promises a warm welcome, make sure that’s as far as it goes. Three cold kisses and a coffin beneath the floor? I’d have much preferred a mint on the pillow.

text:
🚨 WHEN RICE AND NOODLES BECOME THE LANGUAGE OF POLITICAL LOYALTY, NIGERIA HAS A SERIOUS DEMOCRATIC PROBLEM!

A disturbing exchange reportedly captured at a political gathering in Northern Nigeria deserves national attention.

A Tinubu supporter asked members of a crowd what those advising them not to vote for the President had given them.

“Nothing,” they replied.

He then asked what Tinubu had given them.

“Rice and noodles,” came the response.

Finally, when asked whom they would vote for, the crowd answered: “Tinubu, because he gave us rice and noodles.”

Think about the implications of that conversation.

An election should be an opportunity to examine leadership, question policies and decide which candidates offer credible solutions to national problems. It should not become a competition over who distributes the most food packages.

There is nothing wrong with helping families struggling to eat. Food assistance can provide important relief, especially during periods of economic hardship.

But there is a fundamental difference between humanitarian assistance and political inducement.

When food distribution becomes linked to expectations of electoral support, serious questions arise about the independence of voters and the integrity of democratic competition.

The people in that gathering deserve dignity, not ridicule.

A parent worried about feeding children may understandably appreciate anyone who provides immediate assistance. Poverty can make short-term relief especially valuable. That reality should inspire compassion and better public policy, not contempt for struggling citizens.

The responsibility lies with political leaders and institutions to ensure that assistance is not used to compromise free political choice.

President Tinubu's administration has repeatedly defended its economic reforms as necessary for Nigeria's long-term prosperity. Citizens are entitled to assess those policies against their own experiences of food prices, transport costs, employment and household income.

A bag of rice may help a family today. It cannot, by itself, answer questions about agricultural productivity, wages, insecurity or the cost of living tomorrow.

And political support should never be treated as a debt owed in exchange for assistance.

The reported exchange does not establish who funded the food, whether any electoral offence occurred or whether the crowd's answers represented genuine voting intentions. Those facts would require verification.

Nevertheless, the underlying democratic question remains important: are citizens being invited to evaluate government performance, or are material gifts becoming substitutes for meaningful political debate?

Nigeria deserves an electoral culture in which people can receive lawful assistance without pressure, express their political opinions freely and vote according to their convictions.

Food relief should ease hunger. It should never become the price of political freedom.

A citizen's vote belongs to the citizen, not to whoever supplied the rice and noodles. https://t.co/p6aSiIP61m

text:
Engineer caught on video poisoning coworker before she suffered horrific health problems

A California chemical engineer, who pleaded no contest to poisoning a colleague, was caught on hidden video allegedly pouring cadmium into her water bottle.

David Xu, a metallurgist at Berkeley Engineering and Research, spiked his colleague Rong Yuan’s food and water with cadmium, a toxic heavy metal, for nearly 18 months between 2017 and 2019.

“My blood was frozen,” Yuan told The San Francisco Standard of the first time she watched the video. “I almost died. I experienced death so, so close so many times. I cannot let him go.”

Yuan suffered a series of alarming health problems, including persistent vomiting, hair loss, and a strange sour taste in her mouth. Her condition deteriorated to the point that she required repeated hospital visits while struggling to understand what was making her sick.

When Yuan emailed her colleagues on Nov. 27, 2018, to report severe vomiting and take a sick day, Xu responded with chilling nonchalance, The Standard reports.

“You should work from home until you feel better. No reason to rush in,” he wrote, adding, “I think BEAR is moldy.”

The truth emerged after Yuan, suspicious that someone might be tampering with her food and drinks, installed a hidden camera at her workplace.

The footage captured Xu approaching her desk and appearing to pour a substance into her water bottle on separate occasions. Yuan subsequently handed the evidence to police, triggering an investigation that led to Xu’s arrest in March 2019.

After his arrest, Xu was released on $2 million bail. He then received repeated modifications to his home confinement, with his travel restrictions eventually fully lifted, reports The Standard.

In late 2023, under a plea bargain offered by Pamela Price, the former Alameda County District Attorney, the attempted murder charges were dropped.

Xu pleaded no contest to a single felony count of poisoning and received two years of probation, serving just a single day of credited jail time.

Yuan had sought nearly $500,000 in restitution but Xu was ordered to pay only a $7,058 restitution order.

A trend conservatives have argued for years — that the identity surge among teenage girls looked a lot more like social contagion than biology — just got a hard number attached to it, and it isn't coming from a conservative outlet.

The Washington Post, citing CDC data, reports the share of ninth-grade girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual 𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝟑𝟎% 𝐢𝐧 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟏 𝐭𝐨 𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝟏𝟕% 𝐢𝐧 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓. Girls identifying as bisexual alone fell by half, from 26% to 13%. Boys identifying as gay or bisexual barely moved over the same decade — this reversal is a teenage-girl phenomenon, and only a teenage-girl phenomenon.

San Diego State psychology professor Jean Twenge, who published the analysis on her Substack “𝘎𝘦𝘯𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘛𝘦𝘤𝘩,” told the Post the decline began while Joe Biden was still in the White House — which cuts against the easy theory that Trump's return somehow pressured girls back into the closet.

Terry Schilling, president of the American Principles Project, offered his own read: “𝘈𝘮𝘢𝘻𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘩𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘴 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘤𝘶𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘋𝘦𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘌𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘜𝘚𝘈𝘐𝘋.” Not everyone is ready to celebrate — detransitioner and author Walt Heyer called it “𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘦” to treat one report as proof of a lasting shift. Fair enough. But the people who insisted for years this was all biology now have to explain why it's 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐟𝐚𝐬𝐭, 𝐢𝐧 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩, 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐧𝐨 𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐝.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐠𝐞 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐚 𝐥𝐚𝐰 𝐭𝐨 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰. 𝐈𝐭 𝐢𝐬𝐧'𝐭 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐬𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐤.

text:
Bollywood’s undisputed first female superstar slipped into a quiet temple at dawn to marry an already-married producer, keeping the vows hidden for months until a visible baby bump forced the industry’s biggest secret into the open.

The reason might surprise you.

By the early 1990s, Sridevi was an untouchable cinematic force.

Commanding higher fees than her male co-stars and dominating Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu box offices, her stardom was legendary. Producers queued outside her door for dates, and her private life was strictly guarded by her mother, Rajeswari.

Among her most ardent champions was producer Boney Kapoor.

Captivated by her presence since watching her 1970s Tamil film 16 Vayathinile, Boney spent years pursuing her for his magnum opus Mr. India (1987). To secure her, he famously offered her mother ₹11 lakh when her quoting price was ₹10 lakh, and built custom makeup rooms just to ensure her comfort.

Behind the professional admiration, Boney fell hopelessly in love. The complication was immense: Boney was already married to Mona Shourie Kapoor, and the couple had two young children, Arjun and Anshula.

Then came a period of acute personal vulnerability for Sridevi:

In the early 1990s, she lost both her parents within a short span, leaving her emotionally isolated and navigating cutthroat financial disputes alone.

During the production of Roop Ki Rani Choron Ka Raja, a massive commercial disaster that plunged Boney into severe financial debt, the producer stood by her as an unyielding emotional anchor.

When her mother fell critically ill due to a botched neurosurgery in the US, Boney flew across continents to coordinate medical care and handle legal battles on her behalf.

The dynamic shifted from business admiration to a quiet romance that sent shockwaves through Mumbai's elite social circles.

On June 2, 1996, far from the cameras, flashbulbs, and red carpets, the two entered a quiet temple in Shirdi and exchanged traditional garlands in absolute secrecy.

For months, the marriage remained tightly concealed behind studio nondisclosure and industry whispers.

The secret finally became impossible to hide by early 1997, when Sridevi appeared visibly pregnant while completing shoots for Judaai, coincidentally produced by Boney.

The public fallout was ferocious:

Tabloids launched brutal character assassinations, painting Sridevi as a home-wrecker and Boney as an irresponsible patriarch.

Mona Kapoor gave candid interviews expressing deep heartbreak, while Boney’s father, veteran producer Surinder Kapoor, and the extended family initially distanced themselves from the union.

Janhvi Kapoor was born in March 1997, just weeks after Judaai released in theaters, marking Sridevi’s final cinematic outing before she stepped away from films for over fifteen years.

text:
North Korean missiles and Chinese live-fire drills mark a tense day in East Asia

North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles of various types from the Pyongyang area towards the Sea of Japan on Monday, October 12. According to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff, one flew more than 900 kilometres. On the same day, China began live-fire military exercises in five maritime zones along its own coastline.

Japan detected at least two missiles launched 17 minutes apart. The first flew about 220 kilometres and the second more than 910, on an irregular trajectory, a term Japanese officials have used to describe hypersonic weapons. Both landed outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone, with no damage reported to ships or aircraft. Seoul urged Pyongyang to immediately halt launches that violate UN Security Council resolutions. Japan lodged a protest through its embassy in Beijing.

The launches came three days after South Korea flight-tested a domestically developed hypersonic weapon, and nine days after the North tested a hypersonic intermediate-range missile. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said they may also have been a response to Seoul’s test. Kim Jong Un has cut off all dialogue with the South and continues to rebuff offers of talks from Washington.

China’s Maritime Safety Administration announced the exercises, which run until October 17 across the Bohai Sea, the Yellow Sea and the South China Sea, with training activity also taking place in the East China Sea. Taiwan’s Minister of National Defense, Wellington Koo, condemned them. His initial assessment is that they mainly involve artillery fire along the Chinese coast and pose a relatively low threat to the waters around Taiwan.

The drills follow President Lai Ching-te’s National Day address on October 10. Lai said Taiwan cherishes peace but will not give up its freedom, and defended a record defence budget for 2027. Beijing’s Taiwan Affairs Office accused him of distorting the truth and harbouring ulterior motives.

Japan and the United States will hold their joint Keen Sword exercise from October 19 to 29. The key questions now are whether North Korea carries out further tests, and whether China’s manoeuvres stay along its coast or move closer to Taiwan.

Sources: AP, Reuters, Taiwan News

text:
🇺🇸📊 TRUMP FACES FRESH ETHICS QUESTIONS AS AP-NORC POLL MEASURES PUBLIC CONCERNS OVER PERSONAL WEALTH

A new Associated Press-NORC poll published on October 13 indicates that many Americans are concerned about whether President Donald Trump’s personal financial interests are influencing his presidency.

Approximately six in ten respondents said they believed Trump was profiting from the presidency in ways they considered either unethical or illegal. More than half said he had placed substantial emphasis on his own and his family’s financial interests since returning to office.

The survey was conducted among 2,140 US adults between September 24 and 28, with a margin of sampling error of approximately 2.9 percentage points.

Views differed sharply along party lines. Democrats were much more likely than Republicans to believe Trump was acting improperly, while the White House has rejected accusations of wrongdoing and maintained that the president is acting in the country’s interests.

The findings offer a snapshot of public perceptions of presidential ethics, rather than a legal determination that any particular conduct was unlawful. The debate could remain politically relevant as voters approach the November midterm elections.

text:
@KyivPost

Trump did, in fact, throw Ukraine under the bus.

On Friday, as the Ukrainian delegation met his envoys in Miami, the US president had a call with Putin and announced a diesel deal with Russia that lifted sanctions for six months. Zelensky called the whole Miami trip a smokescreen, with Democrats and Republicans calling Trump out for making the deal behind everyone’s back – except the Kremlin’s.

A day later, Trump lambasted Kyiv for hitting Russian refineries and renewed calls for Zelensky’s removal, while Kellogg – contrary to his old boss – said Kyiv should keep just hitting the refineries.

Then, as most Kyivans live without power and water, Trump said out of nowhere on Sunday that an energy truce was in place immediately, with Zelensky saying he only found out like everyone else. Despite that, Kyiv did not strike Russian refineries between Sunday and Monday, but Russia had already hit another power plant in eastern Ukraine’s Kharkiv.

It’s also unclear how the energy truce is supposed to work. Kyiv said it agrees only if it’s bilateral, meaning Russia also stops hitting Ukraine’s energy grid, but the current terms appear to cover refineries only, which overwhelmingly favors Russia. Zelensky also doubled down on Ukraine’s offer by politely saying that Kyiv decides whether and when Russian diesel leaves Russian ports and that Trump should make a deal with Kyiv, not Russia.

Makes you wonder what Putin told Trump in that phone call.

By Leo Chiu

text:
Elon Musk's team offered the mother of his child $40 million to never talk about him, she says. She said no.

In the video below, Ashley St. Clair says it out loud.

"I was offered the opportunity not to speak for $40 million."

She says the offer came through Jared Birchall, the man who manages Elon Musk's money.

The Wall Street Journal reported how it was built. $15 million up front. Then $100,000 a month until their son turns 21.

Do the math. $100,000 × 12 × 21 years is $25.2 million. Plus $15 million. About $40 million, in exchange for silence.

She didn't sign. Instead she went on camera for a documentary about him, out at the end of this month.

Musk says the offer never happened and that she "has a history of making false claims."

Two days ago he posted: "Ashley St Clair was not my girlfriend. We only saw each other a few times."

"I want to set the example for my kids," she says, "that you should never take being materially comfortable over speaking the truth."

Would you have taken the $40 million, or is she right to talk?
