REGIONAL SPORTS ROUNDUP
Tuesday, October 13, 2026

HIGH SCHOOL

CALLOWAY AND MURRAY ADVANCE
Calloway County advanced to Thursday's District 2 Girls Soccer Tournament championship game with an 8-0 goal-rule victory over Mayfield last night at Jim Nix Soccer Complex. Raylee McClure had two goals and an assist while Gabby Yocum logged the clean sheet as the defending district champion improved to 18-2 while Mayfield finished its season at 4-14-1.

In the nightcap, Murray High advanced to Thursday's District 2 Boys Soccer Tournament championship game with a 7-2 win over Graves County. The two-time defending district champion improved to 15-3-2 behind hat tricks from Henri Acreman-Nyamwala and Micah Wyatt. The Eagles season ends with a record of 2-11-1. 

The two seed vs three seed games are on tap this evening at Jim Nix Soccer Complex. In tonight's girls tournament game, Murray will face Graves County at 5:30 with Calloway County hosting Mayfield in the boy's tournament game. 

VOLLEYBALL
Murray High swept Fulton County 3-0 to improve to 15-12 on the season heading into tonight's home match with Tilghman. Trigg County swept Calloway County 3-0 as the Lady Lakers fell to 5-17 as they prepare to host Graves County tonight. 

RICKARD COMMITS TO USM
WPSD-TV reports Carlisle County 6-foot-10 forward Wyatt Rickard has committed to play college basketball at Southern Miss. Rickard averaged 20.3 points and 9.5 rebounds per game as a junior last season and has scored 1,514 career points. He also held Division I offers from UT Martin and Eastern Illinois.

COLLEGE

RACERS 2ND AT JONESBORO
Murray State women's golf shot a 576 over the opening two rounds and sits in second place heading into today's final round of the Lady Red Wolves Classic in Jonesboro, Arkansas. The Racers shot a 286 in Round 1 and 290 in Round 2 which puts them four shots behind first place Austin Peay in the 13-team field. Little Rock's Eleonore Aernouts and Alethea Gaccion of Central Arkansas are the medalist leaders at 140 with Murray State's Ella Scherer and Tina von Arx sharing spots in 12th place at 144. 

DARKNESS HALTS BARNETT TOURNEY
The Murray State men's golf team has a share of fourth place with a 550 after second round play was suspended due to darkness at the Bubba Barnett Intercollegiate in Jonesboro, Arkansas.  Play resumes at 8 this morning with third round immediately following. Murray still has one hole to play in round two and are being led by Sam Guest who is 1 under par through 17 holes of round two. Arkansas State has the lead. 

MBB SINGLE GAME TICKETS ON SALE
The two seed vs three seed games are on tap this evening at Jim Nix Soccer Complex. In tonight's girl's tournament game, Murray will face Graves County at 5:30 with Calloway County hosting Mayfield in the boy's tournament game. te, Alcorn State, Texas Southern, Washington State, Chicago State and Arkansas-Pine Bluff. A limited number of loge boxes and courtside seats remain, while ledge seating is sold out. Upper-level general admission season tickets are available for $99. Fans can purchase tickets at https://t.co/TcfGhmnDRp or call the Murray State Ticket Office at 270-809-3000.

UK PLAYERS HONORED
Two University of Kentucky football players received weekly honors from the SEC yesterday following the team's overtime win against LSU.  Wildcats' wide receiver Kenny Darby was named the conference freshman of the week for a second week in a row.  Wide receiver and punt returner Brock Coffman is the SEC's co-special teams player of the week.  Coffman had a 55-yard punt return for a score for his first collegiate touchdown.

BROHM ADDRESSES ORANGE
Louisville football is back on the practice field as they get set for their week seven matchup against Syracuse.  On Monday, head coach Jeff Brohm acknowledged that Syracuse is always a tough place to play, and that he would like his team to play clean, efficient football on both sides.  The Cardinals are 13-8 all-time against the Orange.  Louisville will face off against Syracuse this Saturday at JMA Wireless Dome.  

UK FINED FOR RUSHING THE FIELD
The Southeastern Conference has fined the University of Kentucky half-a-million dollars after fans stormed the field following the Wildcats' win over LSU.  Folks rushed out of the stands after Kentucky was able to secure a stunning overtime upset on a two-point conversion run by quarterback Kenny Minchey on Saturday night.  SEC officials say this caused UK to be in violation of the league's access to competition area policy.  Because this was a league game, the fine will be paid to Louisiana State.

NO WORD ON VOLS STARTING QB
Tennessee coach Josh Heupel is keeping the starting quarterback decision open after Saturday's Arkansas win.  He says Faizon Brandon's shoulder injury limited practice and left him available only for emergencies.  George MacIntyre made his first career start and led the Vols to a 24-17 victory.  Heupel says MacIntyre knew Monday he would start, but future decisions remain week-to-week.  Brandon has thrown seven touchdowns and one interception this season, with three more touchdowns rushing.

BARNETT BOOTED BY VANDY
Vanderbilt is cutting ties with a football player following his arrest in a downtown Nashville assault case.  Police say 20-year-old wide receiver Kayleb Barnett was seen holding another man in a chokehold during a fight near the pedestrian bridge on Second Avenue South early Sunday morning.  The victim briefly lost consciousness, and Barnett now faces aggravated assault, identity theft and false ID charges. Vanderbilt officials say Barnett violated team standards and is no longer part of the football program.

PROS

MLB RECAP
The Brewers are up 2-0 in the NLCS after topping the Dodgers 7-4 in Game Two at American Family Field.  William Contreras led the way at the plate after going three for four with a solo homer and three runs batted in for the Brew Crew.  Brock Stewart was saddled with the loss after allowing one run on two hits and a walk for Los Angeles, which hopes to claw its way back into the best of seven series when it hosts Milwaukee for Game Three on Wednesday.  

The Guardians took Game 1 of the American League Championship Series with a 7-3 win over the Rays 7-3 in St. Pete.  Jo Adell and Nathaniel Lowe each drove-in a pair of runs for Cleveland.  Cole Sulser allowed three runs out of the pen for Tampa, which will try to draw even at home tonight in Game 2.

MNF RECAP
The Bills fought back in overtime to edge the Rams 37-34 on Monday Night Football in Inglewood.  Greg Rousseau blocked LA's potential, game-winning field goal while Josh Allen marched his squad down the field to set up a 45-yarder to steal the win as Buffalo improved to 4-1.  Matthew Stafford forced overtime with a touchdown drive in the dying seconds of regulation for Los Angeles, which slipped to 2-3.

text:
Hello, I am Palestinian. 
And since honesty is rare in my politics, let me admit a few things.
1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised the war would “throw the Jews into the sea.” Instead, I lost everything and it was called the Nakba. Not because I was not offered a state, but because I rejected it.
1948–2025. The Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they kept me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and cages for me. They used me as propaganda, not as a human being.
1967. After another war I lost, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on “no peace, no recognition, no negotiations.” Three no’s. Fifty years later, I am still without a state. It turns out rejection does not pay the rent.
Oslo, the 1990s. Israel said: “Let’s try.” It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions of dollars in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an Intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.
Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I got a chance to turn Gaza into the Singapore of the Mediterranean. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions of dollars in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.
Democracy? I have not had elections for almost 20 years. Hamas kills opponents in Gaza. Fatah jails them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they are too busy fighting over power.
Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on television who teach children to hate Jews. I praise the “martyrs” who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I replace hope with holy war.
The Arab world. Arab regimes call me “brother.” But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They marginalize me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.
Absurdity. I keep saying I want to “build a state.” And ironically, right next to Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a technological superpower, farms in the desert, cities from dust. Without oil, without endless wealth, only with courage. I could have learned, copied, cooperated. Instead, I chose jealousy and anger.
Anti-Jewish obsession. 
-I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: “Two nations, two states.” Instead, I repeat: “From the river to the sea.” Instead of presenting respect, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I presented only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salam (peace) to Israelis, 
I shouted death to Jews. And then I wonder why Israelis do not trust me, why they are angry, disappointed, and convinced that I do not want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? 
Israel’s fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? 
Israel’s fault. 
I praise death more than life? Israel’s fault. 
Responsibility is not my strong suit.

-I am Palestinian.

I could have built a nation, many times. 
I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. 
I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

—So yes, I am a victim. 
But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own decisions, and my own refusal to abandon hatred.

-And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit.

text:
But if you want to prove something with AI, do it the right way; share the prompt too. 

And if you do it the right way, it almost immediately proves you wrong- a delusional and retarded liar, too. 

@grok Read my post and rate it! Read through my post and evaluate it in light of @BrandynsWisdom’s original post as well as @RuckusHound’s AI-generated statements. Also take into account the claims in my previous post: https://t.co/KsOG88zwO1
because I can’t stand lies and Russian propaganda!

Your screenshot does not establish that Ukrainians want Russian occupation, or that Zelenskyy is refusing peace. Those claims need evidence beyond an AI’s “yes.”

The screenshot actually shows the immediate question. What it does not show is the full conversation, the date or version of the “Trump peace deal,” or a usable underlying source. We can check its factual claims independently, but cannot establish how the answer was produced. AI models can echo a user’s assumptions; research has demonstrated this tendency, known as sycophancy. That does not prove this particular answer was manipulated—it explains why an AI screenshot is not independent verification.

https://t.co/0NdeZCnQre

The central mistake is confusing “comparatively more pro-Russian” with “a majority wants Russia to annex their homes.” Speaking Russian, preferring trade with Russia, supporting a Russia-friendly politician, and wanting Russian sovereignty are different things.

Historically, Crimea and parts of Donbas had stronger pro-Russian political currents than western Ukraine. But KIIS’s April 2014 survey directly asked whether residents wanted their oblast to leave Ukraine and join Russia:
RegionSupported joining RussiaOpposed joining RussiaDonetsk28%52%Luhansk30%52%Kherson4%85%Zaporizhzhia6%82%
Those are substantial minorities in Donbas, and very small minorities in the two southern regions—not majorities welcoming annexation. KIIS’s 2021–early 2022 surveys also found overwhelming support for Ukraine remaining independent, although their Donetsk and Luhansk samples covered only government-controlled territory. These historical figures should not be presented as a current, representative survey of occupied populations.
https://t.co/OYAxd5op1i
Crimea deserves a separate answer. In IRI’s May 2013 poll, 23% wanted Crimea transferred to Russia, while 53% preferred its existing autonomy within Ukraine. After annexation, Pew’s April 2014 survey found 54% of Crimeans supported allowing regions to secede. These were different questions, at different times and under radically different circumstances. They show that Crimea had real separatist support; they do not justify projecting Crimea’s situation onto all the territories Russia claims. The same Pew survey found that 70% in eastern Ukraine—including 58% of its Russian-only speakers—wanted Ukraine to remain united.
https://t.co/6WCJN8Ab5Y
https://t.co/HZsxkB8LHc
“Zelenskyy continues to refuse peace” does not survive checking actual proposals.
11 March 2025: Ukraine accepted the American proposal for an immediate, interim 30-day ceasefire, conditional on Russia accepting and implementing it too. Reciprocal implementation is an essential feature of a ceasefire.
https://t.co/kMtFPwXM6d
12 October 2026: Russia rejected Zelenskyy’s proposed 60-day ceasefire to enable presidential elections. Moscow said it wanted a comprehensive settlement instead; it floated stopping strikes on election day itself. Whatever its stated justification, Russia was the side rejecting that proposed pause in fighting.
https://t.co/IE4UtBbEQI
14 June 2024: Putin’s conditions included Ukraine withdrawing from the entirety of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia—including territory Russia had not conquered—and abandoning NATO membership. Rejecting those territorial and security demands does not demonstrate opposition to peace. It demonstrates opposition to those terms.
https://t.co/0NwNqpfAwB
A temporary ceasefire and a final peace agreement are different. These examples do not settle every disputed negotiation, but they directly contradict the claim that Ukraine simply refuses to stop fighting.
The recruitment abuses are real, and should not be brushed aside. The Council of Europe’s July 2025 memorandum recorded reports of beatings, unlawful detention, denial of access to lawyers, and other serious abuses by Ukrainian recruitment officials. It demanded investigations, independent oversight and respect for conscientious objection. Lawful conscription can require service against someone’s wishes; unlawful detention and violence remain abuses. Describing everything as “Zelenskyy kidnapping young men” collapses that distinction and supplies no evidence that he personally ordered particular unlawful acts. Recruitment abuses also do not establish that Russia’s proposed settlement is acceptable.
https://t.co/LyDiQZXXZ4
Surrender can end conventional fighting. It does not automatically deliver safety, freedom or lasting peace. The UN has documented widespread and systematic torture of Ukrainian civilians detained by Russian authorities. A settlement must therefore address what happens to people under occupation, not merely where the front line stops.
https://t.co/IWaf12HGFk
The UN Charter prohibits aggression against another state’s territorial integrity and recognises its right to self-defence. It does not require an invaded country to surrender whenever its attacker offers to stop on condition of receiving its demands.
https://t.co/VtJJhrRiYO
Russia’s demands were explicitly wider than Ukraine. Read its own draft agreement, published on 17 December 2021:

Article 4 sought to restrict deployments by existing NATO members to the military presence of 27 May 1997, with exceptions requiring all parties’ consent.

Article 6 demanded an end to further NATO enlargement.

Article 7 demanded no NATO military activity in Ukraine, other Eastern European states, the South Caucasus or Central Asia.

“Return to the 1997 borders” is shorthand: the draft concerned deployments and enlargement, rather than simply ordering every later member expelled. Nevertheless, its effect would have been to restrict other countries’ security choices far beyond Ukraine.

https://t.co/0rY5SWEDbL

On 21 January 2022, Russia explicitly confirmed that it wanted NATO forces withdrawn from Romania and Bulgaria. Those are sovereign NATO members, not Ukrainian territories.

https://t.co/8MlYNvRlwe
This supports the conclusion that Moscow seeks a wider sphere of influence and a veto over neighbouring countries’ security arrangements. That is an inference from its documented demands—not proof of a fixed timetable to invade every Eastern European country. Its territorial rhetoric reinforces the concern: on 4 March 2024, Security Council deputy chairman Dmitry Medvedev declared that Ukraine was part of Russia and that supposedly historical Russian territories should “come home.”

https://t.co/PPRiDjBEvU
Russia’s hostile operations against Europe did not start in 2022. There is no single agreed starting date for its modern hybrid campaign. Estonia’s 2007 cyberattacks are an early landmark, although direct Kremlin control should not be presented as conclusively established.

https://t.co/71KBhUkzNb
For more firmly attributed operations, consider the 2014 Vrbětice ammunition-depot explosions in Czechia, which killed two people. Czech authorities identified Russian intelligence operatives as responsible; NATO publicly supported that attribution in April 2021. The 2018 Salisbury nerve-agent attack was also attributed by Britain to GRU officers.

https://t.co/KqxeGSikYZ

https://t.co/yxGkvM5Mjz

In July 2025, the EU formally described Russia’s longstanding campaign as including sabotage, physical attacks, disruption of critical infrastructure, cyberattacks and information manipulation, with escalation since the invasion.

https://t.co/x6C22z5A1g

As for calls to annihilate Ukrainians: there is no reliable exhaustive total, but here are four documented examples by four different figures. They must be distinguished: explicit calls for mass killing, and proposals to erase Ukrainian national identity, are related but different claims.

Timofey Sergeytsev, RIA Novosti, 3 April 2022: advocated “de-Ukrainisation,” ideological repression, censorship and eliminating the name “Ukraine.” This was a columnist’s programme for destroying national identity, published by a state-owned agency—not a formal decree ordering every Ukrainian killed.
https://t.co/YqgSVIfyi1

Alexey Zhuravlyov, Russian State Duma member, May 2022: on Russia-1, described approximately two million supposedly “incurable” Ukrainians as people who should leave or be eliminated. The linked report includes the broadcast footage.
https://t.co/nX31CmEG50

Pavel Gubarev, former Donetsk separatist leader, October 2022: threatened Ukrainians who rejected Russia’s cause with killing “one million, five million, or exterminate all of you.” The linked page contains the video.
https://t.co/yq7bWk0KMr

Anton Krasovsky, RT presenter, October 2022: advocated drowning or burning Ukrainian children who regarded Moscow as an occupier. RT suspended him and condemned those remarks—a relevant fact that should also be included.
https://t.co/e7j8gViaod
These are documented statements, not invented quotations. The UN Commission of Inquiry itself warned in September 2023 that some rhetoric in Russian state and other media may constitute incitement to genocide. That wording is an investigative assessment, not a final court judgment.

Shinkafi thanks Zamfara residents for massive Welcome, says he poised for victory

Governorship candidate in Zamfara State, Bilyaminu Yusuf Shinkafi, has expressed appreciation to the people of the state for the massive reception accorded him during his visit to Gusau last week for the inauguration of the party’s presidential and governorship campaign offices.

Shinkafi described the overwhelming show of support and solidarity as a clear indication of the people’s desire for a new direction in the state, expressing confidence that the ADC would secure victory in the forthcoming elections, by God’s grace.

In a statement signed on Monday, the governorship candidate thanked supporters, party members, youths, women and other residents who turned out to welcome him, saying their enthusiasm had strengthened his determination to offer purposeful leadership.

He said, “The love shown to us by the good people of Zamfara State is massive. We are encouraged by the support and confidence they have demonstrated in our movement.

“We are coasting to victory by the grace of God, and nobody can stop the plans of God for Zamfara State.”

Shinkafi urged residents to sustain the momentum by mobilising more supporters and strengthening the party’s grassroots structures across the 14 local government areas of the state.

He called on the electorate to unite behind the ADC to rescue Zamfara from what he described as the All Progressives Congress-led administration’s style of governance, which he accused of concentrating power in the hands of a few individuals.

According to him, governance should be driven by consultation, accountability, inclusiveness and a commitment to improving the welfare of the people, rather than the decisions of a single individual.

text:
The lyrics to "Karmacoma" by Massive Attack (co-written and performed with Tricky) are famously cryptic, abstract, and paranoid. The track was originally pieced together backstage during a drug-fueled festival trip, resulting in a surreal "fever dream" aesthetic. [1, 2]
However, beneath the psychedelic haze, the song weaves together distinct themes of intimate relationship breakdown and global geopolitical anxiety. [1, 2]

1. Emotional Detachment and Relationship Cynicism

The verses capture a deeply dysfunctional, emotionally distant relationship where both parties have completely checked out. [1, 2]
"You sure you wanna be with me? I've nothing to give... emotional ties, they stay severed": Right from the start, there is an explicit warning of emotional bankruptcy. The speaker admits they cannot offer vulnerability or a healthy dynamic, choosing self-preservation or cold isolation instead. [1, 2]
"Walking through the suburbs, though not exactly lovers / You're a couple...": Tricky describes two people going through the motions of a domestic, suburban partnership without any actual love or intimacy left between them. [1, 2]

2. The Micro vs. Macro: War and Domesticity

The song is highly praised for how it seamlessly juxtaposes mundane, unhappy domestic life with horrific global events happening simultaneously in the background. [1]
"Duplicate and then you wait for the next Kuwait": Written in the shadow of the early 1990s Gulf War, this is the song's heaviest line. Music critics and forum users on SongMeanings interpret this as a cynical social commentary on Western numbness. While a couple physically "duplicates" (reproduces or populates the suburbs), society passively sits back, watching the television and waiting for the next highly televised war for resources to break out. [1, 2]
Tricky himself later noted in interviews that even the lines that seem sexual or romantic are actually about wider anxieties and the state of the world. [1]

3. Self-Medication and Inner Turmoil

"I drink on a daily basis though it seldom cools my temper": This line highlights a cycle of addiction and unresolved anger. The speaker uses alcohol as a coping mechanism to dull their frustration with either their personal life or the world around them, but openly admits it fails to bring them peace. [1, 2, 3]

4. The Chorus: "Karmacoma, Jamaica and Roma"

The phrase "Karmacoma" is a portmanteau invented by the band, combining Karma (spiritual cause and effect) and Coma (a state of profound unconsciousness). It implies being completely numb or asleep to the moral consequences of our actions. [1]
Listing "Jamaica and Roma" serves as a rhythmic, global chant. It acts as a sonic map, tying together Massive Attack's massive sound system influences (Jamaican dub/reggae) and the European urban landscape (Rome/Bristol), emphasizing that this sense of alienation is a worldwide condition. [1]

The Sonic Rebirth

. While "Karmacoma" sounds hip-hop-driven and frantic, "Overcome" leans heavily into a slow, claustrophobic nightmare, adding even more weight to these exact words

Tricky loved these specific lyrics so much that when he split from Massive Attack shortly after, he took them with him. He re-recorded them over a completely different, much darker beat for his debut solo album Maxinquaye, renaming the track "Overcome"

text:
Are Igbo Youths Turning Away From the Military and Police? Soludo’s Question Deserves a Deeper Look

When Governor Chukwuma Soludo spoke about young people from Anambra and the wider South-East joining the military, police and other security agencies, he raised an issue that deserves serious discussion.

But I think the conversation should go beyond telling Igbo youths to enlist. We also need to understand why fewer applicants appear to be coming from parts of the region, what the figures actually prove, and whether the security institutions themselves have work to do to earn public confidence.

At the October 9 memorial service for retired Lieutenant-General Chikadibia Obiakor in Awka, Soludo said negative public perceptions of the military and other security agencies sometimes discourage young people from joining. He also pointed to the importance of role models who could inspire younger generations.

That is what the News Agency of Nigeria report, carried by several media outlets, supports. A stronger viral version claiming that Igbo people are no longer joining the Army, Police or other security services should not be presented as his exact words without checking the original video.

The numbers show a problem, but not the whole story

This is not the first time Soludo has raised the issue. On January 15, 2026, during the Armed Forces Remembrance Day ceremony in Awka, he expressed concern about low participation from Anambra and the South-East in recent Army and police recruitment exercises.

There is data to support concern about police applications. In the 2023 recruitment exercise, the Police Service Commission reported 547,774 applications nationwide. Anambra recorded 1,664, Ebonyi 2,132 and Abia 2,796, while Kaduna recorded 40,272 and Adamawa 36,398.

The gap is striking. And more recent figures reported in February 2026 again placed Anambra and Ebonyi among the states with the fewest applicants.

But I want us to be careful about what these figures mean. They measure applications, not necessarily the number of people who eventually joined the police. They also do not tell us how the figures compare with each state’s population, how many qualified applicants were rejected, or how many people were ultimately recruited.

So, while the figures suggest that recruitment interest is unevenly distributed, they do not, by themselves, explain why.

Is it fear, distrust, or a different career choice?

Several explanations have been raised in public discussion. Some people point to fear of attacks on uniformed personnel, particularly in areas affected by insecurity. Others cite concerns about deployment to dangerous locations, possible discrimination, career progression and the treatment of officers from the South-East.

These are important concerns to investigate, but they should not be presented as established facts without evidence from recruitment records, serving officers, former personnel and prospective applicants.

There may also be economic considerations. Some young people may prefer business, technology or other careers they believe offer better opportunities. Others may simply have no interest in a military or police career.

The question is whether these choices reflect ordinary career preferences, a lack of trust in security institutions, practical barriers to recruitment, or a combination of factors.

We should not assume every Igbo youth who does not apply is afraid, politically opposed to the state or unwilling to serve the country.

The institution must be part of the conversation

I agree that young people should have the opportunity to serve in national institutions without feeling that their background makes them less welcome. But the responsibility cannot rest on young people and community leaders alone.

If the government wants more applicants from the South-East, it should publish clear recruitment information, explain eligibility requirements, make application procedures accessible and provide transparent data on applications, shortlisting, enlistment and eventual postings.

It should also address credible concerns about fairness, safety, welfare and career progression. These are not uniquely Igbo concerns; they matter to anyone considering a career in the security services.

The government should also distinguish between low application numbers and unequal outcomes after application. If fewer young people apply, outreach and public confidence may be part of the answer. If many apply but few are selected, the recruitment and selection figures need to be examined separately.

Without that distinction, we risk arguing over the cause before establishing the problem accurately.

A conversation about belonging and trust

For me, this issue is bigger than whether Soludo is right or wrong. It touches on how young people in the South-East see their place in Nigeria and how they view institutions responsible for the country’s security.

The region’s history, including the Civil War and its lasting memories, forms part of that conversation. But history should be examined carefully rather than used to assume that every young person has the same attitude towards national service.

The goal should not be to pressure people into joining the military or police. It should be to ensure that qualified young Nigerians can consider these careers on equal terms, make informed choices and trust that they will be treated fairly if they join.

Before we conclude that Igbo youths are turning away from the security services, I want to see the full picture: how many apply, how many qualify, how many are recruited, where they are deployed and how their careers progress.

Those figures could help us move from political claims to practical solutions.

So I want to ask: if young people are hesitant to join the Army or Police, what should change first—the way communities view these institutions, the way the institutions treat their personnel, or the way government builds trust with the next generation?

text:
The Watchers Never Left

The oldest book about them reads like a field manual for the modern phenomenon, and the people closest to it keep pointing at the same thing without saying its name

"We are here. We are watching you."

A physicist named Eric Davis was standing in a grove of trees on a remote Utah ranch with binoculars to his eyes, as part of a privately funded study that later fed a Pentagon-contracted program. He watched a dark spot unfold and swell until it covered the canopy. Then, he says, he could not move. "I'm frozen. I can't move a muscle." What came next was "this incredibly loud, multiple metallic-like voices," and they were "in my head." They said: "We are here. We are watching you."

The oldest surviving account of beings that came down to live among humans gives them a name. It calls them the Watchers.

This essay argues the conclusion the record has been circling for more than two thousand years, and it is offered as an argument, not a finding: the Watchers are real, and they never left. They operate among people now, through people, in forms chosen to pass unnoticed. Part of the case is ancient text and part is modern testimony. The newest part is a pattern: the credentialed people closest to the phenomenon all point at the same thing and stop just short of saying it plainly.

The Charge Sheet

Genesis keeps its version to a single verse: "There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them." The Book of Enoch, a text the Dead Sea Scrolls community copied over and over, fills in the file.

There were two hundred of them, "who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon." They took human wives, "and they became pregnant, and they bare great giants." They taught. Azazel "taught men to make swords, and knives, and shields, and breastplates, and made known to them the metals of the earth and the art of working them." A later section of the book, the Parables, adds that another, Penemue, "instructed mankind in writing with ink and paper," and counts even that as a sin, because "men were created exactly like the angels, to the intent that they should continue pure and righteous" (1 Enoch 69:9–11). In this telling, the knowledge the visitors handed down is what made humans mortal.

Most readers stop at the Flood. Enoch 15 does not, and what follows reads less like mythology than a parole report. The giants' spirits "shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling." They "take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst." They "shall rise up against the children of men and against the women, because they have proceeded from them." Then, in chapter 19, the archangel Uriel stands at the place where the fallen angels are held and says of "the angels who have connected themselves with women" the sentence the rest of this case hangs on: "their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods."

The Book of Jubilees supplies the terms of the arrangement. The chief of the spirits, Mastema, pleads with God: "let some of them remain before me, and let them harken to my voice ... for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men." The answer is a quota: "Let the tenth part of them remain before him." Jubilees also names these spirits' lineage plainly: "Thy Watchers, the fathers of these spirits."

The canonical Book of Daniel uses the same word for beings with authority over human politics. "A watcher and an holy one came down from heaven." Then the sentence itself: "This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men" (Daniel 4:17). The watchers issue the decree; the Most High still holds the kingdom. The book places watchers inside the machinery of judgment over kings. In the Book of Giants found among the Scrolls, one of the giants is named Gilgamesh.

The Assyriologist Amar Annus showed in 2010 that the Enochic Watcher stories are "inverted versions of various Mesopotamian myths," built on the apkallu, the sages who brought civilisation's arts to humanity. In that older tradition, he notes, "apkallus could mate with humans, as the Watchers did," the last of the post-flood sages, Lu-Nanna, was "only 'two-thirds apkallu,'" and Gilgamesh, Annus adds, was likewise "two-thirds divine." Skeptics call this borrowing. Read as evidence, it is corroboration: two civilisations with opposite attitudes recorded the same suspect, who descended, taught the arts and interbred. Babylon honoured them. Jerusalem indicted them.

Put the file together and the record does not describe a vanished race. It describes beings whose current form is spirit, who dwell "on the earth," appear in "many different forms," work against humans while needing them, and want to be worshipped "as gods." That is a profile, and the modern phenomenon fits it.

The Same Face in Every Century

In 1900 the ethnologist James Mooney recorded what Cherokee elders told him about the Nûñnë'hï, a spirit people who lived in the mountains: "They were invisible excepting when they wanted to be seen, and then they looked and spoke just like other Indians." More than a century later, the journalist George Knapp described the presence at the center of the Pentagon-funded Skinwalker Ranch study, imagining how the public would take it: "It's invisible. You see it only when it allows you to see it ... It's among you ... They've been here all this time, they're among us, and we don't get to see them."

The computer scientist and astronomer Jacques Vallée spent the 1960s putting the UFO files beside European folklore. His conclusion, restated in *Dimensions*: "the modern, global belief in flying saucers and their occupants is identical to an earlier belief in the Good People. The entities described as the pilots of the craft are indistinguishable from the elves, sylphs, and lutins of the Middle Ages." Modern investigators, he wrote, "are prying into the affairs of the Secret Commonwealth."

The journalist John Keel came to the same view from the field in West Virginia in the 1960s. "We have been observing complex forces which have always been an essential part of our immediate environment," he wrote, "beings and forces which coexist with us but are on another time frame ... yet have the ability to cross over into our reality." His best-known case was a visitor called Indrid Cold, the grinning man, who communicated without speaking: "The grinning man did not speak aloud. Woody sensed the words." Keel also catalogued men "who posed as military officers" yet "obviously had no knowledge of military procedure."

The government's own investigators found that it follows people. Colm Kelleher, a scientist on the Defense Intelligence Agency-funded program, reported that "All five DIA personnel deployed to the ranch experienced profound anomalies" and that all five "brought something home." The family of the team's leader, a Naval Intelligence officer, reported "black shadow people standing over their beds when they awoke." Kelleher called it the "Hitchhiker Effect," wrote of "person to person transmissibility of paranormal phenomena," and estimated that "R0 could be denoted as 3." He was careful to add that the numbers were "too few to draw any firm conclusions." Robert Bigelow, who owned the ranch and paid for the work, was blunter: "we all had hitchhikers. We all took things home with us."

The paranormal researcher Nathaniel Gillis describes what he and his colleagues call "the pre-archetype": "They're orbs ... We would see an apparition with our eyes, look on camera, it's a ball of light. We would see a UFO with our eyes, look on camera, it's a ball of light." The same lights, he says, "can become anthropomorphic ... It could project apparitions of men and women." The British investigator Steve Mera goes further: "they are with us. They are amongst us ... they actually occupy and look through the eyes of man."

Vallée explained why the costume changes while the actor stays the same. "It is possible to make large sections of any population believe in the existence of supernatural races," he wrote, "by exposing them to a few carefully engineered scenes the details of which are adapted to the culture and symbols of a particular time and place." Fairies, then airships, then saucers, then orbs. In *The Invisible College* he put it this way: "this control has been in force throughout history," and "it is of secondary importance that it should now assume the form of sightings of space visitors."

Everyone Is Pointing

The decisive fact is a pattern among the people with the most access and the most to lose. One by one, they describe the Watchers without using the word.

Bigelow. Robert Bigelow is the man who paid for the search. By his own estimate he has "probably" spent more on it than any other individual in the United States. He bought the Utah ranch, funded the private institute that studied it and held the Pentagon contract that followed. In 2017 he told *60 Minutes*: "There has been and is an existing presence, an ET presence." Asked whether humans would meet other intelligent life out in space, he answered: "You don't have to go anywhere." Pressed on where, he said: "It's just like right under people's noses." In 2021 he was asked what he had meant. One reading, he said, is "that they can be among the population, whether they're hybrids, or there's some other kind of, really look alike." He credited that view to a researcher with "fantastic academic credentials," whom he placed "definitely on the more extreme." Asked whether the beings at the ranch, if they are among us, could also be counted as alien, he said: "if you follow the literature and pay attention to a lot of other kinds of sources, they absolutely are." On his own podcast in 2026 he walked up to the old vocabulary and stepped around it. "A lot of people try to say well, these are angels or demons," he said. His own words were "a coexistence" with "other intelligences" sharing "the dimension of space time." Of whatever tore apart a ranch camera, he gave its terms in its own voice: "We can control you. You can't control us. We aren't going to repeat things twice. But we're going to give you some slack." Asked whether non-human beings have souls, he described a ladder. All of them, he said, are connected to "a supreme god force," with "permutations then of attitudes, intelligences, hostility, love," and "maybe we can speculate that the more human that it is, the worse it is."

Vallée. No researcher has more standing. "I propose that there is a spiritual control system for human consciousness," he wrote, "and that paranormal phenomena like UFOs are one of its manifestations." He was explicit about what it is not: "We are not dealing with successive waves of visitations from space. We are dealing with a control system." And about what it does: "It is a control system which acts on humans and uses humans." He noted that witnesses "have thought they had seen demons," and that the winged disk is "consistently associated with the angels." He reported, without dismissing it, the view of the former Jesuit Salvador Freixedo that the phenomenon "originates with entities that manipulate our reality and our destiny for their own purposes," and that "these entities ... play with our emotions in order to be worshipped as gods." Enoch 19:1 says "sacrificing to demons as gods." On the human side of the operation, Vallée wrote: "it is not clear exactly which side is infiltrating the other."

Pasulka. Diana Walsh Pasulka, a professor of religious studies, spent years inside the community of scientists and insiders who study the phenomenon. Her verdict on Vallée's central claim is short: "Vallee argues, however, that the phenomenon has been around for thousands of years, perhaps more. He is right." Working in Catholic archives covering 1200 to 1800, she says, "I kept coming across aerial phenomena ... These were souls from purgatory, these are angels coming down, these are demons." She records that "Carl Jung called the UFO a technological angel." She has also described insiders' talk of a hierarchy of beings, and of "factions in the intelligence community."

Levenda. Peter Levenda is the historian of the occult who co-wrote the *Sekret Machines* nonfiction series with Tom DeLonge, and Vallée wrote its foreword. In the acknowledgments to *Gods*, the authors thank "a group of about ten individuals we refer to as the "advisors." Most of these gentlemen cannot be identified here due to their standing in their respective agencies and departments." With those advisors behind the book, he states its premise without hedging: "the Phenomenon is real and first occurred as an event (or events) in ancient history or prehistory." He then turns to Genesis 6. The bene elohim, he writes, "either have human bodies or can assume human bodies in order to function on the earth. When they do assume human bodies, it seems that they are able to propagate through sexual intercourse with human women." His parenthesis follows: "(In common UFO parlance, these might be considered "hybrids".)" Unexplained events, he writes, call up "a memory buried so deeply in human consciousness" that people reach for "gods and angels and demons and jinn."

Knapp. The journalist who broke the modern era's biggest stories, and who sat at the table of the Pentagon-funded study, offers it, in his own vocabulary, as his best guess: "My guess is that, you know, it's an intelligence that lives here. It's not alien, it lives here. It's always been here ... we're the newcomers." He also reports that one reason the program was "supposedly" killed was that "religious fundamentalists in key positions at the Pentagon thought it was Satan, satanic, demonic."

Elizondo. Luis Elizondo, the former Pentagon intelligence officer best known for his work on its Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, held up a hand drawing during a February 2022 interview. A square stood for "the human body," a circle for "the brain," and a triangle for what "some have referred to as the soul or the id or the chi or the spirit," something that "does reside inside the body but is not contained necessarily with inside the body." He called it "this fourth element if you will" and spoke of "a hidden kingdom to which we're all connected." In the same interview he said: "I've been privy to some pretty extraordinary things I don't talk about them publicly." He did not call the drawing alchemical. But square, circle and triangle are the figures the alchemists nested into their seventeenth-century emblem of the philosopher's stone. A former intelligence officer reached for the geometry of the occult tradition, then said he would not say more.

Grusch. Under oath before Congress, the former intelligence officer David Grusch testified that he "was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access." His account is secondhand by his own description: asked whether he had seen the bodies, he told the committee it was "something I have not witnessed myself." Asked whether the biologics recovered were human, he answered: "Non-human. And that was the assessment of people with direct knowledge on the program I talked to, that are currently still on the program." Asked about contact, he said it "is something I cannot discuss in a public setting."

Friedman. The screenwriter Brent Friedman described what an older military officer's private briefing implied. "The alien thing ... feels like a footnote," he said. What would make a man cry was "the idea that reality is not at all what it seems. And there are beings that have access into our minds potentially." Davis himself, the physicist in the grove, was asked whether humanity has been in touch with multiple kinds of non-human intelligence for many years. He answered: "True."

Luna. Representative Anna Paulina Luna, who ran the congressional task force on these files, pinned a five-word post to the top of her public account in April 2026: "Read the book of Enoch." On the country's largest podcast she laid out the reading in which "angels came down, rebelled against God, interbred with humankind," offering it as "a good starting point" for what the Anunnaki might have been, and spoke of "the technology that was given to mankind by these angels." She added, carefully, "I'm not saying that these things are angels."

Stratton. On October 12, 2026, the night before his memoir *Out of the Shadows* went on sale from William Morrow, Jay Stratton, the first director of the Pentagon's UAP Task Force, sat across from Bret Baier on Fox News. "Both the defense contractor community and the government have craft of non-human origin," he said. Then, in a clip *Special Report* posted that evening, he said something no Enoch scholar would have phrased better: "humanity is not the only intelligent life in the universe, nor do we know the intent of the non-human intelligent life that's here. It's very concerning." Not out there. Here.

Kennedy. In October 2026, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. told Luna on her channel that he had been briefed by "a very high level NASA scientist and then a bunch of Navy SEALs and Green Berets who had been on recovery teams." He said they "had figured out how to call some of the, uh, ships in." Luna answered in general terms, speaking of claims in any field: "People will say a lot, but can you prove it?"

One at a time, each of these is deniable. Together they form a single shape: "control system," "demons," "angels," "bene elohim," "hybrids," "it lives here," "right under people's noses," a "hidden kingdom," "Non-human," "beings that have access into our minds," "Read the book of Enoch." The vocabulary stays inside the clearance and protects the career. The object it describes is the one in the file. A prosecutor calls this associative evidence, and associative evidence is evidence.

First Them, Then Us

The record also fixes the order of events, and the order matters. In Enoch the beings bring the arts: metals, weapons, cosmetics, writing. In Babylon the apkallu bring them. In Luna's paraphrase, the technology was "given to mankind by these angels." Levenda's word for this is "paleocontact," and of the phenomenon he says: "Quite possibly it has always existed. Everywhere."

The pattern holds in the modern record. In April 2023 the director of the Pentagon's UAP office, Sean Kirkpatrick, told a Senate subcommittee that about 52 percent of the reports in its holdings described round orbs or spheres. Its FY2023 annual report put orbs at 25 percent, with no shape recorded for more than half of all reports, and attributes most resolved orbs to balloons, drones and clutter. The orb is the commonest shape reported. Human devices that make glowing orbs exist: laser-induced plasma, a Navy patent for laser-plasma decoys and a military "talking" plasma ball demonstrated in 2018. None reproduces what witnesses describe, which is silent hovering, intelligent pursuit and the change from a light into a figure. *Interpretation:* the reported phenomenon still outruns the human imitations, the same order Enoch describes, in which the Watchers taught and men copied.

How They Operate Among Us

How would such beings move through a world full of cameras and paperwork? The record gives three modes:
- a body of their own;
- a borrowed host;
- no body at all, working directly on perception.

The desk's survey of human-form cases found that every one leans toward the third or second mode, a perception hack or a borrowed host, rather than flesh. That is consistent with the camera problem: of sixteen recording devices present across the cases, none captured a disguised entity. Gillis's line explains the gap: "look on camera, it's a ball of light."

Keel mapped the borrowed-host mode decades ago. "In contactee parlance, persons who perform involuntary acts are said to be "used."" Such people, he wrote, "are prone to controlled hallucinations and possession." Vallée: "acts on humans and uses humans." Mera: "they actually occupy and look through the eyes of man ... I assure you they are already in there somewhere. You know, infiltrate in the highest and the darkest places." The text that began this case said "on the earth shall be their dwelling," in "many different forms."

There is also an institutional layer. Keel documented an official memo describing a man in Air Force uniform who briefed local police and was not who he claimed to be. Knapp said of one government group in the story: "Their job is counterintelligence." Mastema needed his tenth "to execute the power of my will on the sons of men," and such an operation runs through human hands. In Vallée's words, it is not clear "which side is infiltrating the other."

The Objections, Answered

"It's borrowed myth." Annus showed that Enoch reworks Mesopotamian sources. Borrowing explains the paperwork, not the sightings. When two hostile civilisations independently describe the same visitors doing the same things, the duplication is corroboration. The Cherokee had never read Enoch, and their spirits were still "invisible excepting when they wanted to be seen."

"There's no body." The file never promised one. In Enoch, what survives the Flood is spirit: the Watchers' offspring live on as spirits that "take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst." Demanding a skeleton of a being described as disembodied is demanding a fingerprint from a voice.

"Every trail ends in humans and paperwork." It is supposed to. Vallée set out the logic: if an intelligence wanted to "bypass the intelligentsia and the Church, remain undetectable to the military system," then "this is exactly how you would have to act. At the same time, of course, such a process would have to provide its own explanation to make ultimate detection impossible." The evidence looks human because it was designed to.

"Planted evidence is human tradecraft." Granted. Governments have staged incidents, and that history is real. But human tradecraft in the chain does not exclude an operator behind it. Human channels are exactly how the record says the Watchers work.

"The insiders hedge." They do, and the hedges are reported above in their own words: Kelleher's small numbers, Luna's "I'm not saying" and her "can you prove it?" A hedge from someone under oath, holding a clearance or guarding a career is not a retraction. It is the form disclosure takes when it cannot be stated outright, the clearest signal that someone is pointing.

Smoke

*What follows is the case's summation. The record items are sourced above; the conclusion drawn from them is interpretation.*

Here is what has been shown:
- An ancient file describes descended beings who taught the arts, bred with humans, and remained "on the earth" as spirits, the giants' spirits hungry and hostile, the fallen angels' spirits "assuming many different forms" and wanting worship.
- A second, older civilisation described the same beings.
- A canonical prophet placed watchers inside the decree that brings down a king.
- Cherokee elders, the European fairy faith, Keel, Vallée, a Pentagon-funded scientist and today's field investigators described the same behaviour: invisible until it chooses, human when it wants, reading minds, following people home and working through them.
- The best-credentialed people in the field, from a sworn whistleblower and the Pentagon's first UAP Task Force director to a member of Congress, each pointed at that same object in their own careful vocabulary.

No single exhibit convicts. Cases are built the way this one is: witnesses describing the same suspect across more time than any hoax could survive. Some of them could not have coordinated: Enoch's scribes, Babylon's, the Cherokee elders. Others, Bigelow, Knapp, Kelleher and Davis among them, worked side by side on the same ranch, and their agreement counts for less. Where there is this much smoke, from this many directions, over this many centuries, there is fire.

Davis, frozen in a Utah grove, heard metallic voices announce themselves in the present tense. The oldest record of these beings had already given its answer about where they would be after the Flood. "On the earth shall be their dwelling." The name it gave them was Watchers, and that is what the voice in the grove said it was doing: "We are here. We are watching you."
