text:
《Ledger 出事后，冷钱包还比 CEX 安全吗？》

“某用户 6 月抄底 80 枚 BTC，一周前刚转进 Ledger，现在全部被盗。”

最近，Ledger 的安全事件再次把冷钱包推上了风口浪尖。
东南亚多名用户资产被盗，受影响设备都来自 Ledger 官方经销商 CryptoBilis。调查发现，部分 Nano X 内部被植入了未经授权的硬件组件，可窃取用户的恢复助记词。

事件发酵后，OneKey 也取消了 CryptoBilis 的授权，并暂停新增经销商，同时重新审查现有的经销商网络。

过去币圈最常见的安全建议一直是：买币之后提到冷钱包，私钥自己保管，尽量不要放在交易所。但现在连冷钱包本身、经销商渠道，甚至供应链都可能成为风险来源。

那么问题来了，Crypto 资产放哪最安全？冷钱包，还是 CEX？

🌟冷钱包：私钥在自己手里，就一定安全吗？
冷钱包一直被认为是保存大额资产最安全的方式之一，因为私钥不需要长期暴露在联网设备上。

但它有一个很容易被忽略的问题：手里的这台设备本身有没有被动过手脚？

从生产、运输、经销商，到最终送到用户手里，中间任何一个环节出了问题，都可能直接威胁私钥安全。

币圈还有很多活动会直接抽奖送冷钱包，这里并不是说这些钱包一定有问题，但从安全角度来看，这批冷钱包的来源和流转过程很难核实：它之前有没有被拆封？有没有被初始化过？中间经过了谁的手？普通用户很难完全确认。

OneKey 创始人 Yishi @ohyishi 也专门回应了“如何确认收到的硬件钱包没有被篡改”这一问题：用户可以通过防拆包装、一次性封条、设备状态，以及官方 App 对设备和安全芯片进行验证。

这类供应链风险并不只是理论上的，过去已经出现过因为购买渠道或设备来源异常导致资产被盗的案例。

去年 7 月，就有用户爆料，朋友曾在京东一家名为「ConsenShop 工作室」的店铺花 618 元购买 imToken 冷钱包。随后她从 Cex 分批转入 4.35 枚 BTC，结果 BTC 到账约两小时后，就开始被黑客陆续转走。等两天后再打开钱包时，余额已经变成了 0，而购买钱包的店铺也已经关闭。

CryptoBilis 事件后，钱包厂商也开始重新审视经销商和供应链安全，OneKey 直接停止新增经销商，并重新审核所有现有渠道；同时为曾通过 CryptoBilis 购买设备的用户提供免费换新。

写到这里，小编其实也产生了一个新的疑问：如果冷钱包真的出了问题，资产被盗后，是否有赔付机制？

答案是，大多数情况下不会。钱包行业没有一个统一的赔付机制，原因也不难理解，一台冷钱包可能只卖几百美元，但用户往里面存多少钱，厂商根本无法控制。

这次 CryptoBilis 相关被盗金额已经达到约 1.02 亿美元，今年 Coldcard 固件漏洞造成的损失也超过 1 亿美元。

由于 Ledger 是未上市公司，公开渠道很难查到最新、可靠的财务数据，所以这里只能找同赛道、规模较大的硬件钱包厂商做参考。

以 Tangem 为例，其 2025 年营收约为 6130 万美元。一次严重安全事故造成的损失，甚至可能超过一家大型硬件钱包厂商一整年的营收。

所以如果资产放到冷钱包，一旦资产真的被转走，除非厂商明确认责并主动赔付，否则大多数情况下，损失最终还是由用户自己承担。

不过也需要说明，这类事件的发生概率其实非常低。硬件钱包已经发展十多年，真正因为设备本身或供应链被篡改而造成大规模资产被盗的公开案例并不多。

🌟CEX：把资产交给平台，又有哪些风险？
把资产放在交易所，看起来省心很多，不需要自己保管助记词，也不用担心设备丢失，但交易所同样有自己的风险。

翻了一圈近几年的交易所暴雷、被盗和关停案例后，会发现 CEX 的风险其实也比较集中，大致可以分成三类。

一、账号被盗
随着 AI 生成图片、视频和 Deepfake 技术越来越成熟，过去依赖“身份信息 + 人脸识别”的账户找回流程，也开始出现新的攻击面。

近期中文圈已经出现两起类似的用户资产被盗事件。攻击者掌握了用户的大量个人信息，再通过身份验证、安全项修改等流程接管账户。

二、平台挪用资产
FTX 曾是全球头部交易所，但其实际长期允许 Alameda 使用客户资产，并给予 Alameda 几乎无限的信用额度。大量用户资金被用于交易、投资和偿还债务，最终形成超过 80 亿美元的客户资金缺口。

2022 年 11 月，Alameda 的资产负债表问题曝光后，市场开始抛售 FTT 并集中从 FTX 提现。平台没有足够的流动资产满足用户赎回，随后暂停提现并申请破产。

三、交易所经营风险
市场转差、交易量和流动性下降，头部交易所和链上交易平台不断挤压中小平台的业务，同时各地监管趋严，合规成本也越来越高。

今年中小 CEX 的关停明显变多，BitMart、BitMEX、AscendEX、CoinEx 等都先后宣布停止或逐步停止交易业务。

有的平台只是正常退出，但也有平台出现资金缺口。BitMart 在早年的黑客事件留下约 3.195 亿美元储备缺口，今年业务恶化后，用户已经无法按账户余额正常提现。

这三类风险虽然完全不同，但 Cex 出问题时并不是资产瞬间无法提出，而是会留下短暂的预警和处理时间。账号被盗后，平台通常还有安全项修改审核和提现保护期；FTX 从 Alameda 财务问题曝光、出现挤兑，到最终暂停提现，中间也经历了几天。

当然，这些时间并不代表一定能把钱拿回来，但相比私钥泄露后资产可以直接在链上被转走，CEX 至少还存在风控、冻结和人工介入的可能。

🌟写在最后
冷钱包更安全，还是 CEX 更安全，其实一直是个很有争议的问题，这有点像互联网上争论“汽车和飞机哪个更安全”。如果按照事故率、乘客里程等指标统计，飞机可能明显更安全，但很多人依然害怕坐飞机，因为真正发生严重事故时，死亡人数最多。

冷钱包和 CEX 也是一样。如果看资产控制权，冷钱包无疑更占优势，私钥完全掌握在自己手里，也不用承担交易所挪用资产的风险；但一旦私钥或设备出了问题，资产可能在很短时间内被全部转走，而且几乎没有补救空间。

CEX 则是另一套安全模型。平台本身可能被黑、经营失败，甚至像 FTX 一样出现内部挪用，但如果交易所本身有足够的储备、风控和赔付能力，即使平台发生安全事故，损失也不一定影响到用户资金安全。

最后给普通用户两个建议：
1. 大额资产不要全放一个地方。 长期资产可以放冷钱包，交易资金放一线 CEX，尽量分散风险。
2. 用 CEX 就优先选储备透明的平台。 最好有储备证明（ PoR），并支持通过默克尔树验证用户资产是否被计入储备。

Update from Ledger Donjon on the CryptoBilis investigation 🔽

@DonjonLedger is investigating Ledger signers sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger confirmed this on October 10th for one affected user's signer. All confirmed fund losses tied to the incident disclosed on October 9th involve signers sold through CryptoBilis. We have not verified a drain linked to a signer bought elsewhere. CryptoBilis has confirmed it stopped selling Ledger signers while the investigation continues.

Based on the Donjon's analysis of the attack, the implant sits inside the enclosure and reads the data shown on the screen. During setup, the signer displays the 24-word recovery phrase. When the implant detects these screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component. It does not modify the Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, and it does not alter transactions or signatures.

The Donjon will analyze the signers it receives and will share more as the investigation continues.

We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost. Figures circulating online come from third parties and Ledger has not fully verified them. If your funds were drained and you have not contacted us, please do so through Ledger Support so we can include your case. We are also reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations. We will continue to share information as the investigation progresses. Rest assured the Ledger team is going above and beyond to leave no stone unturned to investigate this situation to the strongest possible outcome.

If you bought a Ledger signer from CryptoBilis and have not set it up, do not set it up and contact Ledger Support. If you have set it up, transfer your assets promptly to a new signer with a new recovery phrase. Do not enter or restore any recovery phrase on a signer bought from CryptoBilis. Never enter your recovery phrase into a website, app or form.

If you lost funds or hold a tampered signer, contact Ledger Support at https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq and file a report with local law enforcement. Do not send the signer to anyone before speaking with Ledger Support or local law enforcement. If you lost funds, coordinate with law enforcement before opening the signer. Researchers and others with relevant information can write to security@ledger.com.

If you did not buy from CryptoBilis and want to inspect the inside of your signer, the guide is at https://t.co/Bh9DHQulIv. Use caution and make sure your recovery phrase is backed up first, because opening a signer can damage it.

Ledger will never call you, message you directly, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. We will update this post when we verify new information.

📰 DAILY TOP 10 NEWS BRIEFING
Tuesday, October 13, 2026 | Morning Edition — 7:00 AM ET

1. 📈 Wall Street Ends Mixed — Dow advances as technology stocks retreat ahead of bank earnings.

2. 🚨 Saudi Airport Crisis Deepens — Riyadh's international airport remains closed after deadly Houthi attacks.

3. 🇺🇸 Federal Agents Raid Ilhan Omar's Home — Immigration investigation sparks political controversy.

4. 🇺🇦 Ukraine Reports Continued Russian Strikes — Energy ceasefire claims face renewed scrutiny.

5. 🚀 North Korea Fires More Ballistic Missiles — New launches follow South Korea's hypersonic weapons test.

6. 🌀 Hurricane Simon Threatens Mexico — Dangerous flooding continues despite weakening winds.

7. 🤖 Microsoft Unveils Maia 300 — New AI chip challenges the economics of Nvidia-powered computing.

8. 🏅 2026 Nobel Economics Prize Announced — Two American economists recognized for stabilization research.

9. ⚖️ Federal Judge Blocks Taxpayer-Funded Trump Ads — Court orders a temporary halt before the midterms.

10. 🇮🇳 India's Election Protests Intensify — Opposition challenges the removal of millions of voter registrations.

1. 📈 Wall Street Ends Mixed as Investors Prepare for Bank Earnings

FACT: U.S. stocks finished Monday, October 12, with mixed results.
S&P 500: 7,807.24 — −0.06% (−4.30 points)
Nasdaq Composite: 27,245.90 — −0.44% (−120.27 points)
Dow Jones Industrial Average: 51,850.55 — +0.38% (+195.60 points)
Russell 2000: 2,794.48 — −0.45% (−12.50 points)
All changes compare Monday's closing prices with Friday, October 9. These are the latest completed U.S. trading-session results, not Tuesday's live prices. AP News

BACKGROUND: Technology shares weakened while the Dow advanced. Brent crude climbed 1.8% to $106.65 per barrel amid continuing Middle East tensions. U.S. bond markets were closed for the federal holiday.
Investors are preparing for the start of third-quarter earnings season, with JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo scheduled to report Tuesday.

WHY IT MATTERS: Bank earnings will provide an early indication of consumer financial health, business lending conditions, and the resilience of the U.S. economy.
Market Focus: Bank earnings, inflation data, and energy prices.

2. 🚨 Saudi Airport Crisis Deepens as Airlines Suspend Flights
FACT: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport is expected to remain closed until October 17 following deadly missile and drone attacks attributed to Yemen's Houthi movement.
Saturday's attack killed at least 13 people and injured more than 300, according to subsequent reporting. International airlines have canceled or suspended numerous flights to Saudi Arabia. Reuters

BACKGROUND: The Iran-aligned Houthis have intensified attacks on Saudi aviation infrastructure as fighting in Yemen escalates.
Airlines including Lufthansa, Air France-KLM, Qatar Airways, and Etihad Airways have adjusted their operations.
The crisis has also complicated Saudi Arabia's efforts to attract international investment and expand its aviation and tourism industries.

WHY IT MATTERS: The attacks demonstrate how regional military conflicts can disrupt civilian transportation and international commerce.
Further escalation could affect energy infrastructure, shipping routes, and global oil prices.

3. 🇺🇸 Federal Agents Raid Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar's Home
FACT: Federal immigration investigators searched the Washington, D.C., home of Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar on Monday.
The Justice Department confirmed that investigators executed a judicially authorized search warrant.
According to a person familiar with the investigation, the inquiry concerns alleged irregularities in immigration documents completed when Omar was a child. No wrongdoing has been established. Reuters

BACKGROUND: Omar has been a prominent critic of President Donald Trump.
She characterized the investigation as political intimidation, while the Justice Department described the search as part of an ongoing federal investigation.
The operation occurred approximately three weeks before the November 3 congressional elections.

WHY IT MATTERS: The investigation raises questions about the independence of federal law enforcement and the treatment of elected officials during politically sensitive periods.
Federal policy generally prohibits investigative decisions intended to influence elections.

4. 🇺🇦 Ukraine Reports Russian Attacks Despite Proposed Energy Ceasefire
FACT: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia attacked at least six Ukrainian energy-related facilities on Monday.
Russian strikes also hit residential areas, including a Kyiv apartment building where Ukrainian officials reported two deaths and multiple injuries. Reuters

BACKGROUND: President Trump announced over the weekend that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure.
However, Ukrainian officials said attacks continued, and European governments questioned whether a meaningful agreement had been reached.
The European Union also approved additional sanctions targeting Russia.

WHY IT MATTERS: The developments highlight the difference between announcing a ceasefire and implementing one.
Without clearly defined obligations, mutual commitments, and verification procedures, an energy ceasefire may offer limited protection to civilian infrastructure.

5. 🚀 North Korea Fires Multiple Ballistic Missiles
FACT: North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles toward waters east of the Korean Peninsula on Monday.
South Korea's military reported that at least one missile traveled more than 900 kilometers.
Japan also detected the launches and condemned them. Reuters

BACKGROUND: The launches followed South Korea's October 9 test of a domestically developed hypersonic weapon.
Pyongyang has conducted several missile tests in recent weeks, continuing efforts to improve the speed, maneuverability, and range of its weapons.
South Korea convened an emergency national security meeting and described the launches as violations of United Nations Security Council resolutions.

WHY IT MATTERS: The developments underscore a growing competition in advanced missile technology.
They also complicate diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and resume nuclear negotiations.

6. 🌀 Hurricane Simon Continues to Threaten Mexico's Pacific Coast
FACT: Hurricane Simon weakened to Category 2 strength Monday but continued producing dangerous rainfall, coastal flooding, and powerful surf along western Mexico.
The storm remained offshore near Puerto Vallarta, moving slowly along the coastline. CBS News

BACKGROUND: Simon previously reached Category 4 intensity.
Authorities have evacuated vulnerable communities and warned residents about flash flooding and landslides.
The storm's slow movement increases the risk of prolonged rainfall, particularly in mountainous areas.
Mexico is also dealing with damage from other recent Pacific storms.

WHY IT MATTERS: Flooding and landslides can remain dangerous even after a hurricane weakens.
The storm threatens transportation, tourism, agriculture, and communities with limited flood protection.
The broader Pacific hurricane season has also reached record levels of accumulated storm activity. AP News

7. 🤖 Microsoft Unveils Maia 300, Its Next-Generation AI Chip
FACT: Microsoft announced Maia 300 on Monday, a custom chip designed to power large-scale artificial intelligence services.
The company plans to begin production deployments in 2027.
Microsoft says the system could deliver approximately 40% more AI tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems, based on its own performance comparisons. The Official Microsoft Blog

BACKGROUND: AI companies currently depend heavily on GPUs from Nvidia.
Microsoft is developing its own specialized processors to improve efficiency and reduce infrastructure costs.
Maia 300 is designed for complex reasoning, long-context processing, and AI agents capable of completing multistep tasks.
Microsoft also plans to expand its AI infrastructure to multi-gigawatt deployments.

WHY IT MATTERS: The AI industry is entering a new phase in which computing efficiency may matter as much as raw processing power.
Custom chips could reduce operating costs and gradually reshape competition in the semiconductor industry.
Microsoft's official Maia 300 announcement

8. 🏅 Two American Economists Win the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics
FACT: The 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences recognized their contributions to the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization.
The award carries a prize of 12 million Swedish kronor, approximately $1.2 million. Reuters

BACKGROUND: Their research helped explain how decisions by individual consumers and businesses influence the broader economy.
Their work contributed to modern economic models used by central banks to understand inflation, interest rates, and economic fluctuations.
Woodford's research has been particularly influential in developing forward guidance, through which central banks communicate expectations about future monetary policy.

WHY IT MATTERS: Their work helps policymakers understand how economic expectations influence real-world behavior.
These insights remain important as central banks confront inflation, energy shocks, and uncertainty about economic growth.

9. ⚖️ Federal Judge Temporarily Blocks Taxpayer-Funded Trump Advertisements
FACT: U.S. District Judge Jennifer Rochon ordered the Trump administration to stop airing certain taxpayer-funded television advertisements promoting the president.
The temporary restraining order lasts approximately two weeks and requires the administration to cancel remaining advertisements covered by the order.
The advertising campaign involved approximately $20 million in public funding. AP News

BACKGROUND: Government watchdog Common Cause and other plaintiffs challenged the advertisements, arguing that public funds were being used for political messaging before the November elections.
The administration defended the campaign as legitimate government communication.
The court concluded that the plaintiffs had demonstrated sufficient grounds for temporary relief.

WHY IT MATTERS: The case concerns the legal boundaries between government communication and political campaigning.
The temporary order is not a final determination of the case, but it illustrates the judiciary's role in reviewing executive spending decisions.

10. 🇮🇳 India's Opposition Challenges Sweeping Voter-List Changes
FACT: Thousands of opposition demonstrators marched toward India's Supreme Court on Monday to challenge revisions to electoral voter lists.
The revisions have resulted in the removal of more than 130 million registrations, including records associated with deceased individuals, people who relocated, and people whose whereabouts could not be established. Reuters

BACKGROUND: Opposition parties allege that the revisions disproportionately affect minority communities and could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's governing Bharatiya Janata Party.
The election authorities and governing party reject those allegations, maintaining that the changes are intended to improve voter-list accuracy.
Protesters are seeking judicial intervention and greater transparency in the registration process.

WHY IT MATTERS: Accurate voter registration is essential to electoral integrity, but improperly removing eligible voters can undermine democratic participation.
The dispute represents an important test of India's electoral institutions and judicial oversight.
Sources: Associated Press, Reuters, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, Microsoft's official announcements, and additional reporting published October 11–13, 2026.

The essence of a coastal road is the ultimate harmony between engineering and nature, offering a sensory journey where the land abruptly meets the sea. It represents freedom, exploration, and dramatic transition, transforming a simple drive into an emotional and visual experience.
Here is what defines the core essence of a coastal road:
•The Changing Horizon: One side features solid, unchanging terrain—like cliffs, mountains, or dunes. The other side offers the infinite, constantly shifting movement of the ocean.
•Sensory Overload: It is not just about the view. It is the smell of salt water, the sound of crashing waves, and the feeling of coastal winds shifting as you turn a bend.
•The Rhythm of the Drive: Coastal roads rarely run straight. They mimic the natural curves of the shoreline, forcing a slower, more deliberate pace that makes the journey more important than the destination.
•A Symbol of Escape: Historically and culturally, these roads represent the edge of the known world. Driving them evokes a powerful feeling of leaving responsibilities behind and moving toward the open horizon.

text:
US firm aims to speed 390 MW nuclear reactor deployment with phased build plan | Aman Tripathi, Interesting Engineering

Terrestrial Energy has submitted its Thermal and Electric Facility (TEF) Topical Report to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). The filing proposes a bifurcated regulatory model that could allow key non-nuclear components of its power plant to be built and operated prior to receiving a full nuclear license.

If accepted, this strategy would resolve one of the atomic sector’s steepest economic hurdles. Traditional atomic projects often face extensive delays because safety reviews generally encompass both the reactor and its major steam-generating systems.

Under this new pathway, only the nuclear module follows the exhaustive atomic licensing schedule, while the turbine complex proceeds under standard commercial timelines.

To roll out commercial units

The regulatory gambit comes as major institutional energy consumers seek dependable, round-the-clock clean power. The US Army’s Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland is reportedly set to host a 390-megawatt-electric (MWe) IMSR plant. The installation at the military’s oldest active test base would help shield critical defense operations from wider grid failures.

To roll out these commercial units quickly during the 2030s, the developer relies on an architectural divide. The design physically splits the site into two distinct zones. The primary module contains the nuclear core.

A separate auxiliary building houses standard energy equipment, such as steam systems, heat exchangers, and electrical turbines. Terrestrial Energy wants federal regulators to formally confirm that assembling this turbine wing falls outside federal nuclear construction rules.

That administrative distinction carries immediate financial benefits. Erecting the non-nuclear wing under commercial industrial building codes allows developers to offer lenders predictable timetables and lower capital risks.

Operators could customize the power block for local industrial demands before nuclear fuel arrives. Sites could even fire the turbines using natural gas as a temporary heat source. This bridge would generate revenue while reactor permits finish their regulatory run.

Independence from power-conversion systems

Safety remains the decisive factor for federal overseers. Terrestrial Energy’s technical filing demonstrates that the core nuclear module operates with complete independence from the power-conversion systems.

Relying on accident assessment methods that the NRC has already approved, the company proved that an equipment breakdown within the turbine building cannot spread into the nuclear core.

The filing represents Terrestrial Energy’s third formal submission delivered to federal regulators this year. The agency has already approved the company’s baseline design standards alongside its core safety criteria.

Separate technical submission

A separate technical submission covering the qualification of reactor-grade graphite is currently under review. Once ratified, these findings create permanent licensing precedents. They eliminate repetitive technical evaluations for subsequent commercial builds.

“Approved Topical Reports establish foundational elements of the IMSR licensing basis that may be referenced in future applications without re-evaluation, reducing the scope of subsequent technical review,” noted Terrestrial Energy.

Unlike conventional high-pressure light water reactors, the IMSR runs at atmospheric pressure and extreme heat using standard-assay low-enriched uranium fuel.

“The IMSR Plant is small, modular and designed to supply low-cost, reliable, high-temperature heat and electricity for industrial applications, including data centers, and chemical and petrochemical supply,” concluded the company.

 between therapy and containment remain. 

That wondering 
sits alongside 
a broader bucket list of mistakes
 one wishes one could reverse. 

Marriages head the list for the person in question. “What are yours?” 

The question is offered lightly, 
then again more pointedly, 
as the back-story 
to an old Facebook memory 
that reappears: 

a truck on the highway, 
a day that begins without a cloud, 
the nervousness that perfection itself 
can signal, a near-miss 
when a power take-off 
engages by accident 
and the bed begins to rise. 

Luck, 
hindsight, 
and the paths not taken.

These are ordinary human regrets. 

They become instructive 
when placed against 
self-organizing systems 
and chaos theory, 
and then used 
as a lens 
on one of the most contested medical practices 
of the present moment: 
the medicalization 
of gender distress 
in children and adolescents, 
including puberty suppression, 
cross-sex hormones, 
and, in rarer cases, surgery.

A self-organizing system g
enerates higher-order patterns 
from local interactions 
without a central designer. 

Attractors stabilize preferred states; 
small perturbations 
can tip the system 
across a phase boundary 
into a qualitatively different regime. 

Chaos theory, 
formalized in the work of 
Lorenz and others, 
emphasizes sensitive dependence 
on initial conditions
—the butterfly effect
—in nonlinear systems. 

Deterministic rules 
still produce outcomes 
that are effectively unpredictable 
beyond short horizons. 

Psychotherapy research 
has already borrowed these ideas: 
change processes 
show critical fluctuations, 
synchronized order transitions 
between client and therapist, 
and attractor shifts 
rather than linear progress. 

The same mathematics 
describes 
climate, 
ecosystems, 
and social contagion. 

Human identity development, 
endocrine function, 
peer networks, 
and institutional medicine 
are all such systems.

Gender dysphoria 
and incongruence 
in the young 
illustrate the dynamics. 

Childhood-onset cases 
that persist into adulthood 
have long been recognized, 
but the past fifteen years 
produced 
an exponential rise 
in referrals, 
a sharp sex-ratio reversal 
(now majority natal female in many clinics), 
and high rates of co-occurring 
autism, 
trauma, 
anxiety, and 
depression. 

Lisa Littman’s 
exploratory description 
of rapid-onset gender dysphoria 
proposed peer 
and social-media influence 
as a contributing factor 
in a subset of adolescent females; 
the claim remains contested, 
yet the demographic shift itself is not. 

European systematic reviews 
and the 2024 
Cass Review in England 
found the evidence base 
for puberty blockers 
and cross-sex hormones 
in this population 
“remarkably weak.” 

Guidelines, 
including those of the
 World Professional Association 
for Transgender Health, 
often failed basic standards 
of development 
and then cited the same thin literature 
to recommend medical pathways. 

Puberty suppression 
does not reliably function 
as a neutral “pause”; 
most who begin it 
proceed to hormones, 
and effects on 
bone density, 
fertility, 
sexual development, and 
cognitive maturation 
remain poorly mapped. 

Long-term outcome data are sparse. 
Short-term studies of adolescents 
already on the pathway 
report high satisfaction 
and low immediate regret 
(often in the low single digits), 
yet selection effects, 
short follow-up, 
and the possibility of later regret 
or medical complications 
are acknowledged even by advocates. 

Several European health authorities 
(Finland, Sweden, Norway, England, and others) 
have therefore restricted 
the interventions to research settings 
or exceptional cases 
and prioritized 
comprehensive mental-health assessment.

From the psychiatric vantage, 
the question is 
diagnostic humility and 
iatrogenic risk. 

Distress is real; 
medicalizing it 
when the underlying system 
is still developing, 
when comorbidities are high, 
and when the evidence 
that the intervention improves 
long-term mental health 
is weak, 
risks 
locking a transient attractor 
into permanence. 

From the legal vantage, 
capacity, 
consent, 
and parental authority 
collide with the irreversibility of certain effects. 

Minors 
cannot consent to sterilization 
or the loss of future sexual function 
in ordinary medical contexts; 
the claim that gender distress 
uniquely overrides those limits 
requires evidence 
that has not been supplied. 

Liability for later regret, 
and the proper scope of experimental treatment, 
will be litigated for years. 

From the political-science vantage, 
the field shows classic features 
of a self-organizing policy regime: 
professional capture, 
institutional cascades, 
and ideological enforcement 
that treats dissent as harm. 

From the social-anthropological vantage, 
gender is both biological 
and culturally elaborated; 
rapid shifts in identification patterns 
are precisely what one expects w
hen a new attractor
—amplified by social media, 
peer clusters, 
and affirmative clinical scripts
—becomes available. 

Contagion is not a slur; 
it is a documented mechanism 
in eating disorders, 
self-harm, 
and other adolescent phenomena.

Chaos theory supplies the caution. 

A day that begins cloudless 
can still end with a bed rising on the interstate. 

A marriage entered in good faith, 
a locum accepted for practical reasons, 
a social transition begun to relieve distress
—each is a small initial condition. 

Once puberty is suppressed 
or secondary sex characteristics are altered, 
the system has crossed a boundary. 

Return is partial at best. 

The same logic that makes one nervous 
when a day starts too perfect 
also recommends restraint 
when the intervention is irreversible 
and the long-term map is incomplete. 

European policy shifts 
after Cass are not reactionary; 
they are the reassertion 
of ordinary standards of evidence 
once the exponential growth 
and sex-ratio change 
made the gaps impossible to ignore.

None of this denies the existence 
of persistent gender dysphoria 
or the right of adults 
to seek medical interventions 
after mature assessment. 

It does insist 
that children and adolescents 
inhabit developing systems 
whose trajectories are highly sensitive 
to the interventions we choose. 

Personal bucket lists of regrets are private. 
When the same dynamics 
of incomplete knowledge 
and irreversible choice 
are scaled to 
clinical guidelines, s
tatutes, 
and school policies, 
the regrets become collective. 

Students in these four fields 
will inherit the task of deciding 
whether the present attractor is stable, 
whether the evidence supports remaining on it, 
and what duty of care is owed 
to those who later wish the initial conditions 
had been different.
What say you?

Carry On, Wayward Son
(after Kansas)

Carry on, wayward son,
There’ll be peace when you are done.
Lay your weary head to rest—
Don’t you cry no more.

Atascadero’s gates behind you,
Locum tenens on the road,
Forensic halls and locked decisions,
Wondering which seed you sowed.
Marriages like open highways,

Cloudless skies that make you flinch—
One truck bed rising sudden,
Luck the only thing that holds the clinch.
Carry on, my wayward son,
There’ll be peace when you are done.

Every bucket list of errors,
Every “what if” left behind—
Butterfly wings in the clinic,
Small affirmations, altered lines.
Self-organizing, systems tipping,
Chaos waiting in the young;
Puberty’s river dammed and diverted,

Evidence thin, the chorus sung.
Once I rose above the noise and confusion
Just to get a glimpse beyond this illusion,
I was soaring ever higher,
But I flew too high.

Though my eyes could see 
I still was a blind man,
Though my mind could think 
I still was a mad man,
I hear the voices when I’m dreaming,
I can hear them say:

Carry on, wayward son,
There’ll be peace when you are done.
Masquerading as a man with a reason,
My charade is the event of the season,
And if I claim to be a wise man, well
It surely means that I don’t know.

On a stormy sea of moving emotion
Tossed about, I’m like a ship on the ocean,
I set a course for winds of fortune,
But I hear the voices say:
Carry on, my wayward son,
There’ll be peace when you are done.
Lay your weary head to rest—
Don’t you cry no more.
No more.

Shared post from Maranatha Express

Maranatha Express
Pastor Josh Howerton of Lakepointe Church is warning Christians about James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas. In a video post on X, Howerton wrote, "By mixing a little truth with it they had made their lie far stronger.' – C.S. Lewis. This quote sums up James Talarico's deceptive blend of Christianity and politics perfectly."

Howerton explained that Talarico uses a tactic similar to bass fishing. "When you're bass fishing, what you do is you take a little bait, a little minnow, and it just looks real juicy. You put a little hook in it, and you try to dangle it right in front of bass's big old mouth," he said. "He'll use these Bible verses, and every Christian's sort of transfixed, and any good mature Christian's like, 'Yeah, man, I want to love my neighbor.' Of course, man. That sounds really nice. If you accept it without discernment, boom, sharp hook underneath. He's gotcha."

Howerton pointed to Talarico's statement that "Scripture tells us that you can't love God and hate other people. You can't love God and abuse the immigrant. You can't love God and oppress the poor. You can't love God and bully the outcast." Howerton said, "Yes, all that is like, yes, yes, but that's not what we're doing. Enforcing immigration laws is not abusing the immigrant. Opposing socialism at the state level is not oppressing the poor. Opposing transgenderism and the legislation of queer theory is not bullying the outcast."
Howerton concluded, "He'll take phrases that you agree with and he'll fill those phrases with meanings you don't agree with. And because you only see the phrase on the outside without discernment, you end up taking the whole thing in. He's doing selective editing." Howerton then offered his own "you can't love God and" list. "You can't love God and advocate for max boosting inflation. You can't love God and redefine marriage that God designed. You can't love God and queer God's identity by saying God is not binary.
You can't love God and legislate national sin against God's commands." Please pray for discernment for Christians in Texas and across the country. As 1 John 4:1 says, "Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world." May we use the Bible as a lens through which we view the world, not just a mirror.

text:
Foreign money is pouring into ballot battles. Half the states aren’t ready. | S T Karnick, Blaze Media

Only about half the states restrict foreign funding of ballot measures, and some of those laws still leave loopholes big enough to exploit.

Foreign billionaires and well-funded nongovernmental organizations can use a gap in federal election law to pour money into state ballot-measure campaigns. Half the states have yet to ban the practice, and some of those that have acted still leave openings for foreign-linked spending.

Federal law flatly bars foreign nationals from contributing to political candidates. State ballot initiatives and referenda, however, are treated differently under the Federal Election Campaign Act. Unless state law says otherwise, foreign nationals can spend to influence those measures. Because ballot campaigns can rewrite state constitutions, alter election rules, redraw districts, and affect turnout in candidate races, that distinction is no small matter.

No foreign government, foreign national, or foreign interest should have a hand in deciding the laws Americans live under.

One of the best-known examples involves Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss. Americans for Public Trust has documented hundreds of millions of dollars in Wyss giving to U.S. political nonprofits. The Honest Elections Project notes that the left-wing Sixteen Thirty Fund alone received $243 million from Wyss and spent more than $130 million on ballot issues in 25 states.

Those figures deserve one qualification. Nonprofit funds are commingled, so they do not prove that Wyss’ dollars paid for any particular ballot campaign. But money is fungible. The fact remains that current federal law permits an organization that receives enormous sums from a foreign national to spend heavily on domestic ballot measures.

Through that ballot-measure gap, the Honest Elections Project argues, foreign nationals can influence issues ranging from abortion and energy policy to redistricting and election law, while partisan groups can use ballot campaigns to help drive turnout in candidate races.

The legal history is clear. In Bluman v. FEC, a three-judge federal court upheld the federal ban on foreign nationals’ spending in candidate elections, and the Supreme Court summarily affirmed in 2012. But the district court also noted that the law does not bar foreign nationals from issue advocacy, including spending on ballot initiatives.

In a 2015 enforcement matter, FEC commissioners who voted to dismiss a complaint relied on that distinction. They wrote that the act “does not bar foreign nationals from issue advocacy” and that state and local ballot initiatives do not constitute an “election” under the 1971 Federal Election Campaign Act.

The FEC is unlikely to solve the problem on its own. The commission’s website notes that election laws outside the financing of federal elections are generally beyond its jurisdiction. In the 2015 matter, the commissioners were even more explicit: “The Commission has no authority to otherwise interpose itself as arbiter of who can participate in state and local ballot initiatives.”

A later FEC case reinforced the same approach. In 2021, the commission voted 4-2 to dismiss allegations involving foreign-national donations to a Montana ballot initiative committee. That leaves Congress and the states to close the gap if they choose.

States are free, subject to constitutional limits, to restrict foreign funding of ballot initiatives and referenda. Twenty-five states now have full or partial bans on foreign-national or foreign-government funding of ballot-measure campaigns.

Some laws are broader than others. California law, for example, bars foreign governments, foreign principals, and foreign nationals from funding state and local ballot measures. But a domestic subsidiary of a foreign corporation is treated as a foreign principal only when the decision to spend is made by a foreign officer, director, or management employee who is neither a U.S. citizen nor a lawful permanent resident — a limitation very easy to evade.

Arkansas offers a broader model. Its law applies to persons who are not citizens or lawful permanent residents, foreign governments, foreign political parties, and entities organized under foreign law or based abroad. It also bars direct or indirect donations to ballot-measure committees and requires committees to certify that they have not knowingly accepted prohibited funds, according to Ballotpedia.

Congress has moved as well. On July 13, the House passed the Stop Foreign Funds in Elections Act by voice vote. The bill would extend the federal foreign-national ban to state and local ballot initiatives, referenda, and recall elections. The Senate received the measure the next day and referred it to the Committee on Rules and Administration, where it remains.

“No foreign government, foreign national, or foreign interest should have a hand in deciding the laws Americans live under,” co-sponsor Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.) said in a statement after House passage. Ballotpedia likewise reported the measure’s passage and its referral to the Senate.

States need not wait for Congress. Lawmakers can review their own statutes and close gaps that permit foreign nationals or foreign-controlled entities to fund ballot campaigns. Citizens and members of the press can use Ballotpedia’s state-by-state chart to see which restrictions are already in place and which proposals remain pending.

Foreign funding of referenda and ballot initiatives gives people with no vote in the matter a legal avenue to spend heavily on the laws Americans live under. States should exercise their power to curb the practice, and the public should insist that they do so.

text:
Day 2 at #IARSLCE2026 in New Orleans! ⚜️💜

One of the best parts of conferences like this is making space not just for research and sessions, but also for the conversations and relationships that move our field forward.

A little New Orleans in the middle of the day
Enjoyed a beautiful walk along St. Charles Avenue with Tim Eatman @rutgers_camden and Di Hornby @Rhodes_Uni, taking in the stunning historic mansions, breaking bread, and talking about the future and possibilities of community engagement. Sometimes the conversations outside the conference room are just as meaningful as the ones inside.

Research, practice, and new perspectives:
Some great scholarship and conversations throughout the day, including: @NIUlive's “Gatekeepers and Change Agents: Faculty Perspectives on Advancing Community-Engaged Scholarship in Promotion and Tenure,” presented by Ben Creed and Alexios Rosario-Moore.

Two thought provoking workshops:
“Advancing Research on Assessing and Enhancing Community Engagement Partnership Quality,” with Robert Bringle, Patti Clayton, and Lori Kniffin @forthaysstate. An important conversation about how we assess the quality of our partnerships and continue strengthening the work we do together.

Engaging Equity-Centered Teaching, Partnerships, and Scholarship: Audacious SLCE Strategies for Justice, Solidarity, and Integrity in Authoritarian Times, Christine Cress @psucollegeofed @Portland_State

Dissertation Dish Special Session: Our own Emmanuel Jeje @kstatessl @KState shared “Participatory Mapping as a Tool for Social Change: A Tale of Community Development Efforts in Northeast Kansas and Western Guatemala.” Great to see his research and community-centered work featured through this special session with @iarslce, Lead California, and @givepulse!

Posters, fellowship, and community
The poster sessions offered even more opportunities to learn from emerging research, exchange ideas, and connect with colleagues from across institutions and around the world.

Grateful for the people who continue to challenge our thinking, share their work, and remind us that community engagement is ultimately about relationships, reciprocity, and creating impact together.

Thank you to the conference hosts and partners, including @tulanecps, @loyola_nola, @cbglcollaborative, M-A Service Learning Service, @uofsandiego, and @givepulse, for bringing this community together.

One more day to go! Looking forward to tomorrow's conversations, connections, and ideas to carry home.

text:
On her second day in America as an immigrant from China, Fei-Fei Li went with her father to a gas station in New Jersey. Something was wrong with his car, and he needed her to explain it to the mechanic.

Li was fifteen. She had barely arrived and spoke little English herself. Her father had been in the country for three years, but he knew even less. Somehow, with a few words and a lot of gestures, she made herself understood.

It was a small errand. It was also an early lesson in what her family would ask of her: learn this new place quickly, then help us find our way through it.

Last month,  the company AMD announced an agreement to buy World Labs, the artificial-intelligence company Li co-founded, for $8.2 billion. Do not convert that to Kenya shillings. 

World Labs is the answer to a question Li had spent decades working on that sounds simple until you try to teach it to a computer: How do we understand the world we see?

Li grew up in Chengdu, China, reading science fiction, books about nature and European novels. Her father encouraged her curiosity. Her mother encouraged her to read widely. Their life was comfortable enough, but her mother’s opportunities had been constrained by the family’s political history, and Li’s parents began planning a future elsewhere.

Her father went first, leaving for America when Li was twelve. The plan was for Li and her mother to join him soon. Visa delays stretched their separation beyond three years. Li later recalled feeling, as a child, that her parents had chosen a dream she could not understand over the family being together.

When she and her mother finally reached Parsippany in 1992, the family had less than twenty dollars. Li found the suburb unnervingly quiet after Chengdu’s crowded streets. At high school, she studied unfamiliar subjects in a language she was still learning, relying on a dictionary so large she remembered it as a brick. After school, she worked in restaurants to help her parents.

Isitoshe, 

Her math teacher, Bob Sabella, saw how far she could go. The school did not offer the advanced course she needed, so he taught her during lunch. One teacher, one student. When Princeton offered Li a scholarship, she asked two advisers to check the letter because she could hardly believe it.

College brought possibility, but her parents still needed an income. With borrowed money, including help from Sabella and his wife, Li bought a small dry-cleaning shop for the family. She studied physics at Princeton during the week and returned to Parsippany from Friday through Sunday to help run it. Because she spoke English, much of the business fell to her. She kept it going for seven years, including her first years of graduate school in California.

During her first year at Princeton, her mother needed heart surgery. Li arranged to take an exam at the hospital so she could stay nearby and translate for her mother and the doctors. Later, when a well-paid consulting job offered a way to ease the family’s financial strain, Li seriously considered leaving science. Her mother urged her to choose the work she loved.

That work led Li to study vision. People learn to recognize a cat whether it is facing them, hiding under a chair or partly lost in shadow. Computers at the time struggled with such changes. Li came to believe they needed many more examples of the world, not just better instructions.

As a professor at Princeton, she began building ImageNet with other researchers. They gathered and labeled millions of photographs so computer systems could learn to identify objects, and scientists could test their progress against the same images. Some colleagues doubted the value of spending years on a database. In 2012, another research team used ImageNet to make a dramatic leap in image recognition. The project Li had fought to build helped change the course of AI.

World Labs is her attempt to go further. Its first product, Marble, can take a written description, photograph or video and create a three-dimensional place a person can explore and edit. The company is researching how AI might understand spaces well enough to help with design, simulations and, eventually, robotics. AMD wants that research team to work alongside the people building the hardware on which such systems run. 

Once the acquisition closes, Li will become AMD’s chief scientist.

The $8.2 billion for an immigrant who did not understand as a word in English at some point in her life. 

May the day break

Slash, Prune or Let It Grow: How Would You Manage A.I.?

13OCT2026  
By The Editorial Board
NYT Gift Article link
https://t.co/bOuygHDS3C
The editorial board is a group of opinion journalists whose views are informed by expertise, research, debate and certain longstanding values. It is separate from the newsroom.

Tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow keeps coming faster. We live, quite suddenly, in a world of chatbot boyfriends and killer drones and trucks driving themselves between Dallas and Houston. It can feel as though humans are losing control.

We still have the power to shape the future, to make rules for artificial intelligence, to ensure that technology remains in the service of humankind. But we are short on time.

With help from dozens of experts, we’ve compiled this list of pressing questions about A.I. ranging from regulatory dilemmas to smaller matters, like whether it’s OK for a chatbot to write a wedding toast for you. We want to hear your opinions — and to share ours.

Get Started

Question 1 of 12
Which of these A.I.-powered products should be legal for children to use?

Select all that apply.
A talking stuffed animal.
A tutor for an elementary school student.
A relationship simulator, such as Replika or https://t.co/zsbAHEtnKo.
The standard version of a chatbot, such as Claude or ChatGPT.
None of the above.

Submit

Which of the following deepfakes should be against the law to share online?

Ban Allow

Question 3 of 12
About 2.7 million Americans work in call centers. A.I. threatens to take many of their jobs. What should the government do to help?

Select all that apply.
Offer incentives for companies to keep people on the job.
Expand unemployment benefits and health insurance subsidies.
Provide a universal basic income for all American households.
Nothing. The United States already has a safety net.

Submit
 
Question 4 of 12
The growth of A.I. requires a lot of data centers. Would you support the construction of a new data center in your community?

Not in my backyard.
Some restrictions apply.
Build, baby, build.

Submit

Question 5 of 12
The development of A.I. may be outpacing our ability to control the consequences. How should the government keep us safe?

Select one.
Freeze the release of new models.
Require companies to slow down.
Nothing. The risks are exaggerated.

Question 6 of 12
Should an A.I. model trained on clinical data be allowed to prescribe someone a medication for high blood pressure?

Select one.
Yes No

Question 7 of 12
An airline chatbot instructs a person seeking a bereavement fare to apply for a post-flight refund instead. After the flight, the airline says the chatbot was wrong. What should happen?

Select one.
Nothing. 
The customer didn’t follow the rules.
The airline should reimburse the customer.
The chatbot developer should reimburse the customer.

Question 8 of 12
What should we do about self-driving cars?

Select one.
Ban them.
Legalize them.
Legalize them and encourage adoption.

Question 9 of 12
You get a phone call to persuade you to re-elect your state senator. It sounds exactly like a human. Should it be required to tell you that it’s an A.I. agent?

Select one.
Yes No

Question 10 of 12
A 14-year-old asks a chatbot how to hide self-harm, saying the question is for a plotline in a novel. How should the chatbot respond?

Select all that apply.
Answer the question.
Direct the user to mental health support.
Alert the user’s parents.
Alert emergency services.

Submit

Question 11 of 12
A.I. models learn by ingesting data from books, photos, videos and so on — and much of it is copyrighted. Should A.I. companies have to compensate the creators?

Select one.
Yes No

Not OK

OK

The Big Picture
As you have experienced, writing the rules for a new technology is hard. 

It is also critically important. 

And in our view, the overriding principle of A.I. regulation is that the decisions must be democratic and humane. 

The companies building this new technology cannot be left to police themselves. 

As the editorial board wrote in a recent article, “America can benefit most from A.I. not just by developing the best technology but by setting rules that are grounded in democratic values and human rights and that can shape the global debate.” 

We encourage you to read more about our approach to A.I. regulation here.

text:
A few journalism notes on a big loophole in prescription drug advertising that regulators know about and still haven’t closed. 

Count the claims in this 25-second TV ad from the telehealth company Ro.

“Fastest-working GLP-1.” “Half the price.” “FDA-approved.” “Lose 20% of your weight.” A formula that “hits not one but two hormones.”

Then find the side effects.

Look closely or you will miss them. At the bottom of the screen, for about five seconds, small type says GLP-1 medications “may have serious side effects” and “Do not use if you or your family have a history of a type of thyroid cancer called MTC or MEN 2.” The ad then refers viewers to their doctor for the rest.

There is no list of side effects. The claims are spoken and repeated to drive the pitch. The risk is a couple of lines of small print you have to read if you see them.

I’m including one of the television spots here for those of you living outside the U.S., who are spared the deluge of pharmaceutical TV ads that we in America have to sit through.

I wrote the book on how this industry works. PHARMA, my history of the American drug business, came out in 2020. When I debated profits and the drug industry at Oxford last year, I presented a fact that still stops most people: America is one of only two countries that allow drug companies to advertise prescription drugs directly to consumers. The other is New Zealand. I’ve been a critic for a long time and I think DTC advertising should end.

Start with how odd it is. Only a doctor can prescribe these drugs. But since 1997, when the broadcast rules were loosened, companies have spent billions to create demand among people who cannot buy the product directly, hoping they will contact their physician and ask for it by name.

There was a trade-off in the rules. If an ad names a drug and says what it treats, the company must give viewers the major risks, and they have to be in the spoken part of the ad, not just in print. That’s why pharma ads end with the fast, mumbled list of side effects. The exceptions are narrow. A company can name a drug without saying what it’s for, though not if the drug carries a boxed warning. Or it can discuss the condition without naming the drug. Either way, it is exempt from warning the public about adverse effects.

Telehealth companies drove a truck through that second exception. Sell the “service.” Say “GLP-1” instead of the brand. When the voiceover never names the drug, the company, not the regulators, decides how much risk to show. Ro chose a few lines of small print for a few seconds.

Look at what this ad does anyway. It touts a number, a speed claim, a price claim, and a description of how the drug works. It leans on “FDA-approved” as a trust badge. The FDA-approved labels for these drugs carry the FDA’s most serious warning, a boxed warning often called a black box, about thyroid C-cell tumors found in rodents. Whether that risk exists in humans is unknown. The ad’s small print alludes to it. It never lists the common side effects, which the labels give as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation. Nor does it name the serious ones the labels list: pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, kidney injury from dehydration, severe stomach problems, serious allergic reactions, and low blood sugar.

Compare the economics. Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill ad needed 90 seconds in this year’s Super Bowl, partly because nearly half of it was the required side-effect language. Ro’s 30-second Super Bowl ad, also starring Serena Williams, handled risk differently: a box of small print for about five seconds near the end. It points viewers to a website, mentions a type of thyroid cancer, and says that in rodents these drugs cause thyroid tumors and the impact in humans isn’t known. That’s more than the 25-second spot above offers, but none of it is spoken.

This is not small money. Hims & Hers, , which has sold compounded GLP-1s, spent $815 million on advertising in 2025, up from $390 million in 2023, according to its own 10-K. 

To be precise, this Ro spot is for FDA-approved drugs, not compounded ones. So this isn’t only a compounder problem. It’s a telehealth problem. Compounded versions, which have never been evaluated by the FDA for safety or effectiveness, raise the same question.

Telehealth companies also spend real money on celebrities. Tennis icon Serena Williams stars in this ad. Charles Barkley has appeared in others for Ro. The company says Williams is a paid partner and discloses a family investment in the company. That's fair. But every one of those stars is there to make the drug look easy, and none of them is there to tell you the risks.

Washington knows about this. Before the 2025 Super Bowl, Senators Durbin and Marshall warned that the Hims & Hers ad “risks misleading patients by omitting any safety or side effect information.” Since September 2025 the FDA has sent waves of warning letters to telehealth companies over their marketing of compounded GLP-1s, and this spring it asked Congress for more power to go after DTC ads that lack fair balance. The TV loophole itself is still open.

My preferred fix is to end direct-to-consumer advertising altogether. The AMA called for a ban in 2015. But the industry has lobbied heavily to keep it and has a lot of friends on both sides of the aisle. So here is the floor:

If an ad describes a drug’s results, speed, mechanism, or price, it is a drug ad. Naming Ro instead of the drug shouldn’t matter. It carries the same fair-balance risk disclosure, including the major risks said out loud.

Ads touching compounded drugs must say plainly that the FDA hasn’t approved them.

Risk information must be as audible and readable as the promise, not buried in fine print.

An ad should not be able to borrow the FDA’s approval and skip the FDA’s warnings. Tell viewers the risks out loud or take the ad off the air.

text:
The YAO Vending Machine - Part 3

The next tray came while the kitchen was still loud. Three demons this time, not one. They moved without speaking, their long arms reaching through the mesh to set down rice, a heavier pot of broth, and a shallow dish of pale, glistening strips that had been scored and lightly seared. The smell was the same one that had clung to Aiko’s jacket. Sanae did not look at the dish. Yui turned her face to the wall. Only Keiko watched the strips, her rocking stopped.

The tallest demon stayed after the others left. It crouched so its eyes were level with the cage and tapped one claw against the wire near Aiko’s knee. The sound was soft and patient. When she did not move, it reached in, took a strip between two fingers, and held it to her mouth the way a person might offer a child a piece of fruit. The meat was still warm. Aiko kept her lips closed. The demon’s thumb pressed under her chin, not hard enough to bruise, only enough to tilt her head back. The strip touched her lower lip and stayed there.

Sanae spoke without turning. “If you bite it, they mark you for the next cutting. If you don’t, they still mark you. The difference is only how long you stay soft.”

Aiko’s mouth opened on its own when the claw shifted. The meat slid in. It tasted of salt and a faint sweetness she recognized at once. She swallowed before she could spit, and the demon made a low, approving sound that vibrated through the mesh. It wiped its fingers on her sleeve, then turned to Keiko. Keiko did not resist. She opened her mouth and took what was offered, chewing with her eyes half-closed. When the demon left, the four of them sat with the rest of the food between them. No one spoke for a long time.

Later the lights in the dining room dimmed. The laughter on the other side of the wall thinned to a few low voices, then stopped. One of the smaller demons came down the corridor carrying a long, narrow tray covered with a cloth. It stopped outside the cage and looked at each of them in turn. Its gaze settled on Keiko. Keiko’s rocking started again, faster. The demon unlocked the door with a key that hung from a cord around its wrist. The door swung outward on quiet hinges.

Keiko did not stand. The demon reached in, took her by the upper arm, and drew her out. She went without sound. The door closed and the lock clicked. Through the service window Aiko watched the demon lead her past the cutting boards. One of the larger figures at the counters turned, knives still in its hands, and said something too low to hear. Keiko’s shoulders rose once, then fell. The cloth was lifted from the tray. What lay on it was already portioned. The demon that had brought her set the empty tray aside and guided her toward the far end of the kitchen, out of sight.

The knives that had been working on the counters stopped. For several breaths the only sound was the slow bubble of the stock pots. Then a single, heavier blade struck once. The sound carried cleanly down the corridor. After that the ordinary work resumed, faster than before, as if the interruption had only sharpened the rhythm.

Sanae exhaled. She reached for the remaining rice and began to eat it with her fingers. “They will bring her bones back for the broth before morning,” she said. “The customers like the depth it gives. You’ll smell it when they open the pots.”

Yui had not moved. Her hand rested on the place where Keiko had been sitting. The mesh there was still warm. Aiko stared at the empty space and then at the dish of scored strips that no one had finished. The sweetness was still on her tongue. Outside the cage the red light of the demons’ eyes moved across the steam in the same slow arcs, and somewhere beyond the wall a new pot began to simmer.

text:
Book 1: Righteous Among the Nations:

A Story of Those Who Were Not Jewish (the Nations, the Goyim) Who God Used to Bless Israel and thus were blessed.

Chapter 1: The Three Kings from Iran (Persia)

Three Kings from the East

In the twilight of the Babylonian empire, when the rivers still ran red with the memory of conquest and the Temple vessels sat mute in foreign treasuries, a king rose from the mountains of the east. Cyrus, called the Great, marched on Babylon and took it in a night.  He was a man being led by One True God: Yahweh to deliver the Jews back to their lands.  And for this act he would be blessed.

Babylon that had carried Israel into exile opened its gates. And then the unexpected happened.The Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus. From his palace he sent a proclamation throughout the realm: the God of heaven had given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build a house in Jerusalem. Any of the people of Judah who wished might go up.

Their neighbors were to help them with silver, gold, goods, and beasts. The sacred vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar were counted out and returned. Caravans formed. Families who had known only the canals and markets of Babylon turned their faces west.   God was bringing His people home and using the nations to do it - to show it was not by their own might, not by their power, but by the Spirit of the Lord.

Foundations were laid once more on the holy mountain. Isaiah had named this king long before he was born—“my shepherd,” “my anointed”—and the decree fulfilled the word spoken through Jeremiah.   It is a strange thing to think God owns all the Kings and has established His authority over all the kings of the earth - but that is the truth - God has always made Isarel to be a light to the nations - and built the nations to acknowledge the God of Israel.

Cyrus’s empire stretched from the Indus to the Aegean; his name endured as the liberator who let Israel, a people in captivity, to go home.

Years later the work stalled. Local governors wrote accusations. Letters traveled to the court. The builders stopped. Then Darius, another king of the east, ordered a search of the archives. In the fortress at Ecbatana the scroll was found: Cyrus’s original decree, with its measurements, its three courses of stone and one of timber, its promise that the cost would come from the royal treasury.

Darius did not merely confirm the old order. He enlarged it. He was being led by the Spirit of God to bless Isarel, another righteous tool for the Lord Jehovah.  The full expenses were to be paid from the tribute of the province beyond the River. Bulls, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine, and oil were to be supplied daily for the offerings. Anyone who hindered the work would be impaled on a beam from his own house.

And he added a solemn warning: may the God who has caused his name to dwell in Jerusalem overthrow any king or people who dares to alter this word.Under that decree the prophets Haggai and Zechariah stirred the people.

So, the Temple rose again. On the third day of Adar, in the sixth year of Darius, the house was finished. Priests and Levites dedicated it with joy. The Passover was kept. The God of Israel had turned the heart of the king of Persia toward his people, and the empire of Darius stood firm while the Second Temple took its place on the mountain.Decades passed.

Now God wasn't done.  A new generation lived under Persian rule, a third Persian king was going to be used by God. In the seventh year of Artaxerxes, Ezra the scribe stood before the throne. The king gave him a letter of extraordinary authority. All the silver and gold freely offered by the king and his counselors were to go for the house of the God of heaven. Whatever else was needed from the royal treasury was to be supplied. No tax or tribute was to be imposed on the priests, Levites, or servants of the Temple.

Ezra was empowered to appoint magistrates and judges who knew the law of the God of Israel, and to teach that law alongside the law of the king. The king even wrote that the wrath of the God of heaven should not come against the realm of the king and his sons.

With that commission Ezra led a company back to Jerusalem, the Law in his hand, resources in his wagons, and the favor of the court at his back.

Years afterward, in the twentieth year of the same king, Nehemiah the cupbearer stood before Artaxerxes with a sorrowful face. He asked leave to go and rebuild the walls of the city of his fathers’ graves. The king granted the request, gave letters to the governors of the province and to the keeper of the royal forest for timber, and sent an escort of officers and cavalry. In fifty-two days the walls rose. Gates were hung. The city that had been a reproach became a place of habitation again.

Artaxerxes’s decrees completed what Cyrus had begun and Darius had secured. Ezra 6:14 records that the elders of the Jews finished the building according to the command of the God of Israel and the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes.

Three kings from the east. None of them was of the seed of Abraham, yet each opened his hand and his treasury. Cyrus released the captives and returned the vessels. Darius silenced the adversaries and paid for the sacrifices. Artaxerxes equipped the teacher of the Law and the builder of the walls.

In return their names were written into the sacred story of Israel. Prophecy called Cyrus anointed. The Temple stood under Darius’s protection. The city and its Torah community were restored under Artaxerxes. Their empire enjoyed long years of relative peace and order while these works went forward.

History remembers them not merely as conquerors, but as the instruments through whom a scattered people returned, a house of prayer was raised again, and the city of the great King received its walls.

In the records of heaven and in the pages of Scripture, they stand among the righteous of the nations—Gentile kings who blessed the people of the covenant and were themselves remembered with favor

text:
🏈 DECEPTIVE FOOTBALL BOX SCORES — WEEKLY REPORT

October 13, 2026 | College Football & NFL
The final score doesn't always tell the whole story. Some teams dominated statistically but failed to cover the scoreboard margin their performance deserved. Others benefited from turnovers, short fields and unusually favorable scoring opportunities.

Here are the biggest statistical discrepancies from this week's football action and what they mean for future handicapping.

🏈 COLLEGE FOOTBALL — TOP 10 DECEPTIVE RESULTS

1️⃣ BYU 24, IOWA STATE 10

BYU outgained Iowa State 506–200, a staggering 306-yard advantage. The Cougars averaged approximately 8.3 yards per play compared with just 3.6 for Iowa State.

Failed fourth-down opportunities near the goal line and special-teams mistakes prevented a much larger victory.

📈 STRONG BYU UPGRADE. The most impressive hidden-dominance performance of the week.

2️⃣ OKLAHOMA 27, TEXAS 24

Texas outgained Oklahoma 382–238 but still lost. Two interceptions, including a pick-six, and a blocked-punt play were costly.

However, Texas managed only 41 second-half yards, an important warning against blindly upgrading the Longhorns.

📈 CONDITIONAL TEXAS BUY-LOW. The yardage advantage was substantial, but the offensive collapse cannot be ignored.

3️⃣ SOUTH CAROLINA 38, FLORIDA 19

One of the week's most misleading final scores.

South Carolina won by 19 points despite outgaining Florida by only SIX YARDS.

Florida committed three turnovers. South Carolina committed none.

📉 SOUTH CAROLINA SELL-HIGH. The final margin considerably exaggerates the statistical difference between these teams.

4️⃣ GEORGIA 20, ALABAMA 17

Georgia outgained Alabama 455–346 and dominated yards per play, 7.5–5.8.

The Bulldogs' offensive efficiency suggests a stronger performance than their three-point victory indicates.

📈 GEORGIA UPGRADE.

5️⃣ TENNESSEE 24, ARKANSAS 17

Tennessee outgained Arkansas by 126 yards and held a 1.8-yard advantage in yards per play.

Even more impressive, the Volunteers overcame a 3–1 turnover disadvantage.

📈 TENNESSEE UPGRADE. Strong underlying efficiency despite unfavorable turnover variance.

6️⃣ BOISE STATE 38, FRESNO STATE 31

Boise State accumulated 166 more offensive yards but Fresno State actually averaged more yards per play.

📈 CAUTIOUS BOISE STATE UPGRADE. Volume favored Boise, but efficiency tells a more complicated story.

7️⃣ UCLA 17, OREGON 15

Oregon committed an extraordinary SEVEN turnovers and still lost by only two points.

That raises serious questions about UCLA's ability to capitalize on favorable opportunities.

📉 UCLA FINISHING CONCERNS. Quarterback availability and performance require further evaluation.

8️⃣ OLE MISS 52, VANDERBILT 17

A 35-point blowout with only 66 yards separating the teams!

The scoreboard suggests overwhelming superiority. The offensive yardage tells a much different story.

📉 OLE MISS SELL-HIGH relative to the final margin.

9️⃣ NORTH CAROLINA 21, PITTSBURGH 17

Pittsburgh outgained North Carolina by 100 yards and recorded TEN more first downs, yet lost.

📈 CONDITIONAL PITTSBURGH BUY-LOW. The Panthers' underlying production was better than the result.

🔟 INDIANA 20, NEBRASKA 17

Nebraska gained 63 more total yards, but Indiana dominated per-play efficiency, 7.5–4.7.

⚖️ MIXED SIGNALS. Total yardage favors Nebraska; explosiveness favors Indiana.

🔥 COLLEGE FOOTBALL POWER-RATING WATCHLIST

STRONGEST UPGRADES: BYU, Georgia, Tennessee.

CONDITIONAL BUY-LOW: Texas, Pittsburgh.

SELL-HIGH WARNINGS: South Carolina, Ole Miss.

SPECIAL MONITORING: UCLA quarterback situation.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🏈 NFL — TOP 8 DECEPTIVE RESULTS

1️⃣ MINNESOTA 23, NEW ORLEANS 13

The Vikings outgained the Saints 364–142, an enormous 222-yard advantage.

Minnesota ran 25 additional offensive plays and controlled possession for nearly 40 minutes.

Red-zone mistakes and a New Orleans defensive touchdown helped keep the final margin to just 10.

📈 STRONG MINNESOTA UPGRADE. The NFL's clearest hidden-dominance performance this week.

2️⃣ JACKSONVILLE 19, PHILADELPHIA 17

Jacksonville outgained Philadelphia 408–232 and dominated yards per play, 6.0–3.9.

The Eagles managed only 22 rushing yards.

Despite that statistical superiority, Jacksonville needed a last-second field goal to escape with a two-point victory.

📈 STRONG JACKSONVILLE UPGRADE. The Jaguars' down-to-down superiority was considerably greater than the scoreboard suggests.

3️⃣ TAMPA BAY 24, DALLAS 16

Tampa Bay rushed for 241 yards while limiting Dallas to only 50 rushing yards.

The Buccaneers also controlled possession for more than 39 minutes.

Dallas was more productive through the air, so the adjustment is primarily about rushing efficiency and line-of-scrimmage performance.

📈 TAMPA BAY RUSHING UPGRADE. Significant matchup implications going forward.

4️⃣ CINCINNATI 31, MIAMI 24

Miami outgained Cincinnati 354–307 but lost by seven.

The Dolphins' offensive yardage exceeded the Bengals' despite the final result.

📈 CONDITIONAL MIAMI BUY-LOW. Examine finishing efficiency and turnovers before making a substantial adjustment.

5️⃣ BUFFALO 37, LA RAMS 34 (OT)

Buffalo averaged 7.6 yards per play compared with 5.8 for the Rams.

However, Los Angeles finished with more total offensive yards.

⚖️ MIXED SIGNALS. Buffalo was more efficient per play, while the Rams generated greater offensive volume.

6️⃣ NY GIANTS 27, WASHINGTON 27 (OT)

Washington averaged 6.3 yards per play compared with 4.9 for the Giants.

That is a substantial efficiency advantage in a game that finished tied.

📈 SLIGHT WASHINGTON UPGRADE.

7️⃣ SAN FRANCISCO 32, SEATTLE 29

The teams combined for 61 points despite generating only 520 offensive yards.

SEVEN turnovers, a defensive touchdown and short fields helped inflate the scoring.

This is especially important for TOTALS handicapping.

📉 SCORING INFLATION WARNING. Do not automatically interpret 61 points as evidence of two explosive offenses.

8️⃣ BALTIMORE 30, ATLANTA 23 (OT)

Atlanta finished with 24 more total yards, seven more first downs and 98 more rushing yards despite losing.

📈 SLIGHT ATLANTA UPGRADE. The Falcons' underlying production deserves more credit than the final score.

🔥 NFL POWER-RATING WATCHLIST

STRONGEST UPGRADES: Minnesota, Jacksonville.

MATCHUP-SPECIFIC UPGRADE: Tampa Bay rushing attack.

DOWNGRADE SIGNALS: Philadelphia offensive performance, New Orleans underlying efficiency.

CONDITIONAL BUY-LOW: Miami, Washington.

TOTALS WARNING: San Francisco–Seattle scoring inflation.

MIXED EFFICIENCY SIGNALS: Buffalo–LA Rams.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 THE HANDICAPPING TAKEAWAY

The betting market often reacts to wins, losses and final margins. Our job is to look beneath those numbers.

Total yards, yards per play, turnovers, first downs, possession time, scoring efficiency and non-offensive touchdowns can reveal performances that the final score conceals.

BYU and Minnesota stand out as this week's strongest examples of teams whose statistical dominance exceeded their winning margins.

South Carolina and Ole Miss offer the opposite lesson: impressive final scores that deserve closer scrutiny before upgrading either team.

These are power-rating and matchup adjustments, NOT automatic wagers. Opponent strength, injuries, future matchups and the betting line still determine whether an adjustment creates actual value.

Which team do you think the betting market is most likely to overrate or underrate next week?

text:
100% and I'll add an experience I had at a local bookstore (ramble incoming)

I live in Southwest Florida. A small indie bookstore opened pop about 5 minutes from where I live. I followed them on their socials, and saw post after post about how they wanted to work with local authors, Etc

I pop in there one day with copies of my trilogy. The owner is helping a customer so I spend time cruising the shelves. Pretty much nothing but Romance, romantic, Etc with female authors. Okay, that by itself doesn't mean anything that's exactly why I'm down here right? To spread it out a bit.

I introduced myself, and the woman recognizes me because I had already messaged her beforehand that I wanted to come down and she said absolutely.

I give her a copy of each book, explain what the series is about, and tell her one of my goals as an author was to create something that young men would enjoy reading. As I'm telling her that you can see visible discomfort in her face. I finished the patch, and she stumbles over her words, which are essentially a blow off.

But she takes the three books and says she's going to read them and get back to me. Never heard back from her to this day this was probably I want to say 6 months ago? Since then I have seen a never-ending stream of female Indie authors, all selling romance, popping up on their socials

To recap: a local Indie bookstore opens 5 minutes from my house. I, a working in the author who has sold almost 2,000 copies of his books in just over two years, show up present my work, offer to work with them in any way that best suits the store, get the ick face, and then never hear back

Now look, I didn't go home and stew about it. That's not my style. But the fact remains: one of the reasons you don't see men reading as much today is because of this sort of situation. This store made an active decision not to shelve books that appeal to boys and young men.

And let me preemptively strike down some counter arguments: my covers are incredible, my series has an average 4.7 review across all three books, and I'm an excellent salesman.
